items.title: Availability and Access to Cardiovascular Medicines in Mozambique: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are a leading cause of mortality worldwide, with more than 80% of deaths occurring in low- and middle-income countries. In Mozambique, non-communicable diseases account for approximately 28% of deaths, with CVDs contributing substantially to this burden. Despite the country’s hierarchical health system and the World Health Organization target of 80% availability of essential medicines, access to cardiovascular medicines remains poorly documented. This scoping review mapped the availability, prices, affordability, physical access, and health-system barriers affecting access to essential cardiovascular medicines in Mozambique. The review followed the PRISMA-ScR guidelines and the Arksey and O’Malley framework. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were systematically searched without publication-year restrictions. Eligible studies assessed the availability, stock-outs, prices, affordability, or health-system barriers related to cardiovascular medicines and diagnostics in Mozambique. Study selection and data extraction were independently performed by multiple reviewers. Consistent with the scoping review design, formal risk-of-bias assessment was not undertaken. Fifteen studies met the inclusion criteria. Essential cardiovascular medicines showed persistently low availability, with mean availability of approximately 21% across public hospital pharmacies, private retail outlets, and private hospitals, substantially below the WHO 80% target. Public facilities consistently provided only a limited range of older first-line medicines, while second- and third-line medicines, statins, digoxin, direct oral anticoagulants, and diagnostic reagents were frequently unavailable. When public stocks were depleted, patients relied on private-sector purchases, where generic medicines cost an average of 4.51 times international reference prices. Long-term secondary prevention could require 14.0–17.8 days of wages per month for low-income workers. These barriers were associated with low hypertension awareness, treatment, and control, substantial target-organ damage, high stroke case-fatality, and poor anticoagulation control. Access to cardiovascular medicines in Mozambique is severely constrained by low availability, frequent stock-outs, and unaffordable private-sector prices. Strengthening medicine selection, supply-chain management, financial protection, and decentralized protocol-based care is essential to improve equitable access to cardiovascular treatment.

items.title: From evidence to impact: reflections on the SPECTRUM Consortium’s work on the commercial determinants of health
items.abstract: The SPECTRUM Consortium (Shaping Public hEalth poliCies To Reduce ineqUalities and harM) was a UK Prevention Research Partnership-funded, multi-university, multi-agency consortium that worked between 2019 and 2025 to shape public health policy and practice on non-communicable disease prevention and the commercial determinants of health (CDOH), focusing on tobacco, alcohol and foods high in salt, sugar and fat. Guided by a Theory of Change and an associated Impact Framework, SPECTRUM organised its work around three interconnected impact pathways: Engagement and Knowledge Exchange, SPECTRUM Research, and Research Landscape. This article reflects on the Consortium’s experience of pursuing impact across these pathways, using the Impact Framework to structure both an account of activities and outputs and a critical assessment of what worked well, what fell short, and what this suggests for future research consortia. Effective strategies included embedding knowledge brokers within policy organisations, sustained co-production with public involvement panels and citizens’ juries, and the development of shared analytical tools and conceptual models that strengthened the emerging field of CDOH. Persistent challenges included the absence of systematic monitoring and evaluation of impact, uneven integration across work packages, and tension between the pace of policy windows and the time needed for rigorous research. Reflecting across all three pathways, the Consortium found that the Theory of Change worked well as a tool for aligning stakeholders at the outset but was underused as an instrument for ongoing evaluation once the programme was under way. The experience points to the value of treating impact frameworks as evolving hypotheses rather than fixed blueprints, and of investing deliberately in structural mechanisms, such as embedded knowledge brokers and dedicated evaluation capacity, rather than relying on individual researcher effort alone to sustain the relationships and systems through which policy-relevant, cross-disciplinary research on CDOH generates impact.

items.title: Palliative Care in Surgery: Updated Research Priorities from the Surgical Palliative Care Research Expert Consensus Conference.
items.abstract: Background Surgical palliative care (SPC) research has advanced since the 2017 research agenda, but persistent gaps in patient selection, intervention delivery, and outcome measurement limit implementation across evolving surgical care settings. Study design In November 2025, a national consensus conference convened 28 SPC experts and researchers. Through iterative discussion and consensus-building during the meeting and subsequent months, participants updated research priorities across the surgical continuum and health system context. Full methodology and participant attributes were described in Supplemental Materials https://links.lww.com/JACS/A821. Results The updated agenda identified 11 research gaps across 3 priority areas: patient selection; interventions, care processes, and competencies; and outcome measurement. Priorities were mapped at 2 levels: surgical episodes, encompassing patient-, family-, and provider-level factors, and health systems, encompassing organizational and structural factors affecting SPC delivery. The agenda prioritizes identifying which patients benefit from SPC and when; broadening SPC beyond traditional populations; defining primary SPC competencies and the role of specialty consultation; improving communication of surgical intent, trade-offs, and preference-sensitive decisions; integrating and sustaining SPC across heterogeneous systems and care transitions; transforming clinical cultures; and developing patient-centered, context-specific surgical and systems-level outcomes. Emerging electronic health record, natural language processing, and large language model approaches may support scalable patient identification, intervention delivery, and outcome measurement, while requiring attention to bias and task-dependent performance. Conclusions SPC research should move beyond narrow proof-of-concept settings toward pragmatic, scalable approaches that define who should receive SPC, what should be delivered, and how success should be measured across diverse surgical environments.

items.title: Night eating syndrome is associated with the nutritional status among college students in Universitas Gadjah Mada, Indonesia.
items.abstract: Objectives To describe the prevalence of night eating syndrome, nutritional status, and the relationship between the two among college students. Methods A cross-sectional study of 156 college students was conducted using quota sampling techniques. A validated questionnaire was used to collect data on night eating syndrome, and the study team provided direct measurements of nutritional status. Chi-square test analysis was to determine the link between night eating syndrome and the nutritional status, while the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test was performed to determine the presence of confounding variables. Results Of the participants, 20.5 % were overweight, while 34 % were diagnosed with night eating syndrome. Night eating syndrome was significantly linked to the nutritional status (p=0.010). Conclusions A significant statistical association was found between night eating syndrome and the nutritional status of college students. Those experiencing night eating syndrome were 2.77 times more likely to be overweight.

items.title: Advancing colorectal cancer management through clinical proteomics: from genotype to proteotype toward clinical translation.
items.abstract: Introduction Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the leading causes of cancer death worldwide, with outcomes depending on the stages at diagnosis. Genomic and transcriptomic classifications are largely inferential because the genotype-phenotype relationship is non-linear and is influenced by post-translational regulation, protein turnover, and the tumor microenvironment (TME). Proteomics measures this functional layer directly. Areas covered This review surveys proteomic technologies for CRC emphasizing mass spectrometry, affinity- and aptamer- based multiplex platforms, post-translational modification proteomics, spatial proteomics, AI-driven structural and predictive analysis, and multi-omics integration. Each platform is evaluated based on clinical questions, the supporting evidence and the barriers to implementation. Literature was drawn primarily from PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus (2020-2026), emphasizing advanced and translational applications. Expert opinion Alongside approved blood cfDNA and stool-RNA molecular tests, proteomics is a functional complementary technology that may improve biological interpretation, assay triage and treatment response prediction, although prospective clinical utility remains to be established. The decisive barriers are standardized biospecimens, validation evidence, clinical utility data and interoperable public data sharing.

items.title: Cobertura da triagem neonatal biológica no Brasil e fatores associados, 2014-2023: estudo de séries temporais
items.abstract: Biological newborn screening (BNS), known as the “heel prick test,” is a vital public health strategy for the early diagnosis of treatable congenital diseases. This ecological time-series study analyzed BNS coverage in Brazil between 2014 and 2023 based on data from DATASUS. Trends were assessed using Prais-Winsten regression, and the correlation between coverage and indicators such as adequate prenatal care, hospitalizations in children under 1 year of age, mortality, and HDI was verified. National coverage increased from 73.75% to 83.28% (APC = 1.06%). The South region had coverage above 90%, whereas the North had coverage below 70%. There was a strong correlation between coverage and adequate prenatal care (r = 0.93) and a moderate correlation with hospitalizations and neonatal mortality. HDI was not significantly associated. Despite the progress, regional inequalities persist. These findings highlight the need for targeted policies, better integration of health services, and equity-oriented strategies to achieve universal BNS coverage in Brazil.

items.title: Digital media engagement and its relationship with depression severity
items.abstract: Introduction Throughout the pandemic, social media became the new newspaper, and the widespread information created a vulnerable state for the user. The study's goal is to determine the presence of depression in the Czech Republic's local population as well as how the use of media correlates with depression in the Czech population. Methodology A web-based interviewing technique was employed. A longitudinal study method was employed, and the data were collected in 5 waves. In each wave, the population varied in number: 2,192 (2020), 2,164 (2021), 1,717 (2022), 1,707 (2023), and 2,072 (2025), and listwise 1,120 participants participated in all 5 waves. The trend analysis of depression using PHQ-5 and MUQ was calculated for the years (2020–2023 & 2025). Results Total PHQ mean scores rose progressively from 7.41 ( SD = 3.02) in 2020 to 8.60 ( SD = 3.58) in 2025. Correlation analyzes revealed distinct, wave-dependent patterns across media engagement dimensions. Component 2 (Interactive Content and Reader Comments) demonstrated the most consistent positive correlation with depressive symptoms across all waves ( r = 0.233 to 0.305, p < 0.01, moderating it r = 0.147, p < 0.01 in 2025). Component 3 (Emotional Impact and Media Stress) was positively correlated with depression during active crisis years ( r = 0.069 to 0.125, p < 0.01 from 2020 to 2023) but exhibited a negative correlation in 2025 ( r = −0.268, p < 0.01). Component 1 (Economic Reporting and Serious News) maintained weak or non-significant associations throughout the study period ( r = 0.011 to 0.055). Conclusion The results indicate that Emotional reactivity is significantly correlated with media-related depression, while interactive content has a variable multiplier effect, and analytical news has a low direct effect. Public health interventions should prioritize emotional regulation, media literacy, and affective platform design to curb population-level mental health declines.

items.title: A novel Artificial Intelligence enabled framework for automated audio visual speech in noise evaluation
items.abstract: Presbycusis, or age related hearing loss, affects over 430 million individuals worldwide. Despite the widespread use of hearing aids, users frequently report persistent difficulties in noisy, multi talker environments. A critical discrepancy exists between conventional audio only (AO) clinical assessments and the complex, multimodal nature of real world communication. This research addresses this gap through the development and validation of a novel AI powered audio visual speech in noise (AVSIN) evaluation framework designed to simulate ecologically valid communicative scenarios. To facilitate the development of this framework, essential resources were established in the form of two custom designed audiovisual corpora: a structured dataset of IEEE sentences and a naturalistic, free flowing conversational corpus. These datasets served as the foundational ground truth for both perceptual assessments and the training of machine learning models. Validation of the AVSIN framework was conducted through extensive intelligibility testing with normal hearing and hearing aid users. Results indicated a statistically significant improvement in speech recognition thresholds (SRT) in AV conditions compared to AO, with an absolute AV benefit of 7.1 dB (p < 0.001). To automate this evaluation, a novel deep learning (DL) based intelligibility metric was developed. This model demonstrated superior predictive accuracy, achieving a predicted intelligibility score of 58.0% that was identical to the human ground truth (58.0%). This performance significantly surpassed conventional metrics such as STOI, which underestimated intelligibility at 46.9%. Beyond intelligibility, the framework integrates an objective assessment of cognitive load (CL). A multimodal fusion approach was implemented, combining pupillometry with non invasive radio frequency sensing. This combination provided a robust indicator of CL, with the fusion model achieving a strong overall Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.84 between the physiological modalities. To further align the framework with patient needs, data driven social media analysis was employed to map population level sentiment. This spatio temporal analysis validated the clinical relevance of the framework by quantifying real world patient sentiment regarding service disruptions and hearing technology limitations. In conclusion, this thesis presents a unified, interdisciplinary platform that successfully bridges the gap between subjective clinical testing and real world utility. By integrating deep learning predictions, physiological sensing, and ecological datasets, the AVSIN framework establishes a robust standard for the next generation of user centred, multimodal hearing assessment.

items.title: From AI-Assisted Performance to Independent Thinking: A Framework for Developing Higher-Order Thinking with Generative AI in Higher Education
items.abstract: In an AI-supported task, a student may explain a weak comparison once it has been identified, yet fail to notice a similar problem without a reminder. A decision about further help therefore needs evidence about what the student did without being prompted. We examine such decisions in English-medium university argumentation and evidence evaluation. The framework brings together English-language work on scaffolding, learner-generated reasoning, metacognitive calibration, and cognitive offloading. We distinguish help that supplies a reason from help that initiates a check. Readiness to work without the first does not establish readiness to work without the second. Coding examples and boundary cases make evidence about these functions interpretable, while six conditional propositions connect reconstruction and regulation to adaptation and transfer. A proposed experiment gives every group comparable diagnostic practice but varies whether teachers use its results to adjust assistance. This comparison isolates the value of using the evidence from learning through the diagnostic task itself. We relate the account to four GenAI approaches and illustrate it with a hypothetical sociology lesson. Help may be retained or restored when a new task requires it. The framework and coding rules need validation, particularly beyond the language and disciplinary settings considered here.

items.title: Paradigma Belajar dan Pembelajaran: Tinjauan Teoritis dan Psikologis
items.abstract: This study examines learning and instructional paradigms from a theoretical and psychological perspective. The aim of the study is to understand how classical and modern learning theories can be integrated with students' psychological aspects, resulting in a more comprehensive learning paradigm. The research method used is a literature study by analyzing various academic literature related to learning theories (behaviorism, cognitivism, humanism, and constructivism). The results show that each theory has a significant contribution to educational practice, but also has limitations when applied partially. Behaviorism emphasizes behavioral reinforcement, cognitivism emphasizes internal mental processes, humanism emphasizes personal needs, while constructivism emphasizes the active involvement of students in constructing knowledge. In addition, psychological factors such as intelligence, attention, interest, talent, motivation, attitude, and readiness have been shown to significantly influence learning effectiveness. The integration of learning theories and psychological understanding allows for the creation of a learning paradigm that is more adaptive, humanistic, and relevant to the demands of the digital era. Thus, this study confirms that learning success is determined not only by theoretical foundations, but also by the psychological condition of students and the educator's strategy in creating a conducive learning atmosphere.

items.title: The Association Between Socioeconomic Status and Academic Achievement Mediated by Psychological Factors
items.abstract: This narrative literature review proposes an integrative dual-pathway model to explain how socioeconomic status (SES) shapes academic achievement through interacting psychological mechanisms. Drawing on allostatic load theory, central executive functioning, self-efficacy, and learned helplessness, the model identifies two interconnected routes: a cognitive depletion pathway, in which allostatic load overburdens the prefrontal cortex and constrains limited working memory resources; and a motivational pathway in which low self-efficacy and repeated failures develop into learned helplessness that undermines motivation for learning. Crucially, these pathways do not operate independently but dynamically reinforce each other. Cognitive depletion undermines motivational beliefs, while diminished motivation reduces cognitive engagement, forming a self-reinforcing downward cycle. This integrated framework offers a more ecologically valid understanding of educational inequality than single-factor explanations. Practical implications suggest that educators should implement integrated interventions that simultaneously reduce extraneous cognitive load (e.g., scaffolded instructional sequences) and foster self-efficacy (e.g., process-oriented feedback) to break this bidirectional cycle. As the proposed model remains theoretical, future empirical research using longitudinal and experimental designs is required to validate its causal pathways and inform evidence-based educational policies.

items.title: From AI labels to trust: cognitive pathways linking authenticity judgments, risk perception, and trust in AI-generated videos
items.abstract: Background The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) has raised concerns regarding the authenticity and trustworthiness of synthetic media. Although AI disclosure labels are increasingly used as transparency mechanisms, the cognitive processes through which these cues influence trust formation remain unclear. Objective This study aimed to develop and test a cognitive pathway model explaining how AI disclosure labels, authenticity judgments, perceived risk, cognitive processing styles, and literacy factors shape trust toward AI-generated videos. Methods A 2 × 2 between-subjects experiment was conducted with 617 participants randomly assigned to four conditions involving AI-generated instructional videos with different AI label and video quality combinations. Participants evaluated authenticity, systematic and heuristic processing, trust, perceived risk, adoption intention, sharing intention, AI literacy, and media literacy. Regression, bootstrapped mediation, and moderation analyses were performed. Results AI disclosure labels significantly reduced perceived authenticity but did not directly affect trust, adoption, sharing intention, or perceived risk. Trust formation occurred through cognitive pathways: systematic processing increased trust, whereas heuristic processing reduced trust. Authenticity enhanced trust and lowered perceived risk, with perceived risk mediating the authenticity–trust relationship. Trust positively predicted adoption and sharing intentions, while AI and media literacy moderated selected relationships. Conclusion Trust in AI-generated videos was not directly determined by transparency labels alone. Instead, the observed associations among authenticity judgments, perceived risk, information processing, and trust were consistent with a multi-stage cognitive interpretation, although the cross-sectional post-exposure measurement of these constructs does not establish their temporal or causal sequence.

items.title: Social support processes link gratitude and well-being across cultures and over time
items.abstract: Abstract Strong evidence shows that gratitude enhances well-being, though the mechanisms driving these effects are unclear. Here, we test the idea that gratitude may enhance well-being by (1) attuning people to the support that they receive and boosting perceptions of social support and (2) promoting support provision. Using data from over 148,000 participants across two studies, we explore the mechanistic roles of perceived social support and support provision in linking gratitude to well-being. With both cross-sectional and longitudinal data, we find that social support processes—especially perceived social support—partially mediate the link between gratitude and well-being. Moreover, we find evidence of weaker associations between gratitude and social support provision in more collectivistic countries. This suggests that gratitude’s consequences for social support processes—and their implications for well-being—may depend upon local cultural norms about community and social support.

items.title: The rise of super-emotional intelligence
items.abstract: The debate about the future of artificial intelligence (AI) runs along a single axis: cognitive capability and its projected culmination in superintelligence. We argue that this framing leaves a complementary axis unexamined and propose the goal of Super-Emotional Intelligence (SEI): systems that perceive, model, regulate, and respond to affect better than skilled human experts, while remaining human-centered. SEI is a performance construct realized by a functional architecture, not a claim about machine experience, and we give measurable criteria for each of its four capacities. Today's affect-aware AI, from multimodal emotion recognition to empathic chatbots, recognizes, or simulates emotion at or below human level and is judged against human ceilings. Three things would set SEI apart: perception that adds peripheral and contactless physiological channels, none of them emotion-specific, but some, like the vestigial ear muscles, resolving affective processing at the timescale of the events that evoke it; a generative model of affect grounded in active inference rather than pattern matching; and functional allostatic self-regulation. The decisive gap in current systems is architectural. A sensed state conditions a prompt, but nothing carries a state estimate across turns, models the effect of the system's own responses, or selects actions under an explicit objective. We specify such a closed loop, state the conditions under which it is stable and steerable rather than manipulative, propose a preregistered validation plan whose failure would falsify our claims, and treat governance as a design constraint of the loop rather than an afterthought.

items.title: The Mechanisms Through Which Social Media Marketing Influences Purchase Intentions among Generation Z Consumers
items.abstract: As the Z-generation (born between 1997 and 2012) is gradually reaching adulthood, this group has become the main driving force in the current and future global consumer market. Understanding how social media marketing influences their purchasing decisions is a key market direction that the industry is focusing on. This article systematically examines the mechanism by which social media marketing affects the purchasing intentions of the Z-generation, with a particular focus on the roles and pathways of key opinion leaders (KOLs), key opinion consumers (KOCs), and live-streaming sales. The study reveals that social interaction and trust building are the core psychological mechanisms driving purchasing intentions - the professionalism and social appeal of the merchants' agents stimulate the audience's emotional attachment and imitative behavior, which in turn positively influence the brand purchase intention. The high-traffic content produced by these agents aligns with the values of the Z-generation, providing the emotional compensation that this group finds difficult to obtain in school and at home, thereby inducing impulsive consumption. At the same time, the trust relationship driven by social interaction is inherently fragile. Account scandals or trust breakdowns can quickly erode the accumulated consumer credit and company marketing assets. Based on this, this article proposes references from three aspects: content design, long-term trust relationship building, and values-driven marketing, to construct a research report on the consumption tendencies of the Z-generation.

items.title: Editorial: Psychological dynamics in knowledge management: cognitive, emotional, and social influences
items.abstract: Liu, Yang, and Gao (2026) extend this cognitive lens from the individual mind to the information environment. Their study of online emergencies shows how anchoring, representativeness, and availability heuristics shape cognitive bias through adaptive expectations and implicit attributions, with meaningful differences across demographic groups. In digital knowledge environments, therefore, the problem is not only whether information reaches people, but how context frames what appears credible, memorable, and actionable. KM must concern itself with the quality of sensemaking, not merely the quantity of information circulated.From cognition, the collection moves naturally to the emotional and relational conditions of knowledge sharing. Zhang and Xu (2024) show that psychological capital is connected to knowledge sharing through emotional intelligence and psychological safety among e-commerce practitioners. Their findings position hope, optimism, resilience, self-efficacy, emotional regulation, and interpersonal safety not as peripheral "soft" variables, but as resources that help determine whether knowledge is exchanged. Bai (2025) adds a leadership perspective, demonstrating that transformational leadership supports employee career growth partly through knowledge sharing, while self-efficacy and psychological capital shape the strength of these relationships. Together, these studies make a clear point: people share what they know when they feel capable, supported, and safe enough to do so.The next contributions ask what happens when knowledge must be mobilized under pressure. Wu, Lai, and Li (2025) show that pilots' personal knowledge management capability is positively associated with career resilience, with safety behavior acting as a partial bridge between knowledge capability and resilient functioning. Their nonlinear findings for safety climate and work pressure are equally important: supportive conditions can strengthen adaptation, but "more" is not always "better." Knowledge becomes valuable when it is translated into disciplined action within an appropriate psychological and operational climate.At the team level, Yang and Suntrayuth (2025) make this translation especially visible. Drawing on knowledge creation and dynamic capability perspectives, they show that team knowledge dynamics contribute to resilience through communicative, leadership, interpretive, and analytical capacities. Knowledge creation alone is insufficient; teams must discuss, interpret, judge, and enact what they know. Resilience, in this sense, is an emergent achievement of collective cognition and coordinated action.Wang, Zhang, and Zhao (2025) then carry the argument to the organizational level. Their study of technology-oriented small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) identifies a learningresilience pathway through which strategic human resource management supports innovation. Organizational learning builds knowledge; resilience enables adaptation; together they help convert human resource practices into innovation. Yet the inverted U-shaped role of environmental dynamism reminds us that psychological and knowledge capabilities are always contingent. When turbulence becomes excessive, established routines and capabilities may no longer be enough.Across these seven papers, three themes converge. First, psychological dynamics are not antecedents sitting outside KM; they are part of the mechanism through which knowledge is acquired, interpreted, shared, and applied. Second, KM is best understood as a multilevel process: cognitive control and personal resources scale into interpersonal exchange, team sensemaking, resilience, learning, and innovation. Third, context matters. Task demands, leadership, psychological safety, safety climate, digital information fields, human resources (HR) systems, and environmental dynamism can enable knowledge to become action-or distort and constrain that translation.The agenda opened by this Research Topic is therefore both practical and intellectually demanding. Future work should connect levels of analysis more deliberately, combine selfreport evidence with longitudinal, behavioral, neurocognitive, and digital-trace methods, and examine whether psychological mechanisms travel across occupations, cultures, and technologies. This is especially important as artificial intelligence (AI) becomes embedded in knowledge work: the central question will not only be what AI can capture or generate, but how human attention, emotion, trust, agency, and social interaction shape what people accept, share, challenge, and ultimately use.The enduring message of this collection is simple: knowledge does not manage itself. Between information and intelligent action stands the human mind in a social world. Understanding that space is essential if KM is to become more adaptive, resilient, and genuinely useful.

items.title: Epistemic trust, mentalizing and extremist attitudes in a German community sample
items.abstract: Introduction While extremist attitudes, here conspiracy mentality, antisemitic attitudes, and the ideological support of violence, are typically studied in political or sociological psychological contexts, their investigation in relation to clinical psychological concepts may offer additional insight with respect to underlying psychological mechanisms. In this study, we aimed to explore the relation between self-reported extremist attitudes and epistemic trust, mistrust, and credulity, as well as mentalizing. The different epistemic stances as well as difficulties in the ability to mentalize are assumed to represent non-pathological individual variations in psychological vulnerability and resilience. Methods This questionnaire study investigates the relationship between levels of epistemic trust, mistrust, and credulity, assessed via the Epistemic Trust, Mistrust and Credulity Questionnaire, mentalizing deficits assessed via the Mentalization Questionnaire and endorsement of extremist attitudes (antisemitic attitudes assessed via 2 items of the model questionnaire on right-wing extremism by the German Federal Agency for Civic Education, conspiracy mentality assessed via the Conspiracy Mentality Questionnaire, and violence supporting attitudes assessed via the Violent Extremist Attitudes Scale) in a German community sample (N = 566). Due to scarcity in empirical research on these concepts, we took an exploratory approach to investigate potential associations using structural equation modeling. Self-indicated presence of a mental disorder and participants` gender were integrated into the model. Results Epistemic mistrust and all extremist attitudes were positively related via mentalizing deficits; as was the marginally significant negative association between epistemic trust and conspiracy mentality. No other indirect effects of epistemic trust or credulity on extremist attitudes reached significance. Presence of a mental disorder was associated with epistemic credulity, epistemic mistrust, and mentalizing deficits, but not with extremist attitudes. Female gender was associated with higher epistemic trust and lower antisemitic attitudes as well as lower endorsement of violence supporting attitudes. Conclusion Exploratory findings should inspire future longitudinal or experimental research on the investigated constructs to identify whether they might be promising candidates to reduce extremist attitudes in the general population. Moreover, gender-specific mechanisms seem of relevance and need to be further explored.

items.title: The Influence of Cultural Differences on the Neural Mechanisms of Risky Decision-Making
items.abstract: Risky decision-making is an important cognitive process involved in financial, health-related, social and everyday decisions. Previous research suggests that individuals from different cultural backgrounds may differ in risk preference, information processing, and the evaluation of probability and potential outcomes. However, cultural differences cannot be understood solely through behavioral outcomes because similar choices may result from different cognitive and neural processes. This paper reviews research on the relationship between culture, risky decision-making, and the neural systems involved in risk processing. Existing evidence suggests that culture may influence risky decision-making by shaping information processing, self-construal, and the subjective evaluation of probability, reward and loss. These influences may further affect how common neural systems involved in value evaluation, reward processing, uncertainty and cognitive control process information. However, culture should not be viewed as a deterministic factor because substantial individual differences exist within cultural groups. Overall, cultural experience appears to function as an important modulator of the cognitive and neural processes underlying risky decision-making.

items.title: СОЦІАЛЬНО-КОГНІТИВНІ НАСЛІДКИ РІЗНИХ ТИПІВ ЦИФРОВОЇ АКТИВНОСТІ: РИЗИКИ ТА РЕСУРСИ САМОРЕГУЛЯЦІЇ
items.abstract: Вступ. У статті розглянуто проблему впливу цифрових технологій на соціально-когнітивний розвиток особистості в умовах тотальної цифровізації. Актуальність зумовлена стрімким зростанням часу взаємодії з цифровими пристроями, раннім початком їх використання та суперечливими даними щодо наслідків цього впливу. Мета роботи − проаналізувати особливості впливу цифрових технологій на соціально-когнітивний розвиток особистості (переважно дітей, підлітків та молоді) з урахуванням типу цифрової активності, вікового періоду залучення та ролі рефлексивних стратегій саморегуляції. Наукова новизна полягає в авторському теоретичному узагальненні диференційованого характеру впливу цифрових технологій. Виокремлено три взаємопов’язані групи чинників: 1) тип цифрової активності (активна, цілеспрямована взаємодія сприяє розвитку окремих когнітивних функцій, тоді як пасивне споживання фрагментарного контенту пов’язане зі зниженням когнітивних показників); 2) віковий період залучення до цифрового середовища; 3) наявність рефлексивних стратегій саморегуляції, які виконують компенсаторну функцію. Запропонована рамка має характер теоретичного узагальнення. Висновки. Аналіз літератури свідчить про амбівалентний вплив цифрових технологій: активне цілеспрямоване використання може сприяти розвитку окремих когнітивних функцій, тоді як пасивне споживання фрагментарного контенту пов’язане зі зниженням показників довільної уваги, робочої пам’яті та здатності до глибинного читання. Одним із можливих механізмів є нейропластичність та особливості дофамінової системи винагороди, однак більшість даних мають кореляційний характер. Рефлексивні стратегії саморегуляції можуть компенсувати негативні ефекти, хоча їх ефективність потребує подальшого вивчення. Найбільш перспективним напрямом вважаємо лонгітюдні дослідження довгострокових наслідків різних типів цифрової активності.

items.title: Development and preliminary psychometric evaluation of a modified Chinese instrument for self-rated mastery of diabetes exercise knowledge (DEKS-C)
items.abstract: Background Exercise knowledge is seldom evaluated as a standalone construct in China, and no validated instrument exists for self-perceived mastery of exercise knowledge among patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Adapting the Turkish Diabetes Exercise Knowledge Scale (DEKS) required item consolidation, supplementary items and a revised response format, yielding a modified, DEKS-derived instrument rather than a direct translation. Methods This sequential exploratory mixed-methods study was conducted at a tertiary hospital in Hangzhou, China (February–July 2025). In total, 438 patients with T2DM completed the 17-item DEKS-C following forward-backward translation, content validation and three rounds of cognitive interviewing ( n = 23). Internal consistency and the exploratory factor structure were evaluated using Cronbach’s α and principal axis factoring with oblimin rotation; factor retention followed Horn’s parallel analysis, with the three-factor solution re-examined on a polychoric matrix. Results Content validation consolidated nine overlapping items into three and added three new items. Cognitive interviewing then consolidated or relocated four items and merged one into the foot-care item, producing 17 items scored 1–4 (total range 17–68). Cronbach’s α was 0.967 (corrected item-total correlations 0.668–0.837), the Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin measure 0.965, and Bartlett’s test χ 2 (136) = 6945.15, p < 0.001. Floor and ceiling effects were 13.47 and 8.90%, arising entirely from the 59 all-lowest-response and 39 all-highest-response respondents, the former answering faster (median 89 vs. 232 s, p < 0.001). Horn’s parallel analysis identified three substantially intercorrelated factors (|r| = 0.51–0.79) explaining 55.73–71.23% of total variance (71.23% in the full sample), corresponding to exercise benefits cognition, exercise implementation and exercise safety; an equivalent structure emerged on a polychoric matrix. One pattern coefficient nevertheless exceeded unity and inter-factor correlations were elevated, leaving the solution provisional. Conclusion The DEKS-C showed high internal consistency and a three-factor grouping that was broadly stable across sensitivity samples and alternative correlation matrices, supporting content relevance. However, because the factors were substantially intercorrelated and the structure remains unverified, the proposed multidimensional model cannot be regarded as firmly established; independent multicenter and multiregional confirmatory factor analysis is required.

items.title: Association between an ITHBC theory-based nursing pathway and discharge readiness among mothers of preterm infants: a non-randomized controlled study with a historical control group
items.abstract: Objective To evaluate the effects of an Integrated Theory of Health Behavior Change (ITHBC)-based nursing pathway on discharge readiness in mothers of preterm infants. Methods In this non-randomized controlled study with a historical (temporal) control group, 115 mothers were divided into an observation group (ITHBC-based care, n = 57) and a control group (routine care, n = 58). Discharge readiness, discharge instruction quality, care ability, self-efficacy, resilience, anxiety, and depression were assessed at discharge; infant growth, complications, readmission, and maternal satisfaction were followed up at 6 months. Multivariable linear regression was used to adjust for baseline covariates for key outcomes. Results The observation group showed significantly higher discharge readiness, discharge instruction quality, care ability, self-efficacy, and resilience, with lower anxiety and depression (all P < 0.05). At 6 months, their infants had better growth metrics, fewer complications (thrush, diaper rash), and lower readmission rates, alongside higher maternal satisfaction ( P < 0.05). These differences remained significant after covariate adjustment. Conclusions The ITHBC-based nursing pathway was associated with better maternal psychological status and care competence, more favorable infant health outcomes, lower readmission rates, and higher satisfaction, providing a practical framework for transitional care in preterm infants.

items.title: The Effect of the Nudge Theory on the Consumption Decision of Older Adults
items.abstract: As the phenomenon of fraudulent marketing takes place among the older population more and more frequently, behavioral research is increasingly focusing on how the older population can avoid deception. By reviewing previous relevant studies, this paper summarizes the causes of older adults' vulnerability in decision-making, which is caused by both internal factors such as physiological aging and psychological aging, as well as external societal factors, and further explains the mechanism of fraudulent marketing using the Nudge Theory. While the Nudge Theory is usually used to benefit the decision-makers, the non-benevolent usage of the Nudge Theory by merchants is called "Sludge", which uses various patterns to complicate the process of consumption decision-making, leading to irrational and false judgment. Most importantly, this paper concludes with practical means for the older population and product designers in order to minimize the harm brought by fraudulent marketing and sludge. Future research should expand more on the strategies of how to avoid sludge, protecting the financial rights of older adults.

items.title: Different paths, same destination: similar benthic nitrogen cycling sustained by distinct biogeochemical mechanisms in artificialized coastal systems
items.abstract: Abstract. Human activities are increasingly affecting coastal ecosystems, with shoreline stabilization structures becoming a prevalent response to sea-level rise and extreme climatic events. While these structures aim to protect coastal communities and infrastructures, their effects on ecosystem functioning, and particularly nitrogen cycling and fixed-nitrogen loss processes such as denitrification, remain poorly understood. To assess the ecological impacts of breakwater construction, we employed a space-for-time substitution approach to examine changes in sediment biogeochemistry, macrobenthic community structure, and nitrogen cycling in an intertidal salt marsh in the St. Lawrence Estuary, Canada. We measured benthic fluxes, denitrification rates, and macrofaunal assemblages at five locations: two landward of the breakwater (impacted sites), one situated immediately seaward of the breakwater (intermediate site) and two reference sites (one vegetated and one unvegetated). Landward sites exhibited finer sediment with higher organic carbon content and supported distinct macrobenthic communities dominated by opportunistic Oligochaetes while reference sites were dominated by Molluscs and Crustaceans. The intermediate seaward site closely resembled the unvegetated reference site in both sediment characteristics and oxygen dynamics. Surprisingly, despite these substantial physical and biological changes, dark total benthic oxygen uptake, NO3−, NH4+ benthic fluxes and benthic denitrification rates showed no significant differences between impacted and reference sites. This functional similarity suggests a degree of ecosystem plasticity, where different combinations of abiotic and biotic factors can maintain similar ecosystem function. However, such functional plasticity might not apply to all ecosystem services offered by natural salt marshes, emphasizing the importance of careful consideration in coastal management decisions.

items.title: Mechanisms of Pesticide Stress Responses and Green Mitigation Approaches in Astragalus membranaceus
items.abstract: Pesticide application is essential for managing pests in medicinal plants, yet it inevitably introduces risks of pesticide residue accumulation, plant growth inhibition, and changes in the biosynthesis of bioactive compounds. Understanding the responses of medicinal plants to pesticide stress and developing effective approaches for reducing pesticide toxicity are important for the safe production of medicinal materials. Using Astragalus membranaceus as a model medicinal plant, this dissertation systematically investigates the uptake, translocation, metabolism, and phytotoxicity of three representative pesticides, including tebuconazole (TEB), atrazine (ATZ), and avermectin (AVM). In addition, two approaches for alleviating pesticide stress and reducing residues, namely endogenous hormone regulation and rhizosphere microbial remediation, were further evaluated. All pesticides exhibited distinct patterns of uptake and distribution in A. membranaceus. ATZ was readily transported to the shoots, whereas TEB mainly accumulated in the roots and AVM showed very limited transport within the plant. These differences were closely associated with the physicochemical properties of the pesticides. All of them inhibited plant growth and caused membrane damage, but induced different physiological responses. TEB mainly affected phenylpropanoid metabolism and increased the expression of several genes associated with lignin biosynthesis, AVM induced changes in detoxification enzyme activities and peroxidase activity, whereas ATZ mainly affected flavonoid metabolism and energy related pathways. In addition, pesticide exposure altered the accumulation of triterpenoid saponins, and different biosynthetic branches responded differently to the three pesticides. Although the physiological responses varied among pesticides, all three treatments disturbed cytokinin homeostasis and inhibited root growth. Increased IPT expression, decreased CKX expression, and changes in cytokinin profiles were observed across the treatments, suggesting an association between altered cytokinin metabolism and root growth inhibition. TEB was selected as a representative pesticide for subsequent intervention experiments. Exogenous methyl jasmonate (MeJA) partially restored plant growth, altered responses associated with Phase I and Phase II detoxification, and partially restored the accumulation of some bioactive compounds under TEB stress. Root TEB residues decreased by 6.23%. In contrast, DIECA treatment was associated with greater TEB accumulation, and reduced accumulation of some saponins, providing pharmacological evidence for the involvement of jasmonates in the response to TEB stress. Meanwhile, TEB changed the composition of root exudates and affected both endophytic and rhizosphere microbial communities. A bacterium capable of degrading TEB, Sphingobium yanoikuyae IPPH-98, was isolated from the rhizosphere of A. membranaceus. This strain showed chemotactic responses to selected compounds detected in root exudates and degraded TEB in culture. Inoculation with IPPH-98 reduced TEB residues in soil and plant roots, promoted plant growth, and increased root Soyasaponin I accumulation. This study improves the current understanding of the physiological and molecular responses of medicinal plants to pesticide stress and provides a theoretical basis for pesticide residue control, quality maintenance, and the green production of medicinal plants.

items.title: Exploring the effective management of potato upstream food loss and waste policy in Scotland - circular economy approach
items.abstract: Food Loss and Waste [FLW] is a contributor to food insecurity and environmentally unsustainable practices. Extensive studies have explored food loss and waste in the downstream sector (e.g. homes, restaurants, and others), with less attention paid to upstream loss and waste. Emerging evidence suggests that upstream potato waste is increasingly contributing to environmental degradation, thereby undermining the attainment of the circular economy (CE) and contributing to the growth of greenhouse gases (GHG). This study aims to explore the perspectives of stakeholders (potato Farmers, Waste Recyclers and Policy Makers) within the Scottish upstream potato food chain to identify the drivers of food loss and waste and drivers of CE. Employing a unique cross-sectional, qualitative research design grounded in interpretivist principles, this study delves into the perspectives of stakeholders within the Scottish upstream potato food chain. Qualitative instruments, including in-depth interviews (IDIs), were used to collect data through both face-to-face (one-on-one) and phone interviews, conducted at the participants' convenience. The purposive sampling gathered Twenty-One (n = 21) participants, categorised as Farmers (n = 17), Waste Recyclers (n = 2), and Policy Makers (n = 2). Data saturation and triangulation improved data quality. The interview audio was manually translated into a research manuscript using the Edinburgh Napier Microsoft transcribing tool. Data analyses were conducted manually, following the stages outlined by V. Braun & Clarke (2006), for reflexive thematic analysis. No incentive was provided to participants. Four (4) primary themes emerged from the study: (i) Drivers of choice of potato cultivation and processing, (ii) Drivers of potato waste and loss, (iii) Policy and market contributions to CE, and (iv) Practices promoting circular economy (CE). The findings from this study suggest that family history, market acceptance and available support motivated Farmers to cultivate and process potatoes. Farmers showed adherence to best farming practices. However, climatic factors, pest invasion, the cost of machinery, workforce, and storage drove potato loss, while Waste Recyclers faced inconsistent policies and financial barriers in managing wastes generated on farms. Similarly, stakeholders demonstrated effective loss and waste management practices. However, overdependence on cosmetic grading, high cost of storage and uncontrollable variables such as weather contributed to losses and waste. The study revealed the presence of policy failure. Inconsistent, ineffective, or poorly implemented policies contributed to the stakeholders' inability to mitigate the impact of loss and waste drivers and their inability to attain CE in the sector. The Scottish upstream potato sector significantly contributes to the inability to attain CE in the Scottish agricultural food chain. Despite the efforts of stakeholders to achieve CE, the policy failed to address gaps which could have harnessed the efforts of stakeholders. It is clear from this research that it is necessary to have an integrated systems approach regarding the upstream potato loss in food in Scotland. The results achieved in terms of a refined conceptual framework show that sustainability in the potato chain is only possible if it is done in collaboration between policymakers, potato producers, and waste recyclers. This is a crucial step in addressing the issue and moving towards a more sustainable future.

items.title: Investigating drivers of seagrass loss in Kenya and testing local solutions to seagrass conservation
items.abstract: Seagrass ecosystems are vital marine habitats, supporting biodiversity, carbon sequestration, and the livelihoods of millions of people worldwide. Despite their ecological and economic importance, seagrass meadows are in global decline due to natural and anthropogenic pressures. This study investigates the drivers of seagrass loss, focusing on Kenya, where seagrass cover is decreasing at an estimated rate of 1.6% annually. A systematic review revealed that 27% of African countries with coastlines lack data on seagrass, while only 29% have complete coverage. Anthropogenic activities, particularly fishing, accounted for 66.7% of identified threats to seagrass. Within Kenya, population growth was significantly associated with seagrass loss, with declines concentrated in high-density areas, though no evidence supports eutrophication as a major factor. Field experiments demonstrated that seine netting significantly reduced seagrass cover by 8.3% in a single use, whereas basket traps had no observable impact. This study also evaluated three seagrass monitoring methods: video analysis, quadrat sampling, and point counts, highlighting their trade-offs in accuracy, cost, and community applicability. Video analysis showed high precision but required technical expertise and resources, while quadrat sampling was reliable but labour-intensive. Point counts were the least resource-intensive but tended to overestimate seagrass cover. The findings suggest integrating technical training with simplified tools to enhance community-based conservation efforts. This thesis underscores the urgent need for better seagrass extent estimates in Africa, improved understanding of drivers of decline, and effective conservation strategies. It provides actionable recommendations to strengthen local and regional seagrass management, emphasizing the importance of community engagement and international policy alignment to ensure sustainable management of these critical ecosystems.

items.title: Applying and evaluating visual surveys, passive acoustic monitoring, and eDNA metabarcoding for biodiversity assessment of European flat oyster beds
items.abstract: European flat oysters (Ostrea edulis) are ecosystem engineers that create biodiverse biogenic habitats. Following significant declines caused by overfishing, pollution and environmental degradation, these habitats are considered collapsed, prompting restoration efforts and a demand for effective monitoring tools to assess restoration success and measure biodiversity gains at scale. Traditional underwater visual surveys are widely used but often labour intensive. Novel, potentially more scalable techniques for assessing biodiversity are available, but their robustness and efficiency need to be tested in the habitat of concern. In this study, biodiversity associated with European flat oyster beds, along oyster shell cover gradients, was assessed at the Scottish and Swedish west coasts. Underwater visual census (UVC), supplemented by baited remote underwater video (BRUV), were conducted and, for the first time for this species, compared with concurrent passive acoustic monitoring (PAM) and environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding. Baseline visual surveys revealed a significant positive relationship between species diversity and oyster shell cover. Similarly, acoustic indices and phonic richness correlated positively with oyster shell cover, albeit with lower sensitivity than UVC. eDNA metabarcoding with universal markers (18S and COI) showed positive correlations with shell cover for only a few taxonomic groups, particularly under low tidal flow. While eDNA results did not always align with UVC, they revealed differences in community composition across shell-cover gradients at fine spatial scales. Indicator species for high oyster shell cover were identified, including the black goby (Gobius niger) (UVC, BRUV and PAM) and certain algae (UVC, PAM and eDNA). This study demonstrates how different biodiversity assessment methods can be applied as robust, efficient and complementary tools to monitor the trajectory and success of European flat oyster restoration. By identifying the strengths and limitations of each approach, the findings provide valuable guidance for researchers, practitioners and environmental managers involved in European flat oyster restoration and beyond.

items.title: Originality in scientific practice. Is it clear enough or should we continue discussing it?
items.abstract: The guidelines for publishing articles, awarding grants, or obtaining a doctorate at an academic institution all stipulate originality. But how is it measured in practice? Research aimed at testing a creative solution (i.e., a novel idea) to an interesting, unsolved problem is undeniably original. But is the presence of a novel hypothesis a standard requirement or condition for evaluating the originality of a scientific proposal? It seems that such a condition would set the bar too high. While we value both plausible and original hypotheses in scientific proposals, the assessment of originality in day-to-day academic practice should hinge on whether the proposal addresses a research problem or question that remains unresolved. We highlight the balanced contributions of observation (e.g., natural history) and theory in inspiring and justifying scientific problems of significant interest. Identifying well-founded problems constitutes —or should constitute— the best way to evaluate originality in scientific practice.

items.title: Living with Wilt: Disease, Control, and Plantation Ecologies in Chinese Banana Farming in Cambodia
items.abstract: Drawing on fieldwork conducted in August 2026 at four Chinese-invested banana enterprises in Cambodia and interviews with a biotechnology supplier, this article examines how plant disease is understood, managed, and experienced within plantation production. Managers, technical specialists, and Cambodian workers offered overlapping explanations centred on fungi, bacteria, mixed infections, continuous cultivation, and insects. These accounts reflected differences in occupational responsibilities, training, and exposure to economic risk. Yet causal explanations did not translate straightforwardly into control practices: actors with similar diagnoses adopted different interventions, while those with different explanations converged on the same cultivar or microbial products. Access to capital, professional experience, commercial interests, and perceived limitations in public plant-health support mediated these choices. Cultivar replacement emerged as the principal response, alongside soil amendments, biological products, and chemical treatments. Interview accounts also linked disease and its management to concerns about soil condition, unstable earnings, labour mobility, and changing relations between plantations and villages. The article develops the concept of a “control race” to describe efforts to sustain production through successive cultivar changes and spatial relocation while underlying vulnerabilities remain unresolved. Rather than establishing pathogen identity or treatment efficacy, the study shows how disease management redistributes uncertainty and risk across a plantation social–ecological system.

items.title: Estudio socioecológico de Sembrando Vida en los agroecosistemas del centro de Veracruz
items.abstract: The objective was to conduct a comparative analysis of the Sowing Life program along an altitudinal gradient in the central region of the state of Veracruz, using a socioecological approach. The research was carried out from January 2023 to November 2025; the sample comprised 90 structured questionnaires and 30 semi-structured interviews administered to active legal subjects in three municipalities (Puente Nacional, Chocamán, and Atlahuilco). The research method was a survey with a comparative and diachronic multiple case study design. Data collection combined quantitative and qualitative techniques. Qualitative information was analyzed using the socioecological systems framework (SES Framework), and quantitative data were analyzed using nonparametric descriptive and inferential statistics (Kruskal-Wallis test). The results indicate that the program consolidated a circular and agroecological management model based on technological sovereignty, which articulates three dimensions (natural, social, and economic) through six operational axes. The impact of the model is heterogeneous according to the altitudinal gradient: the middle zone achieved the highest socioecological performance (89.3%) due to coffee social capital; the upper zone, 85.7%; and the lower zone, 75%, due to risks of economic dependence. The role of the woman planter emerges as the key driving force of the system, whose leadership transforms government subsidies into resilience and community autonomy. It is concluded that the Sowing Life program consolidated a circular, agroecological management model based on technological sovereignty and the self-management of bioinputs. The impact is heterogeneous according to the altitudinal gradient, with the middle zone standing out for its social capital and low risk of economic dependence.

items.title: Emergent socioecological dynamics in Eastern Polynesian chiefdoms: a comparative network analysis of the Society and Gambier Islands
items.abstract: Methods from complexity science can help us better understand the development of socioecological systems. Here we investigate how human relationships with diverse species were structured through ecological and cultural networks in the Society Islands and the Gambier Islands, two archipelagoes of Central Eastern Polynesia. Each archipelago was settled by voyaging societies derived from similar ancestry concomitantly experiencing European contact, thus having remarkably short c. 800–900-year pre-contact cultural sequences. These short cultural sequences allow us to examine how similar cultures colonized contrastive, yet pristine island ecosystems with similar imported taxa and cultural principles yet ended up with social systems of differing socio-political complexity some 800–900 years later. To investigate these dynamics, we apply the “Human Interactions with Other Species” (HIOS) network analysis to archaeological, ethnographic, and historical evidence of human engagement with local and introduced taxa. Rather than framing sociopolitical change as the product of either environmental constraints or cultural agency alone, our analysis emphasizes the development of social and ecological systems together through time. The results demonstrate that differences in biodiversity structure, resource availability, and interspecies interactions influenced subsistence practices, material production, and social organization, while also highlighting the importance of local social dynamics in mediating ecological constraints. A secondary finding is methodological: correspondence analysis, a tool long used in anthropology, produces patterns broadly consistent with those identified through network analysis, while network analysis additionally reveals structural relationships that correspondence analysis cannot capture. More broadly, this study illustrates how comparative socioecological network analysis can contribute to understanding historical dynamics in island societies and demonstrates the value of complex systems approaches for examining cultural diversification in Polynesia.

items.title: Rethinking collaborative governance in Papua: toward institutional transformation
items.abstract: After more than two decades of implementing the Special Autonomy policy, Papua continues to lag behind other regions in Indonesia in terms of development. The complex legal, political, and human rights context, combined with the region's diverse social, economic, cultural, environmental, and natural resource characteristics, poses significant challenges to the implementation of current approaches. This paper is grounded in the proposition that the key challenge lies in developing a shared vision capable of accommodating diverse actors, sectors, and social aspirations within a coherent and legitimate social welfare framework. Using a qualitative approach and drawing on the concepts of collaborative governance, joined-up government, and proper governance, this study examines governance challenges in Papua. The analysis suggests that Papua's governance challenge requires institutional transformation beyond administrative coordination. The proposed joined-up cross-provincial agency model provides a mechanism to strengthen intergovernmental coordination, promote inclusive participation, incorporate local knowledge, and reduce elite dominance. The proposed model differs in several important respects from existing models of intergovernmental collaboration implemented in Papua. First and foremost, it places horizontal collaboration at the center of governance through the establishment of a Joined-Up Cross-Provincial Government Agency. Unlike predominantly top-down arrangements driven by central government directives, the proposed model adopts a bottom-up approach that is more responsive to local contexts and cross-provincial priorities. In doing so, it provides a foundation for more collaborative, context-sensitive, and mission-oriented governance during the second phase of Papua's Special Autonomy (2021–2041).

items.title: Intraspecific diversity of fan-tailed brook lamprey (Lethenteron satoi) with its ecological and distributional notes
items.abstract: Abstract Lethenteron satoi is a species of brook lamprey recently described from a single river in the Ishikari River system, Hokkaido, Japan. To date, the species had been known only from the six specimens used in the original description, and its basic biological information remained extremely limited. Herein, we examined genetic and morphological variation in L. satoi based on 38 individuals collected from four rivers. Mitochondrial DNA analyses revealed that genetic diversity is highest in the lowland areas of the Ishikari River system and that populations are genetically differentiated from one another. Morphological analyses showed that a population from the upper reaches exhibits partially distinct characters and allow us to update the known ranges of metric traits for the species. We also provide new information on the distribution, ecology, and sexual dimorphisms of L. satoi . These findings provide a foundation for future conservation of this recently described species.

items.title: G reen C onstruction M anagement in O ffshore W ind P ower P rojects
items.abstract: The transformation to clean energy in the world promotes the development of offshore wind power in deep and Far Seas. The construction is greatly affected by complex sea conditions, with short effective operation time and a long ecological chain impact path. Most of the existing management methods are based on land-based construction, and no effective circular control measures have been developed for the unique marine pollution factors, which can not meet the needs of emerging industries. This paper summarizes the literature review and typical engineering project examples, summarizes the theoretical research progress and governance experience of green construction of offshore wind power, and compares the policy transmission mode and technology docking mode in different jurisdictions. The academic community has reached a conclusion that the land green construction standard can not be well applied to the marine field. Practice has shown that centralized approval and marine spatial planning are feasible, but the transnational spread of floating wind power is still controversial, mainly due to the contradiction between the requirements for stability and construction flexibility. The current research lacks a localization evaluation method combining micro and macro perspectives and the internalization path of ecological cost.

items.title: Exploring Economic Valuation, Green Accounting, and Fiscal Policy Optimization of Locally Generated Revenue in Jayapura City
items.abstract: This study examined an economic valuation model for mangrove ecosystems within a green accounting framework, serving as a regional fiscal policy instrument, and its implications for optimizing Locally-Generated Revenue (PAD) in Jayapura City. Mangrove ecosystems possess direct, indirect, and sustainable economic values that have not yet been systematically internalized into public accounting systems and regional fiscal planning. The research employed a qualitative approach utilizing natural resource economic valuation (Total Economic Value/TEV), regional fiscal policy analysis, and a study on integrating environmental accounting into public financial management. Data were collected through interviews with relevant Regional Government Agencies including the Regional Development Planning Agency, Environmental Agency, Marine and Fisheries Agency, Regional Financial and Asset Management Agency, Inspectorate, Tourism Agency, MSME Agency, and Regional-Owned Enterprises involving 45 respondents comprising agency heads, secretaries, finance staff, division heads, and Technical Implementation Units. The findings disclosed that implementing green accounting based on mangrove economic valuation can strengthen the legitimacy of sustainable fiscal policies, improve budget allocation efficiency, and unlock opportunities for regional revenue generation. Ecosystem service-based programs, such as ecotourism, Payments for Environmental Services (PES), and blue carbon schemes, serve not only as instruments for ecological conservation but also as strategies for sustainable regional economic development. Implementing this integrated model in Jayapura City has the potential to enhance regional fiscal resilience, strengthen environmental governance, and create a systemic, long-term balance between economic growth and the sustainability of coastal ecosystems.

items.title: From territorio to Pacha: The epistemology of land system science in Latin America
items.abstract: Abstract. Land system science (LSS) has emerged as a central discipline at the intersection of global environmental change and sustainability research, yet its core vocabulary, publication networks, and conceptual frameworks remain largely anchored in the English language and associated Western scientific traditions. This creates particular challenges in Latin America, where decades of academic, governmental, and Indigenous and local knowledge on land-related processes have developed through distinct terminological and epistemological traditions that do not map directly onto LSS concepts. We conducted a multilingual survey of 156 land systems actors across Latin America, spanning academic, governmental, non-governmental, and community-based organizations, to characterize how the field is understood, translated, and operationalized across the region. We found that engagement with land systems topics exceeds identification with the LSS term itself, suggesting that the Latin American land systems community is larger than those identifying with LSS. Conceptual frameworks used in the region are pluralistic, with social-ecological systems, territorial studies, landscape ecology, and political ecology all sharing questions that LSS addresses under a single label. A majority of respondents supported developing a shared Spanish and Portuguese equivalent for LSS, with a clear preference for terms rooted in territorio over biophysical alternatives, reflecting deeper ontological commitments to land as a socially constructed and politically inhabited space. Drawing on these preferences, we propose Ciencias de sistemas territoriales (Spanish) and Ciências de sistemas territoriais (Portuguese) as working translations of land systems science for the Latin American context. Inclusion of Indigenous and local knowledge into research remains shallow and epistemologically stratified, concentrated among researchers with critical or transdisciplinary orientations rather than fixed within the whole field. Taken together, these findings call for deeper engagement among the broader community of LSS actors in terminological dialogue and knowledge co-production that would allow Latin American, Indigenous, and relational traditions to shape the foundations of land system science globally.

items.title: Beyond Complexity: Evaluating Simple vs. Complex Deep Learning Architectures for Urban Density Mapping
items.abstract: The spatial distribution of population density and land use is a fundamental metric for targeting spatial planning policies under the Sustainable Development Goals. This study presents a comparative evaluation of deep learning architectures for urban density estimation, with an emphasis on spatial generalization. The study was conducted in Jakarta and its surrounding cities (Jabodetabek), a highly heterogeneous region that provides a rigorous setting for evaluating model generalization. Sentinel-2 satellite imagery and European Space Agency WorldCover 2020 data were acquired through Google Earth Engine, together with the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index and the Normalized Difference Built-up Index to explicitly represent vegetation and built-up characteristics. Quantitative evaluation showed that all deep learning models performed well, with R² exceeding 0.94 in all experiments. The U-Net architecture achieved the highest predictive accuracy, with the lowest mean squared error (MSE = 0.0006954). Notably, the lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) proved to be a highly competitive alternative (MSE = 0.0006998), requiring approximately four times fewer parameters and delivering roughly twice the inference speed of the deeper U-Net and ResNet models. In contrast, complex models such as EfficientNet and ResNet showed diminishing returns in accuracy relative to their design complexity, while classical machine learning baselines (Random Forest and XGBoost) failed to capture spatial configurations robustly. These findings demonstrate that increasing network depth does not necessarily improve performance in spatial fractional regression. Therefore, model selection should balance predictive accuracy against computational and environmental costs. items.title: Decolonized and resistant ecologies: An examination of John Still’s The Jungle Tide
items.abstract: This article focuses on John Still’s ([1930] 1955) novel, The Jungle Tide that describes the impact of the European colonial enterprise on the ecologies of South Asia, specifically on their post-independence predicaments. It examines how even a loyal imperialist like Still was deeply disturbed by the ways in which colonialism initiated the ruinous intersection of racial-capitalism and plantation-monoculture, resulting in the large-scale movement of people for labour, and extensive deforestation programmes that led to the destruction of rainforests, species depletion, and biodiversity loss. The novel provides insights into the ways in which the Sri Lankan forests were destroyed to make way for plantation monoculture while also challenging the prevailing colonial assumptions that legitimized this conversion. This article explores Still’s interrogation of the ideologies of colonial, postcolonial, and neocolonial governance, structural racism, global capitalism, and environmental degradation and how these interconnected forces become imbricated in Sri Lankan and South Asian histories.

items.title: Species composition and assemblages of ichthyoplankton during winter and summer around the Korean Peninsula
items.abstract: Background Understanding the spatial distribution of ichthyoplankton is fundamental for identifying spawning habitats, evaluating recruitment processes, and monitoring changes in marine fish populations. However, previous studies in Korean waters have largely focused on individual coastal regions, limiting nationwide comparisons of assemblage structure. Methods We conducted standardized surveys in February and July 2017 across the Yellow Sea, Korea Strait, East Sea, and Jeju waters. Ichthyoplankton was sampled at 133 stations, with valid samples from 130 stations in February and 133 in July. Species were identified morphologically, with DNA barcoding used for selected specimens requiring confirmation. Results We identified 30 egg taxa and 61 larval taxa in February, and 53 egg taxa and 154 larval taxa in July. Species richness increased markedly in July, and larval assemblages consistently contained more taxa than egg assemblages. Ammodytes japonicus dominated larval abundance in February, whereas Engraulis japonicus dominated both egg and larval abundance in July. Regional differentiation was more apparent in July. Surface temperature and salinity also differed among the four regions. Discussion Differences between February and July were consistent with species-specific spawning periods. Regional differentiation previously reported for fish assemblages in Korean waters was also evident in ichthyoplankton. Because the surveys covered only February and July of a single year, the results do not represent the full seasonal variability of ichthyoplankton assemblages.
