items.title: Biochar for post-war land remediation in Ukraine: A critical review supported by bibliometric analysis.
items.abstract: This critical review analyzes the current state of scientific research on biochar in Europe and examines its potential use for post-war restoration and improvement of soil fertility in Ukraine. A bibliometric analysis of scientific publications in the Scopus and Web of Science databases for the period 2014-2023 was conducted using VOSviewer visualization and data processing methods. The analysis identified the main areas of research and gaps in knowledge that are relevant to the future application of this technology in Ukraine. Moreover, remote sensing methodologies were employed to identify potential remediation requirements in the Ukrainian territory. This involved the analysis of changes in the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) and the normalized difference moisture index (NDMI) of a part of Ukraine's agricultural territory situated along the frontline, prior to and following a period of three years during a full-scale war. The results revealed changes in vegetation and moisture levels, indicating land degradation in the border area under study. However, these observations do not constitute direct evidence of soil contamination or the effectiveness of biochar; rather, they indicate areas where further field studies and an assessment of restoration measures are needed. A strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats (SWOT) analysis was used as a strategic discussion tool to identify the opportunities and challenges associated with the implementation of biochar in Ukraine. This review also identifies the main scientific uncertainties, barriers, economic aspects, and research priorities that should be considered before the large-scale implementation of biochar-based technologies in Ukraine.

items.title: Contrasting CH<sub>4</sub> flux responses to distinct drought regimes and nitrogen enrichment in a temperate steppe.
items.abstract: Drought and nitrogen (N) deposition alter greenhouse gas fluxes, but how distinct drought scenarios interact with N enrichment to regulate the methane (CH 4 ) sink remains poorly understood. We conducted a 4-yr field experiment in a temperate steppe to examine CH 4 fluxes under three drought regimes - early-season intense drought (ID), mid-season chronic drought (CD), and mid-season reduced rainfall frequency (RF) - and N addition. CH 4 uptake and its driving mechanisms were assessed through field measurements and structural equation modeling, focusing on the interplay between soil physicochemical properties, microbial abundance, and plant-mediated emissions. All drought treatments reduced the CH 4 sink with divergent temporal dynamics; reduced RF caused the most persistent reduction, while N addition alleviated the inhibitory effects of CD. These shifts were driven by distinct mechanisms: ID acted via lowering previous-year belowground net primary productivity and increasing dissolved organic N, CD functioned through increased Artemisia frigida cover and reduced arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal abundance, and RF suppressed uptake via the morphological expansion of A. frigida. We conclude that CH 4 sink stability is highly sensitive to drought regime, and that the morphological expansion of specific plants such as A. frigida may partially offset the soil CH 4 sink.

items.title: Evolutionary shifts to gynomonoecy correlate with changes in capitulum architecture in South African Helichrysum (Asteraceae).
items.abstract: Gynomonoecy has evolved repeatedly in Asteraceae, suggesting selective advantages for species whose capitula combine pistillate and bisexual flowers. Theories invoking conspicuous peripheral flowers and achene heteromorphism do not account for gynomonoecy in the southern African-centred genus Helichrysum, which lacks both these features. We investigated whether gynomonoecy is associated with changes in capitulum architecture in South African Helichrysum, focusing on flower packing density and achene size. We compared flower packing density and achene size between hermaphroditic and gynomonoecious Helichrysum species using phylogenetic generalised least squares and reconstructed ancestral sexual systems using a well-sampled, time-calibrated phylogeny. Gynomonoecious species produced nearly twice as many flowers per unit receptacle area as hermaphroditic species and had subtly but significantly smaller achenes. Ancestral-state reconstruction strongly supported hermaphroditism as ancestral, with gynomonoecy originating independently 18 times. Our results provide the first phylogenetically informed evidence within a single Asteraceae genus that shifts to gynomonoecy correlate with shifts in capitulum architecture. The association between gynomonoecy, denser flower packing, and reduced achene size is consistent with the hypothesis that accentuated resource gradients within capitula and priority access to resources by first-maturing peripheral flowers may have favoured the evolution of gynomonoecy.

items.title: Operational comparability of ecological status assessment in Iberian transboundary rivers.
items.abstract: The European Union Water Framework Directive (WFD) requires member states to assess the ecological status of surface waters using biological quality elements (BQEs). Although the WFD includes intercalibration procedures to harmonise class boundaries, differences between national assessment systems may affect the comparability of ecological status classifications, particularly in transboundary rivers. This study evaluated the consistency of Portuguese and Spanish ecological status assessments in 32 water bodies across Iberian transboundary rivers in the Minho, Lima, Douro, Tagus and Guadiana basins, using data collected between 2019 and 2021. Comparisons included fish, macrophytes, benthic macroinvertebrates and diatoms. Biological assemblages, ecological quality ratios (EQRs) and ecological quality classifications were analysed. Results differed markedly among BQEs. Fish showed no significant differences in assemblage composition or EQR values between countries and a moderate positive correlation in ecological quality classifications. Macroinvertebrates displayed weak compositional separation, no differences in EQR values and a weak, nonsignificant positive correlation between countries. Macrophytes showed significant compositional differences despite similar EQR distributions and a weak, nonsignificant positive correlation in ecological quality classifications. Diatoms showed the strongest divergence, with clear assemblage separation, higher EQR values in Spain and a very weak, nonsignificant negative correlation between countries. Final ecological classifications also showed a weak, nonsignificant positive correlation between countries. These findings show that formal intercalibration alone does not guarantee operational comparability in shared river systems. Cross-border assessment consistency depends strongly on the BQEs considered and on methodological differences between national monitoring systems, highlighting the need for improved harmonisation of monitoring procedures and taxonomic practices.

items.title: Scaling of dimensions and concentrations of plastics in two Dutch rivers.
items.abstract: Plastic pollution raised great environmental concerns due to its persistence and widespread presence. To model ecological impacts, such as ingestion by wildlife, information on the abundance and dimensions of plastic particles is fundamental. Our study examined the relationships between size dimensions (length, area, circumference) of individual particles and the length of particles, their concentration, and cumulative surface area. Plastic particles were collected with trawl nets from upstream and downstream sites in two Dutch rivers in 2023 and 2024. Particle dimensions, including length (defined as the longest axis), surface area, circumference, and the number of particles, were measured. Geometric means of particle concentrations and cumulative surface area concentrations were calculated for equal-sized bins based on length and plotted against particle length on a log-log scale. Reduced major axis and ordinary linear least squares regressions determined the power relationships between size dimensions of individual particles. For length-based bins, we evaluated how concentrations and total surface area co-varied with length classes. Size dimensions were strongly and positively related, indicating differences in shape across size classes. Contrary to previous research, the length of plastic particles was not strongly correlated to their concentration in the Meuse River and varied between sampling locations. The cumulative surface area concentration increased significantly with length. The findings of the study should be viewed with caution, as they were based on two Dutch rivers. Even greater caution is warranted for the relationships between particle length and concentration, and between particle length and cumulative surface area, as they were based solely on measurements in the Meuse.

items.title: The kinetic basis of photosynthetic heat tolerance.
items.abstract: Photosynthetic heat tolerance constrains primary productivity and defines the upper temperature limit of the biosphere. However, current approaches to heat tolerance either overlook the duration of heat exposure or describe temperature-time relationships without characterizing causal mechanisms, constraining hypothesis testing and prediction under novel conditions. Heat inactivation of photosynthesis has been posited to result from protein denaturation or lipid membrane breakdown, but their relative contributions are not well resolved. Here we develop and test a quantitative theory of photosynthetic heat inactivation based on chemical kinetics and use the theory to evaluate these competing mechanisms. By analysing photosystem II temperature responses in 177 plant species from 157 families, we show that protein denaturation, not lipid membrane breakdown, governs heat tolerance. The theory also predicts an upper acclimatization limit of ~60 °C, set by the thermal stability of heat shock proteins and supported by global data for 826 species. Our findings provide a predictive, mechanistic basis for photosynthetic heat tolerance and the thermal limits of the biosphere in a changing climate.

items.title: Plant reproductive palaeobiology: a window into long-term reproductive dynamics.
items.abstract: Reproductive dynamics strongly influence genetic diversity and population structure, with important implications for ecological interactions and evolutionary trajectories. However, our understanding of plant reproductive dynamics remains limited due to the scarcity of long-term studies. Here, we propose a conceptual and methodological framework for tracking plant reproductive dynamics over long timescales using pollen, plant spore, and seed records preserved in sedimentary archives. The analysis of counts, morphology, and DNA from fossil propagules enables reconstruction of reproductive patterns over centennial to million-year timescales. When integrated with other palaeoproxies, these records provide insights into environmental drivers and eco-evolutionary consequences of reproductive dynamics. The proposed framework opens new avenues for optimising conservation strategies, safeguarding key ecological functions, and improving predictions of future biotic responses.

items.title: Behavior and Toxicity of Buckminsterfullerene (C<sub>60</sub>) in Aquatic Environments: A 30-Year Review.
items.abstract: Buckminsterfullerene (C 60 ) is widely applied in various fields due to its unique physicochemical properties and has been increasingly detected in aquatic environments. This review examines the current knowledge of C 60 behavior and toxicity in aquatic environments over the past 30 years. Once released into aquatic systems, C 60 undergoes complex processes, including dispersion, aggregation, sedimentation, transformation, and interactions with co-pollutants. These processes influence its mobility, bioavailability, and toxicity, affecting organisms from algae to benthos. Mechanisms for these toxicities involve solvent-related effects, reactive oxygen species generation, physical contact, and carrier effects with co-pollutants. Furthermore, current evidence suggests that the ecological risks of C 60 are likely underestimated, particularly in sediment-associated, food-web, and multi-pollutant exposure scenarios. This review also identifies critical knowledge gaps, including the fate of sediment-associated C 60 , the limited diversity of test organisms, the lack of environmental realism in exposure conditions, and challenges in maintaining C 60 purity during preparation.

items.title: Acyloxyneryl esters in Doronicum austriacum subsp. giganteum essential oil: structure elucidation, synthesis, and GC-MS/RI library development.
items.abstract: The essential oil of the underground parts of Doronicum austriacum subsp. giganteum (Griseb.) Stoj. & Stef. (Asteraceae) was studied here for the first time. Based GC-FID peak-area normalization, neryl isobutyrate (44.2%) and neryl 2-methylbutyrate (28.8%) were the two most abundant identified constituents. Targeted chromatographic fractionation guided by GC-MS revealed a series of oxygenated acyclic monoterpene diesters that proved difficult to identify by conventional means. By combining the synthesis of authentic reference compounds with high-field NMR spectroscopy (HSQC, HMBC, NOESY) and diagnostic 13 C- 1 H coupling constants, nine previously undescribed natural products were identified, including 8- and 9-acyloxyneryl isobutyrates and the corresponding 2-methylbutyrate analogues. Systematic relationships between structure and linear retention indices on nonpolar and polar stationary phases provided transferable criteria for distinguishing C-8 vs C-9 oxygenation and neryl (Z) vs geranyl (E) geometry, and enabled estimation of chromatographic behavior for related, not-yet observed congeners. A re-evaluation of reported NMR patterns further suggests that a subset of literature "acyloxyneryl/geranyl" assignments may correspond to C-10-acylated isomers. Collectively, these findings expand the phytochemical space of acylated monoterpenes in Asteraceae roots and provide a validated spectral and retention-index reference framework for future studies of closely related metabolites.

items.title: Expanding photosynthesis through biosolar oxic N<sub>2</sub> fixation: toward a sustainable BioNitrogen Economy.
items.abstract: Atmospheric dinitrogen (N 2 ) is far more abundant than carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), yet photosynthesis has been studied and harnessed predominantly for photosynthetic carbon fixation (PCF), underpinning the global biocarbon economy. In contrast, biological N 2 fixation-the natural gateway for atmospheric nitrogen into the biosphere-remains comparatively underexploited. Modern agriculture and industry consequently depend heavily on the fossil-fuel-intensive Haber-Bosch process, with substantial energy and environmental costs. Diazotrophic cyanobacteria offer a fundamentally different paradigm by coupling oxygenic photosynthesis to nitrogenase-mediated N 2 fixation. We term this process photosynthetic nitrogen fixation (PNF), which uses solar energy to convert water and atmospheric N 2 into bioavailable nitrogen. Beyond its ecological significance, PNF expands the functional scope of photosynthesis beyond carbon fixation and provides a biological foundation for sustainable nitrogen production, biofertilization, and N 2 -based biosolar manufacturing. Recent advances in cyanobacterial physiology, ecology, evolution, synthetic biology, and AI-enabled multi-omics are accelerating efforts to harness this potential. This review examines the diversity of diazotrophic cyanobacteria, their strategies for protecting oxygen-sensitive nitrogenase, and emerging approaches for genetic engineering cyanobacteria as programmable platforms for nitrogen production and crop-associated nitrogen delivery. We further propose a roadmap toward a solar-powered BioNitrogen Economy encompassing bioprospecting, synthetic biology, genomic engineering, crop integration, and scalable agricultural and industrial deployment. By expanding photosynthesis from carbon fixation to the solar-powered capture of both carbon and atmospheric nitrogen, PNF could help drive the transition from a fossil-fuel-dependent chemo-nitrogen economy toward a sustainable BioNitrogen Civilization.

items.title: Combining essential oils and kaolin clay increased repellency against Bemisia tabaci (Hemiptera: Aleyrodidae): implications for management.
items.abstract: The sweetpotato whitefly, Bemisia tabaci (Gennadius) (Hemiptera: Aleyrodidae), is a major pest of vegetable crops worldwide. Management of this pest relies on insecticides, but overuse has led to resistance development and negative effects on non-target organisms. Repellent essential oils can be a sustainable alternative to insecticides. The residual efficacy of essential oils is relatively short, but combining them with kaolin clay provides enhanced repellency against whiteflies and a slower release rate. While many essential oils have been evaluated against whiteflies, most studies utilize different protocols, making comparisons between compounds challenging. In this study, 12 essential oils were screened against B. tabaci using a Y-tube olfactometer. Limonene, E-cinnamaldehyde, citral, cumin oil, and geraniol had a significant repellent effect on whiteflies, while the other oils did not. A dual-choice bioassay evaluated the significantly repellent oils, with and without kaolin clay, on whitefly-infested squash plants. Plants treated with E-cinnamaldehyde displayed phytotoxicity symptoms at the concentration tested. Among the remaining 4 compounds, citral applied alone repelled more whiteflies than limonene, geraniol, and an untreated control. Combining each oil with kaolin clay significantly improved their repellency compared to just the oil or kaolin alone. Combining limonene and kaolin was as effective as combining citral and kaolin despite citral being the most repellent compound on its own. This study demonstrates that kaolin clay has an additive effect for each oil tested, which may be used in an integrated pest management (IPM) program to extend the repellency duration against whiteflies in squash.

items.title: Functional roles of abyssal benthos in sustaining polymetallic nodule fields.
items.abstract: Polymetallic nodules form a critical habitat in the abyssal plain ecosystems where they occur, supporting high benthic biodiversity. 1 They form over millions of years in areas of extremely low sediment accumulation rates, 2 , 3 but it is unclear how the nodules remain on the surface, and hence are available for benthic biota. Here, we use seabed time-lapse photography to explore the potential role of benthic faunal behavior in the maintenance of polymetallic nodules on the seabed surface. We observed several species directly removing sediment from the nodule surface, mainly holothurians and gastropods, and infauna activity causing nodule uplift. Derived estimates of the area covered by animal movements, as a proxy for benthic activity, 4 , 5 indicated that yearly to decadal timescales are needed to remove sediment from and uplift all nodules within the field of view. If these behaviors significantly counteract nodule burial over the long term, then benthic activity may be a key mechanism in nodule maintenance, 6 , 7 as hypothesized for over 40 years. 8 This essential function for the maintenance of abyssal biodiversity in nodule-field seascapes has been largely overlooked, highlighting that substantial gaps in knowledge remain in our understanding of the functioning of nodule-field ecosystems. Improving the assessment of habitat engineers may enhance predictions of ecosystem resilience if commercial mining activities occur. However, this study opens new opportunities for monitoring benthic ecosystem functioning to provide a more holistic understanding of abyssal ecosystem status and dynamics.

items.title: Aging dynamics and subsequent dissolved organic matter evolution of microplastics regulated by UV-salinity conditions.
items.abstract: The aging of marine microplastics (MPs) and their release of plastic-derived dissolved organic matter (MP-DOM) have raised growing concern, yet comparative assessments of conventional polyolefins versus biodegradable polyesters under synergistic UV-salinity stress remain limited. Here, we systematically compared the surface alteration and DOM release of polyethylene (PE), polypropylene (PP), and polylactic acid (PLA) across a salinity gradient (0, 15, and 30 PSU; Practical Salinity Unit) under UV-exposed and dark conditions over 60 days. UV irradiation markedly accelerated aging in all three MP types, as evidenced by progressive enrichment of oxygen-containing functional groups. For PE and PP, increased salinity further intensified photo-oxidative degradation, and released DOM exhibited optical shifts from protein-like toward humic-like fluorescence signatures characterized by elevated SUVA 254 and HIX values. In contrast, PLA degradation was consistent with ester bond hydrolysis, producing 2-6 times greater DOM yields than PE and PP, with released DOM dominated by protein-like fluorescence components. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) indicated that UV exposure exerted stronger effects than salinity on the surface oxidation of PE and PP (β = 0.39-0.41 vs. 0.20-0.31), while salinity showed no significant effect on PLA aging. These findings reveal contrasting pathways by which conventional and biodegradable MPs contribute to marine dissolved organic carbon pools, providing a basis for assessing their differential environmental behaviors under variable salinity regimes.

items.title: A validated Nile Red fluorescence method following KOH/H₂O₂ digestion for microplastic detection in marine molluscs.
items.abstract: Microplastic (MP) in marine ecosystems poses an increasing risk to the environment and human health. However standardized rapid methods for monitoring large numbers of samples are still lacking. This study validates a semi-automated Nile Red dye (NRD) fluorescence method combined with a two-step KOH/H₂O₂ digestion protocol for MP detection in marine molluscs. Twelve reference materials, including six synthetic polymer types (PE [two size fractions], PP, PA-66, PET, PMMA) and six natural materials (cotton, hemp, cellulose, wool, viscose, olive stone powder), were evaluated before and after digestion. Treatment resulted in 83.2 (± 4.8%) digestion of the natural reference, and reduced fluorescence intensity by 83.9 (± 14.9%). In comparison, the synthetic polymers lost only 13.0 ± 11.6% of their initial mass and 42.7 ± 18.4% of their fluorescence intensity, thus increasing the fluorescence discrimination ratio between synthetic and natural materials from 3-fold to 16.9-fold. The protocol retains the chemical integrity of the synthetic polymers (FTIR Hit Quality Index: 89.7-99.3%), which allows further reliable identification of the particles by FTIR. The protocol was applied to samples of Black Sea invertebrate organisms (M. galloprovincialis and R. venosa, 67 specimens) and achieved near-complete organic matter removal (>99.8%). The MP load was higher in M. galloprovincialis (median: 1.3 MPs g -1 WW; Q1-Q3: 0-3.2; n = 27) than in Rapana venosa (median: 0 MPs g -1 WW; Q1-Q3: 0-0.2; n = 40). This validated workflow provides a reproducible and cost-effective approach for large-scale MP monitoring in marine bioindicator species.

items.title: Sinking rates of phytoplankton in the Bohai and Yellow Seas: Insights into the regulatory role of the Yellow Sea cold water mass on carbon export.
items.abstract: Phytoplankton sinking is a key process in the biological carbon pump, driving vertical transport of organic carbon in the ocean. The Yellow Sea Cold Water Mass (YSCWM) is a prominent hydrological feature in the Yellow Sea in warm seasons, yet its association with phytoplankton sinking rates and subsequent carbon export remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated phytoplankton sinking and carbon export in the Bohai Sea and in waters inside and outside the YSCWM through field and statistical analyses. Phytoplankton sinking rates, determined using the settling column (SETCOL) method based on chlorophyll a redistribution after water collection, ranged from -0.20 to 1.64 m d -1 . Both phytoplankton carbon biomass and flux exhibited pronounced spatial heterogeneity, and their spatial patterns were similar. In the Bohai Sea, sinking rates were statistically associated with multiple variables, whereas outside the YSCWM, chemical and biological variables were identified as important predictors. Inside the YSCWM, variance partitioning indicated that measured variables explained only a small fraction of the variation, suggesting that sinking rates in this stratified region are associated with more complex mechanisms. Structural equation modeling indicated that stratification was indirectly and negatively associated with carbon flux inside the YSCWM, whereas the nitrogen to phosphorus ratio was identified as an important indirect predictor outside the YSCWM. However, such statistical associations do not necessarily imply independent ecological mechanisms. These findings provide insights into phytoplankton-mediated carbon export in temperate shelf seas under climate warming.

items.title: Cross-ecosystem assessment of macroplastic pollution in mangrove, coral reef, seagrass, and beach habitats of tropical small islands.
items.abstract: Marine plastic pollution poses an increasing threat to tropical coastal ecosystems; however, comparative understanding of macroplastic accumulation across interconnected habitats remains limited, particularly in small-island environments. This study assessed macroplastic density and composition across mangroves, coral reefs, seagrass meadows, and beaches on three tropical small islands (Panjang, Semujur, and Ketawai) in western Bangka, Indonesia. Field surveys were conducted in May 2025 using ecosystem-specific transect methods, and macroplastic debris was quantified in terms of abundance, weight, volume, and composition. Macroplastic accumulation exhibited clear habitat-dependent patterns. Across the three islands, beaches consistently recorded the highest debris densities (0.193 ± 0.0083-0.680 ± 0.0310 items/m 2 ), whereas coral reefs exhibited the lowest densities (0.003 ± 0.0005-0.009 ± 0.0011 items/m 2 ). Seagrass meadows showed generally low to moderate accumulation (0.002 ± 0.0003-0.082 ± 0.0102 items/m 2 ), while mangroves exhibited intermediate densities (0.067 ± 0.0027 items/m 2 ). Habitat-level differences were statistically significant (Kruskal-Wallis: χ 2 = 78.9, p 2 = 0.465, p = 0.104). These findings demonstrate that macroplastic accumulation across tropical small islands is primarily structured by habitat characteristics and local retention processes, highlighting the need for habitat-specific mitigation measures and integrated coastal management.

items.title: Tillage practices affect the synergetic relationship between soil organic carbon and crop yield under straw return.
items.abstract: Straw returning is a pivotal strategy to enhance soil organic carbon (SOC) concentration and crop yield. However, the synergy between these two outcomes and its spatial variability under different tillage practices remain poorly quantified. Therefore, we conducted a meta-analysis using 1767 paired observations from 222 studies in China, including 726 SOC comparisons and 1041 yield comparisons, with 428 observations contributing to both analyses. Observations with complete baseline soil data were then combined with harmonized gridded spatial predictors to generate scenario-based adaptation maps. Our findings demonstrate that straw return significantly increased SOC concentration by 10.66% and crop yield by 7.96% compared to straw removal, with a significant positive correlation between the two responses. The strength of this synergy, however, was strongly modulated by crop type and tillage practice, and differed between topsoil and subsoil layers. Notably, subsoiling (SS) and no-till (NT) more frequently produced simultaneous benefits for both SOC and yield, whereas conventional tillage (CT) and rotary tillage (RT) showed greater variability. However, these estimates carry uncertainty due to uneven observational coverage for certain crops and the inherent limitations of grid-based environmental data. Our findings suggest that strategic combinations of straw return with appropriate tillage and crop selection can effectively reconcile SOC concentration with productivity goals. We conclude that region-specific adaptation is essential for sustainable agricultural management under straw return.

items.title: Historical trends show more declining than increasing species among European pollinators.
items.abstract: Anthropogenic global change presents a growing threat to insect pollinators. Yet, long-term, continental-scale assessments of their population trends remain limited. Here, we leveraged a curated database of over four million occurrence records, covering 88% of extant bee and hoverfly species in Europe, to assess persistence, richness, and occupancy trends over the past century. Species persistence at the European level was relatively high, with modern records available for 87% of bee and 89% of hoverfly species. Regional richness changes were modest, with declines in the Atlantic and Continental regions for both pollinator groups. Recent increases were observed in the Alpine region for bees, but species richness remained largely stable elsewhere. At the species level, however, a more concerning picture emerged: Most bee species and about half of hoverfly species declined in occupancy. Species traits explained little variation in these trends, although there was a weak tendency for cold-adapted bees to show steeper declines than warm-adapted ones. Genera showing some of the steepest declines include parasitic or dietary specialists, though neither of these traits significantly predicted occupancy trends. Overall, we highlight clear warning signs of species population declines, but with potential recovery opportunities if we take urgent actions to reverse those trends.

items.title: Biotic response networks are an important organizer of the transcriptome in wild Arabidopsis thaliana populations.
items.abstract: Extensive laboratory experimentation has revealed conserved molecular pathways controlling growth and stress responses in plants, yet how these programs operate in natural settings remains poorly understood. We have investigated the organization of the transcriptome in wild populations of Arabidopsis thaliana by sampling plants across 60 natural sites in Europe and North America over two seasons. Transcriptomes varied extensively among individuals and were only weakly structured by geography or season. No groups of plants stood out due to clear biotic or abiotic stress signatures known from the laboratory. While only a small portion of transcriptome variance was explained by disease symptoms or environmental and phenotypic variables, infection-associated signals accounted for the largest share of the explainable fraction. Biotic-response networks identified in controlled laboratory conditions were well conserved in wild transcriptomes, while other networks, including abiotic-response networks were substantially reorganized in wild plants. Together, these results indicate that while certain transcriptional modules are easily reidentified when moving from the wild to controlled conditions, many regulatory relationships differ in these two contexts, highlighting how ecological complexity shapes transcriptome organization in natural populations.

items.title: Integrating airborne chemical ecology with informed intercropping for sustainable crop protection.
items.abstract: The role of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in plant-insect interactions has been studied in detail in recent decades, especially in the context of environment-friendly integrated pest management (IPM) in agroecosystems. Field-based study and behavioural investigations have shown that specific VOCs (or combinations of VOCs) of companion crops are crucial in diverting phytophagous insects from main food or cash crops, along with attracting beneficial insects which decimate pest species. The functional mechanisms of these olfactory cues, however, are not always clear and distinctive, especially since these ecological interactions are highly variable. The complex 'odourscapes' occurring in mixed cropping systems are determined by species-specific interactions, local climate, prevalent agricultural/landscaping practices, and other environmental factors which need to be examined in localized contexts. This review aims to cover the dynamics and mechanisms of VOCs mediating plant-insect interactions in mixed crop settings, the variables and technical constraints to be considered for implementing these interactions for cost-effective IPM, and potential challenges presented by ecological fine-tuning of such interactions.

items.title: Distribution and potential carcinogenicity of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in beached and pelagic tarballs along the eastern Arabian Sea.
items.abstract: Tarballs, the weathered residues of petroleum hydrocarbons, are a recurring feature along the west coast of India, yet their role as carriers of toxic and carcinogenic compounds remains insufficiently quantified. This study presents a comprehensive assessment of the distribution, composition, abundance and carcinogenic potential of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in pelagic and beached tarballs collected along the Eastern Arabian Sea and the adjacent coastal regions (2018-2024). Results indicate that both pelagic and beached tarballs are dominated by low and medium-molecular-weight(LMW) PAHs, with phenanthrene consistently identified as the most abundant compound. Total PAH concentrations were markedly higher in pelagic tarballs than in beached tarballs. Diagnostic PAH ratios and principal component analysis suggest that the observed differences in PAH composition between pelagic and beached tarballs are consistent with the effects of environmental weathering. Assessment based on benzo[a]pyrene toxic equivalents (BaP-TEQ) and carcinogenic PAH fraction (cPAH%) indicates higher carcinogenic potential in pelagic tarballs, whereas beached tarballs exhibited greater spatial variability in PAH composition. Despite evidence of weathering, carcinogenic PAHs persisted in both tarball types, with some locations exhibiting notably elevated contributions. Overall, the study demonstrates that pelagic tarballs function as mobile vectors of carcinogenic hydrocarbons in the marine environment, while beached tarballs act as persistent secondary sources of contamination.. These findings highlight the potential environmental concern associated with tarball-derived PAHs and underscore the need for sustained monitoring and management of petroleum residues along coastal ecosystems.

items.title: Ontogenetic shifts in the metabolomic profiles of Battus polydamas (Lepidoptera: Papilionidae: Troidini) Feeding on Aristolochia gigantea.
items.abstract: Insect development involves profound physiological reorganization that can alter the assimilation and allocation of metabolites across life stages. In herbivorous insects, these processes are tightly linked to diet-derived chemical exposure, yet how metabolic organization shifts throughout ontogeny remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated ontogenetic metabolomic variation in Battus polydamas feeding on Aristolochia gigantea, a system characterized by a specialized ecological interaction between insect and host plant. We examined how chemical profiles vary across larval, pupal, and adult stages, as well as in the host plant and larval frass, to determine whether metamorphosis is associated with stage-specific reorganization of the insect metabolome. Multivariate analyses revealed clear separation among sample types, and PERMANOVA confirmed significant differences among groups. Pupae and adult bodies showed the greatest similarity, whereas plant and frass formed distinct clusters. Wings exhibited a differentiated metabolomic profile. Molecular networking revealed a diverse set of primary and secondary metabolites, including carbohydrates, amino acids, phenolics, fatty acids, and sterol-related compounds. Nine metabolites differed significantly among plant, insect stages, and frass. Lipid- and sterol-related compounds showed stage-specific variation, particularly in pupae and wings, while phenolic derivatives and fatty acids distinguished insect tissues from plant and frass samples. Frass displayed marked chemical divergence, consistent with differential assimilation and metabolic processing. In summary, the metabolomic profile of B. polydamas is reorganized across ontogeny, reflecting stage-specific patterns of metabolite retention and transformation throughout development.

items.title: An update on the mosquito fauna of Aguascalientes, Mexico: morphological and molecular identifications, host-feeding patterns, and the removal of Aedes idahoensis (Theobald) from Mexico
items.abstract: To better understand taxonomic identity and feeding patterns of mosquitoes in all physiographic regions and sub-regions of Aguascalientes, Mexico, we conducted surveillance followed by morphologic analysis and DNA metabarcoding. We sampled natural larval habitat for immature stages and adults were collected using Shannon and CDC light traps, mechanical aspirators, and human landing catch method. In addition, curated specimens from Aguascalientes deposited in a local institution were re-examined. Overall, 5,227 mosquito specimens consisting of 357 larvae, 199 larval exuviae, 373 pupal exuviae, 33 pupae, 3,000 females, 1,264 males, and 1 male genitalia were examined using taxonomic keys. Most immature and adult species (n = 20/34 species representing 58.8% coverage) were barcoded for molecular species designation, and a subsample (n = 64) of engorged female mosquitoes were analyzed for blood feeding patterns. Two subfamilies, four tribes, seven genera, 14 subgenera, and 34 species were identified, which one tribe, three genera, nine subgenera, and 22 species are new records. Phylogenetic analysis of specimens from Aguascalientes identified 20 species. Morphological observation of mosquitoes deposited in entomological collections resulted in the removal of Aedesidahoensis from Mexico, leaving the country with a total of 255 species documented. Bloodmeal metabarcoding was successful in 23 mosquitoes of five species, revealing evidence of feeding on more than a single vertebrate species in 17 individuals. Birds were the most common host with the cattle egret (Ardea ibis) found in 18 out of 23 mosquitoes. This update on the taxonomic identity and mosquito richness and feeding patterns from Aguascalientes affords a better understanding of the ecology of medically important mosquito species.

items.title: Disentangling the effect of maternal mental health on children's academic achievement: A random intercept approach.
items.abstract: A wealth of transactional mother-child effects has been proposed in developmental research, including the potential influence of maternal mental health on children's academic development and vice versa. However, longitudinal multi-informant studies spanning several years remain scarce. In the present study, two birth cohorts were followed from ages 8 to 14 ( N = 747, 49.4% girls) to examine whether maternal anxiety and depression differentially predicted children's academic achievement and vice versa. A cross-lagged random-intercept model was applied to biennially collected data, controlling for stable, unmeasured, time-invariant factors (e.g., shared genetics, parental education) as well as time-varying covariates (e.g., negative life events). Results showed that higher levels of self-reported maternal anxiety and depression consistently predicted-at comparable magnitudes-lower teacher-reported academic achievement across all time points. These effects persisted after adjusting for prior levels of children's emotional problems, school performance, and exposure to negative life events. Moreover, lower academic achievement predicted increased maternal depressive symptoms between ages 10 and 12. The findings underscore the long-term impact of maternal mental health difficulties on children's functioning beyond the immediate family context, likely representing one of several mechanisms contributing to the intergenerational transmission of social marginalization. items.title: An optimized flow cytometry sorting-sequencing workflow reduces storage, sorting, and extraction bias in sorted microbial communities.
items.abstract: Fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) followed by metataxonomics is commonly used to probe the composition of microbial subpopulations with a functionality of interest. Metataxonomic analysis of sorted low-microbial-biomass samples is prone to contamination and bias introduced during sorting and DNA extraction. To improve metataxonomic accuracy, the DNA yield obtained by the DNeasy PowerSoil Pro kit was first maximized. FACS-sequencing using the optimized DNA extraction method distorted the composition of sorted microbiota by introducing sheath fluid contaminants, termed the FACSome. Since FACSome contaminants were experiment-specific, a standardized, applicable in silico decontamination method was developed to characterize and remove FACSome contamination in PacBio and Illumina metataxonomic sequencing data based on carefully selected controls. The optimized DNA extraction and decontamination methods were validated in soil, water, feces, saliva, gut reactor, and mock microbial communities. Metataxonomic profiles of non-selectively sorted and unsorted samples derived from these ecosystems did not perfectly match due to relic DNA depletion during FACS. Effective (97%) relic DNA depletion was confirmed with a spike-in experiment and is desirable since naturally present relic DNA can interfere with function-driven FACS-sequencing. A nuclease-based digest further enhanced relic DNA depletion. Since FACS depleted relic DNA, the preservation of intact cells prior to sorting is essential for activity- or viability-targeted FACS. Intact cells were best preserved during long-term -80°C storage of fecal samples that were not amended with glycerol-1× Tris-EDTA cryoprotectant.IMPORTANCEBulk meta-omics fail to provide sufficient resolution to gain mechanistic insights in microbial ecosystems. Function-driven microbiome research requires high-throughput profiling of active microbial subpopulations. These can be singled out through fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) combined with function-, activity-, or viability-based labeling. The resulting low-biomass sorted samples present a currently overlooked challenge for accurate 16S rRNA gene profiling. We systematically identified all potential sources of interference to enable decontamination of 16S rRNA gene sequences from sorted microbiota. While this study focused on metataxonomic read-outs, our optimized extraction and decontamination workflow can advance other sequencing-based omics analyses of sorted microbial communities. Our optimized FACS-sequencing workflow is thus imperative to unlock the full potential of single-cell labeling and FACS, in turn enabling mode-of-action studies that will broaden our understanding of microbe-environment interactions.

items.title: Seasonal and evolutionary patterns of planktonic Hikarchaeia reveal ecological niches of marine rare biosphere constituents.
items.abstract: Members of Marine Group IV, now termed Hikarchaeia, hold an important transitional evolutionary position among Archaea but remain uncultivated, and their ecology remains uncharacterized. Over a 5-year period, we performed monthly profile sampling in the North Atlantic Subtropical Gyre and sequenced V4 16S rRNA gene amplicons, while also collecting additional size-fractionated and metagenomic samples. Hikarchaeal relative abundance annually peaked at ~1% of prokaryotic amplicons. Their relative abundances were significantly higher after deep winter mixing when thermal stratification isolated exported dissolved organic matter in the twilight zone (TZ), the boundary region between the epipelagic and mesopelagic. A diminutive 1.17 Mbp complete hikarchaeal genome was recovered by sequencing and co-assembling diel TZ metagenomes from 200 m during summer, where their relative abundances were highest. Phylogenomic reconstruction incorporating our new metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) and public MAGs established five clades. Clades I and III were in subtropical and tropical environments, with vertical partitioning: Clade I dominated the TZ, and Clade III detection initiated in the lower mesopelagic and extended into the bathypelagic. Clade V is polar-associated. Data sparsity makes Clade II and IV distributions unclear. All Hikarchaeia recovered thus far appear to be free-living aerobes capable of heterotrophy. Unlike MGI, MGII, and MGIII Archaea, and most marine pelagic bacteria, the Hikarchaeia encode bacterioruberin biosynthesis, except deep Clade III. Hikarchaeia also have nitrile hydratases alongside enzymes for carbon monoxide oxidation and menaquinone biosynthesis, suggesting previously unrecognized roles in nitrogen and carbon cycling. Collectively, our studies reveal niche partitioning of evolutionarily distinct uncultivated Hikarchaeia clades and patterning within the rare biosphere.IMPORTANCEThe ocean and its vertical water-column structure are changing with planetary warming; yet, there are many enigmatic microbes, especially those that inhabit the deep ocean. Here, we illuminate a group of uncultivated Archaea that were discovered over two decades ago but still lack clear distributions and habitat preferences. With the first complete hikarchaeal genome now in hand, we identified distinct lineages within the Hikarchaeia that occupy different marine niches. Strong reoccurring seasonal patterns were observed that closely followed the annual cycle of temperature-driven ocean stratification. Given rapid natural and anthropogenic perturbations at hand, establishing baselines for these Archaea is critical for improving our understanding and modeling of marine microbiomes and their biogeochemical functions.

items.title: Comparative dietary profiling of smoked and non-smoked paprika (Capsicum annuum L.) in Wistar rats: metabolomic, biochemical and gut microbiota responses in a healthy animal model.
items.abstract: Paprika ( Capsicum annuum L.) is a widely consumed spice whose bioactive composition is substantially influenced by processing conditions. Traditional smoking, as applied in the production of PDO Pimentón de la Vera, enriches paprika with wood smoke-derived phenolics while also introducing polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), warranting an integrated evaluation of processing-related biological responses and safety considerations. This study compared physiological, biochemical, metabolomic, and cecal microbiota responses to dietary supplementation with smoked and non-smoked paprika in healthy Wistar rats. Thirty animals of both sexes (16 females and 14 males) received a control diet or diets supplemented with 5% smoked or non-smoked paprika for 30 days. Histological examination revealed no treatment-related alterations in the organs evaluated. Hematological and biochemical analyses showed diet- and sex-associated differences in hematocrit, plasma glucose, total antioxidant capacity, and lipid-related parameters, although all values remained within normal physiological ranges. Untargeted urinary metabolomics, restricted to males because of insufficient urine volume in females, identified features tentatively annotated as phenolic conjugates and other metabolites associated with paprika intake, with several signals showing higher abundance in the smoked paprika group. Cecal metagenomic analyses showed sex-dependent changes across taxon-level abundance, alpha diversity, and beta diversity. In females receiving smoked paprika, lower TC and LDL-C coincided with higher alpha diversity and lower cecal lipid content, suggesting a potential link between intestinal microbial ecology and lipid handling. Overall, paprika processing was associated with distinct biochemical, metabolomic, and cecal microbiota response patterns in this healthy animal model.

items.title: Metal-organic frameworks for photocatalytic CO<sub>2</sub> reduction: recent advances, design principles, and mechanistic insights.
items.abstract: The rising atmospheric CO 2 levels demand sustainable technologies for converting CO 2 into fuels and chemicals. Photocatalytic CO 2 reduction mimics natural photosynthesis but faces great challenges from the inertness of CO 2 , high CO bond energy, slow kinetics, and competing hydrogen evolution. With ultrahigh surface areas, tunable porosity, and modular architectures, metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) serve as a versatile platform, enabling molecular-level integration of light harvesting and catalysis to overcome these limitations. Rational optimization via linker functionalization, heterometal doping, defect engineering, heterojunctions, and morphology control has improved the efficiency and selectivity in CO 2 photoreduction. This review summarizes recent advances in framework engineering and their photophysical mechanisms. Despite progress, there still remain great challenges, such as limited visible-light absorption, low charge mobility, rapid recombination, poor stability, difficulty achieving C 2+ products, and insufficient operando understanding. Future efforts should focus on π-conjugated frameworks, conductive linkers, single-atom/dual-site centers to enable C-C coupling, and in situ / operando spectroscopies combined with theoretical analysis. Moreover, developing sacrificial-agent-free systems using water as an electron donor shows great promise for practical solar-fuel production.

items.title: Curcumin in inflammatory bowel disease: highlighting gut microbiota-metabolite-host interactions.
items.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is driven by a complex interplay among epithelial barrier breakdown, immune dysregulation, microbial dysbiosis, and redox imbalance. Curcumin, a major curcuminoid from turmeric ( Curcuma longa L.) and a widely used food ingredient, has attracted sustained interest as a dietary bioactive for IBD prevention and adjunct management. Notably, curcumin shows low systemic bioavailability, allowing a substantial fraction to reach the distal gut, where it can be biotransformed by the gut microbiota and act locally on the mucosa. This review synthesises recent evidence on: (i) curcumin's gastrointestinal fate, including host conjugation and microbial reduction to more stable metabolites; (ii) the bidirectional curcumin-microbiota relationship, whereby baseline microbial functions shape curcumin metabolism and response, while curcumin remodels microbial ecology and metabolite outputs (short-chain fatty acids, bile acids and tryptophan-derived indoles); and (iii) downstream host pathways linked to barrier integrity, NF-κB and MAPK signalling, immune cell polarisation, and redox-sensitive programmes (Nrf2 and ferroptosis susceptibility). We further discuss food-grade formulation and delivery strategies that tune colonic exposure and microbiota engagement, and outline research priorities for evidence mapping, responder stratification and standardised biomarkers to accelerate translation of curcumin-based functional foods for IBD.

items.title: High-throughput mitochondrial aerobic metabolism measurement: assessing a plate-reader approach using avian blood cells.
items.abstract: Mitochondria power biological processes, driving interest in measuring mitochondrial aerobic metabolism to understand individual variation in performance and fitness. High-resolution respirometry (HRR) is the gold standard because of its sensitivity and versatility, but it is time-consuming and has low throughput, limiting its use in large-scale studies. We assessed the validity of a high-throughput, fluorescence-based plate reader by comparing it to HRR. In a first experiment, we measured mitochondrial respiration in blood cells from two bird species (quails and chickens) across three temperatures (hypothermia, normothermia, and hyperthermia). The two methods were moderately correlated and revealed similar species effects; however, temperature effects differed between approaches, particularly under hyperthermic conditions, indicating that the plate-reader approach is best suited for stable, normothermic conditions. In a second experiment on sex differences in quails at normothermia, the two methods agreed quantitatively for proton leak and oxidative control efficiency and qualitatively for oxidative phosphorylation, although the plate-reader estimate was marginally significant (P=0.060 versus P=0.046 for HRR). The plate reader's main limitation is its lower sensitivity and greater measurement error, which could be offset by increasing sample sizes. Following protocol optimisation for each study system, this approach may offer a useful high-throughput complement to HRR for studies prioritising larger sample sizes.

items.title: Naturalistic Driving Engineered Trajectories Forecast Future Cognitive Decline.
items.abstract: Objectives Early population-based screening for Alzheimer's disease remains limited by the scalability and accessibility of conventional biomarker testing. We tested whether passive naturalistic driving changes predict progression from cognitively normal status to sustained mild cognitive impairment. Methods Season-adjusted monthly driving data from 298 older adults, including 25 progressors, were summarized into within-person trajectory features capturing drift and instability in cornering and destination diversity relative to a six-month baseline. A GEE logistic regression was evaluated under leave-one-out cross-validation with a paired-consecutive flagging rule. Landmark survival analyses at 12 and 24 months assessed prognostic value. Five held-out clinical subgroups (n = 82 evaluable), plasma pTau217, MoCA trajectories, and depression scores provided independent post hoc validation. Results The model detected 19/25 progressors (AUC=0.752, 95%CI: 0.627-0.863; 76% sensitivity; 75% specificity) with an 18-month median lead time before sustained CDR conversion. Adding static baseline driving features reduced discrimination (AUC=0.702), supporting that within-person driving change, not absolute level, carries a predictive signal. Driving markers stratified risk at 12 months (HR = 6.02, 95%CI: 2.35-15.41) and 24 months (HR = 13.38, 95%CI: 3.03-59.04). Signals converged or were directionally consistent with higher pTau217 among detected progressors and clinically ambiguous single-endpoint cases, whereas flagged stable participants showed MoCA decline without pTau217 enrichment. Depressive symptoms did not explain the driving signal (Spearman rho=0.05, p=0.53). The sustained conversion rate (12.3/1,000 person-years) matched epidemiological expectations. Discussion Scalable driving-trajectory features can detect preclinical functional decline with clinically meaningful lead time, without demographic, genetic, or cognitive data, and may serve as an objective neurobehavioral screening tool.

items.title: Attentional territories: The influence of gaze and interpersonal distance in the navigation of public space.
items.abstract: Human gaze is a potent social signal; it communicates attention, intention and social engagement, and allows observers to infer not only where others are attending but also how they are socially related. Although gaze has been extensively studied in direct social interaction, far less is known about how it shapes the perceptions and actions of uninvolved observers in shared environments. Here, we investigate whether mutual gaze creates an 'attentional territory' that third parties implicitly respect. In a large-scale field study across four university campuses in Europe and Canada (N = 4680 pedestrians), two confederates stood facing one another in a public space. We manipulated gaze direction and reciprocity (mutual, unilateral or no interaction) as well as interpersonal distance (2-6 metres), holding body orientation and spatial arrangement constant. Pedestrians were less likely to cross between individuals engaged in mutual gaze. This effect weakened with increasing distance, but was robust across all locations. Together, the findings demonstrate that gaze does not merely coordinate interaction between individuals but also shapes how uninvolved others perceive and move through shared environments. By isolating gaze reciprocity from spatial arrangement, we demonstrate that mutual gaze functions as a dynamic social boundary organizing the permeability of public space.

items.title: Modeling Progressive Brain Volume Losses in Chronic Moderate Severe Traumatic Brain Injury: Extensive, but Attenuating.
items.abstract: Objective Progressive brain atrophy has now been widely observed in the chronic stages of moderate-severe traumatic brain injury (msTBI), but there is only coarse information regarding its prevalence and magnitude, and whether rate of atrophy accelerates or attenuates across time. We examined these questions in a Canadian inception cohort from the Toronto Rehab TBI Recovery Study. Methods N = 123 patients with post-traumatic amnesia ranging from > 1 h to 10 weeks (70%, > 7 days) were administered up to three MRIs at approximately 5 months, 1 year, and 3 years post-injury. N = 32 healthy controls were scanned up to two times on average 14 months apart. Ventricle-to-brain ratio (VBR) was calculated and manual segmentation of the hippocampi (HPC), corpus callosum (CC), and substructures was employed. For each region, annualized rates of progressive atrophy were modeled from approximately 5 months to 1 year and 1 to 3 years post-TBI; proportions of patients with annualized volume losses of 2.5%-5%, 5%-10%, and > 10% were estimated. Results Mixed-effects longitudinal models estimated robust progressive atrophy in both time windows in all regions compared to controls, but with significant attenuation across windows. In the earlier window, > 10% annualized loss was estimated in 76.2% of patients for VBR, 53.2% for CC, and 25.0% for HPC bilaterally. In the later window, at least 5%-10% annualized loss was estimated in 63.3% of patients for VBR, 49.4% for CC, and 17.7% for right HPC; for left HPC, 6.3% of patients showed at least 2.5%-5% annualized decline. Interpretation Clinically concerning prevalence and degree of progressive volume losses were observed in the chronic stages of msTBI, with tapering of losses across time, and regional variations. Research is needed to understand and mitigate clinical impact of these declines.

items.title: Cortical Cholinergic Pathway Degeneration Reflects Cognitive Impairment and Dementia in Parkinson's Disease.
items.abstract: Background Cognitive impairment is a prevalent and debilitating feature of Parkinson's disease (PD). Increasing evidence from postmortem and in vivo positron emission tomography imaging studies supports cholinergic dysfunction in PD. There is, however, little evidence regarding the influence of the structural integrity of cortical cholinergic pathways that emanate from the nucleus basalis of Meynert (NBM). Objectives To investigate the association between cognition and the structural integrity of medial and lateral cortical cholinergic projection pathways in PD. Methods Neuropsychological assessment, T1 imaging, and high angular resolution diffusion imaging (HARDI) were acquired from 108 participants with PD (41 female, mean age 71.3 years) and 41 control participants (22 female, mean age 70.6 years). Streamlines representing three cortical cholinergic pathways (one medial and two lateral) from the NBM were extracted from anatomically constrained tractography. Structural integrity was compared across controls and cognitive subgroups (PD with normal cognition [PD-N], with mild cognitive impairment [PD-MCI], and with dementia [PDD]) and using a continuous global measure of cognition. Results In PD, we found evidence that lower cognitive performance was associated with increased mean diffusivity across all pathways, especially the perisylvian component of the lateral pathway. In those individuals with dementia, increased free water fraction and decreased fractional anisotropy and fiber density and cross-section was detected across all pathways. Conclusions Degeneration of the cortical cholinergic system is associated with cognitive decline in PD. Future work should determine whether pathway degeneration predicts future cognitive decline and dementia. © 2026 The Author(s). items.title: The Japanese Adaptation of the Reading the Mind in Films Test: Differentiating Autism Spectrum Disorder From Depression Using an Ecologically Valid Social Cognitive Task.
items.abstract: Cognitive tests that reflect the complexity of real-world social interactions are essential for autism spectrum disorder (ASD)-related clinical assessment and research. This study developed and adapted a Japanese version of the Reading the Mind in Films (RMF) test, which assesses mind-reading ability through dynamic, multisensory, and context-rich stimuli. Participants included 23 autistic adults, 39 typically developing adults, and 40 adults with depression as a clinical control. RMF scores in the autistic group were significantly lower than in both the typically developing and depression groups. Hierarchical logistic regression analyses showed that RMF performance provided incremental predictive value beyond Reading the Mind in the Eyes test performance in differentiating autistic individuals from typically developing participants and from participants with depression. Receiver operating characteristic analyses further indicated moderate discriminative accuracy of the RMF for differentiating autistic from non-autistic individuals. In contrast, the depression group performed comparably to the typically developing group on the RMF, suggesting that the RMF captures ASD-specific social cognitive difficulties rather than social dysfunction. These findings provide preliminary support for both the construct validity and the potential discriminative utility of the Japanese RMF. This tool has potential applications in future transdiagnostic and cross-cultural studies.

items.title: Mapping mental health complexity in esports: an exploratory psychosocial network approach.
items.abstract: Background The rapid rise in popularity of esports has brought increased attention to the unique mental health challenges faced by esports players, yet research in this area remains in its infancy. Early research suggests a substantial mental health burden and has examined associations between esports-specific stressors, mental health, and sleep disturbances. However, much of this work has relied on traditional methodologies, providing limited insight into how affective, psychosocial, sleep-related, and esports-specific indicators are organised within this competitive performance environment. Methods To address this gap, we developed a bespoke 17-item questionnaire tailored for Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) network analysis, an exploratory approach for mapping the conditional dependency structure of complex multivariate systems such as mental health. Results A total of 1025 esports players from over 60 countries completed the survey. Game-related thought preoccupation, a core feature of gaming disorder, emerged as the most robust structural sink node, downstream of several psychosocial indicators, raising the hypothesis that it represents a compound indicator of broader upstream psychosocial strain. Depressed mood occupied an upstream position within the network, an observation that held more robustly for the psychopathological subnetwork as a whole than for depressed mood as the single source. Mental fatigue occupied an intermediate, connecting position between affective variables and the sleep and fatigue indicators. Its high prevalence, together with a positioning upstream of the sleep indicators, suggests that it may warrant closer examination in future research on training load, recovery, and sleep in esports, though this ordering rested on edges with moderate directional support. Emotion control and a sense of autonomy appeared to connect upstream affective distress with downstream esports-specific indicators such as esports-related stress, though was the least stable of the structural features identified. Conclusions Collectively, these findings provide an exploratory map of how mental health-relevant indicators were organised in this performance environment, and generate concrete, testable hypotheses for future longitudinal, experimental, and intervention research.

items.title: Emotion regulation and its association with subjective memory performance among undergraduate students at port said university.
items.abstract: Background Emotion regulation (ER), particularly through cognitive reappraisal (CR) and expressive suppression (ES), plays an important role in psychological well-being and higher-order cognitive functioning. Both ER and subjective memory performance (SMP), as measured by the Prospective and Retrospective Memory Questionnaire (PRMQ), have been proposed to draw on shared executive control resources. Although memory complaints have been reported among Egyptian university students, the association between ER strategies and SMP remains largely unexplored. This study aimed to assess ER strategies and SMP among undergraduate students at Port Said University and examine the association between these constructs. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional study with an analytical component was conducted among 1,287 undergraduate students from seven randomly selected faculties at Port Said University. Data were collected using a self-administered questionnaire comprising the Emotion Regulation Questionnaire (ERQ) to assess CR and ES and the PRMQ to measure SMP. Data were analyzed using Jamovi version 2.3.28 employing descriptive statistics, nonparametric tests, Spearman's rank correlation, and multiple linear regression. Results Participants had a median total ERQ score of 44 and a median total PRMQ score of 50. Males reported significantly higher ES and total ER scores than females (p Conclusion The findings suggest that greater reported use of ER strategies is associated with fewer self-reported memory complaints among undergraduate students. Although the association was statistically significant, its magnitude was weak, indicating that ER represents only one of several factors associated with SMP. This suggests that effective emotional processing may support the cognitive resources required for daily memory tasks.

items.title: Life's Essential 8 and Psychological Wellbeing in Those with and without Schizophrenia, Schizoaffective Disorder, and Bipolar Disorder.
items.abstract: Background Poor cardiovascular health (CVH) remains a leading cause of early mortality among individuals with serious mental illness (SMI). While psychological well-being (PWB) is linked to CVH in the general population, its role among those with SMI is less understood. Method This cross-sectional study characterized CVH using the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 among those with and without SMI and examined relationships between CVH and PWB. Demographic, clinical, and PWB data were obtained from the electronic health record and a health and wellbeing survey for 156 individuals with SMI and 311 matched controls (2015-2020). CVH and PWB were compared across groups. General linear models examined associations between CVH and PWB factors, and interaction terms tested whether associations differed by SMI status. Results Individuals with SMI had poorer CVH and reported worse PWB in domains of life satisfaction, perceived social support, and gratitude compared to controls. Life satisfaction (b = 1.06, 95% CI [0.35, 1.76], p = 0.004) was positively associated with CVH in the total sample and did not vary by SMI status (p = 0.82). The association of social support with CVH varied by SMI status, such that the positive effect of social support on LE8 was greater among individuals without SMI (b = -11.37, 95% CI [-20.28, -2.48], p = 0.012). Gratitude was not associated with CVH. Conclusion Patients with SMI compared to those without SMI have poorer CVH and PWB. Greater life satisfaction and social support may be protective for CVH, but social support may not have the same association among those with SMI.

items.title: Human-in-the-loop LLM-assisted thematic analysis: A validated, reproducible tutorial for large-scale qualitative research.
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support qualitative research, yet clear methodological frameworks for integrating them into thematic analysis remain limited. A central challenge is how to scale qualitative coding with LLM assistance while preserving methodological rigor and reproducibility. This tutorial presents a structured, human-in-the-loop workflow for conducting large-scale thematic analysis with LLM support. Grounded in inductive and hybrid approaches to thematic analysis (Braun & Clarke, 2006), the workflow proceeds in three phases. First, researchers conduct manual thematic analysis on a subset of data to establish an initial codebook and assess relevance. Second, the same subset is analyzed using an LLM to iteratively refine prompts and evaluate alignment between human and model outputs. Third, the validated approach is applied to the full corpus using a modular four-step pipeline: key-idea extraction, chunk-level thematic coding, theme consolidation, and clustering, with iterative human verification through random sampling of outputs. We demonstrate the workflow using 2,952 publicly available Reddit posts. Structured prompt design and JSON-formatted outputs enable traceability between themes and source data and support reproducible analysis. Prompt engineering is treated as an iterative analytic process rather than a one-time instruction. Under controlled conditions, human and LLM coding showed high agreement (Cohen's κ = 0.91). All prompts, code, and reproducibility materials are openly available via an Open Science Framework repository. By providing detailed implementation guidance, embedded validation procedures, and safeguards against common failure modes such as hallucination and overgeneralization, this tutorial offers a practical and extensible framework for integrating LLMs into qualitative research across domains.

items.title: Generative AI vs. Human Sources for Sexual Health Information: Credibility, Trust, and Behavioral Intentions in a U.S. College Sample.
items.abstract: Limited access to comprehensive sexual health education has prompted a need to consider the utility of alternative strategies, such as generative artificial intelligence (genAI), for delivering accurate and accessible sexual health information. Although genAI tools can generate health information, less is known about how perceptions of the source of information shape evaluations of content (e.g., human vs. genAI). The present study examined whether college students' perceptions of sexual health information differed based on source attribution. Participants (N = 266) were students recruited from a single university in the southeastern USA in 2025. They were randomly assigned to conditions in which they were made to believe that three sexual health passages that were identical across conditions (sexual communication, body image, and sexual pleasure and safety) were written by genAI, an academic expert, a community health professional, or a peer/social media influencer. Across outcomes-including perceived accuracy and clarity, warmth and helpfulness, trustworthiness, self-efficacy, and willingness to act-genAI-attributed information was evaluated less favorably than identical information attributed to human sources. For willingness to act, there were differences in source effects across topics, such that effects were strongest for sexual pleasure/safety and weakest for sexual communication. Findings remained significant after controlling for genAI familiarity/use and attitudes. Findings indicate that evaluations of sexual health information depend not only on informational content but also on perceived source legitimacy, suggesting that AI-based tools may be the most effective when paired with human guidance to support trust and actionability.

items.title: Shared cortical morphometry and molecular signatures across depression and physical diseases.
items.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is highly comorbid with physical diseases, suggesting shared neurobiological mechanisms. However, the common structural and molecular substrates underlying this comorbidity remain poorly understood. We analyzed multimodal MRI data from 577 patients (MDD, asthma, fibromyalgia, gastroesophageal reflux disease, type 2 diabetes) and 275 healthy controls, constructed individual morphometric similarity networks (MSN) to identify shared cortical alterations, and applied principal component analysis with multiscale molecular annotation (transcriptomic, cell-type, neurotransmitter, and cognitive mapping) to characterize underlying mechanisms. All patient groups exhibited regional MSN abnormalities. A shared MSN pattern emerged, featuring increased similarity in visual and somatomotor regions and decreased similarity in ventral attention, limbic, and default mode networks, and was replicated in independent cohorts. This pattern was significantly associated with spatial gene expression enriched for synaptic signaling, membrane potential regulation, and neuronal architecture, with predominant expression in excitatory/inhibitory neurons and astrocytes. It further mapped onto specific neurotransmitter systems, with exploratory cognitive decoding suggesting possible relevance to emotion and social cognition. Related genes overlapped with known risk loci for Alzheimer's disease and bipolar disorder. These findings identify a robust across diseases cortical MSN phenotype linked to convergent molecular and neurochemical correlates, offering a framework for studying shared vulnerability and transdiagnostic mechanisms across depression and physical diseases.

items.title: Motor abstraction training generalizes to the refinement of specific movement patterns.
items.abstract: The ability to abstract the invariant structure of an experience while discarding incidental details underlies generalization across virtually every domain of human cognition, from vision and language to concept learning. Yet whether the motor system generates such abstractions and whether they causally contribute to skilled performance remain open questions. Here we introduce a paradigm in which human participants learned novel movement patterns by precisely copying unfamiliar handwritten characters. To examine the role of motor abstractions in this form of learning, participants were trained on markedly rotated versions of the characters, which recruited substantially different lower-level movements while still maintaining the relevant abstract movement trajectory. Across 11 experiments, abstraction training drove robust performance improvements that were comparable to having repetitive practice on the canonical form of each character. Moreover, this effect was largely motoric in nature: it did not require a visual template, sustained trajectory feedback or mental imagery, and was sensitive to the sequential structure of the movement trajectory. These findings establish a causal role for abstractions in motor learning, revealing that the motor system probably deploys abstractions in the earliest stages of skill acquisition.

items.title: Perceived neighborhood crime and social cohesion trajectories and mental health during COVID-19: Evidence from a 2020-2024 cohort.
items.abstract: We examined longitudinal changes in perceived neighborhood crime and social cohesion from 2020 to 2024 and their associations with depression, anxiety, and loneliness. U.S. adults (N = 895) recruited in spring 2020 completed at least one annual follow-up surveys through 2024. Group-based trajectory modeling identified four perceived-crime trajectories: low (71.7%), increasing (14.9%), decreasing (8.7%), and high (4.8%), and three stable social-cohesion trajectories: high (18.2%), middle (63.9%), and low (17.9%). Multivariable logistic regression showed that, compared with the low-crime trajectory, high and increasing crime were associated with higher odds of depression (OR = 2.61 and 1.82) and anxiety (OR = 3.08 and 1.87), whereas decreasing crime was associated with lower odds of loneliness (OR = 0.55). Compared with high cohesion, low cohesion was associated with higher odds of depression (OR = 6.38), anxiety (OR = 4.81), and loneliness (OR = 4.17). Complementary within-between mixed-effects models showed that within-person increases in perceived crime were associated with higher depression (β = .12), anxiety (β = .15), and loneliness (β = .19), whereas within-person increases in social cohesion were associated with lower symptoms (β = -0.02 to -0.04). Findings indicate consistent longitudinal associations between neighborhood perceptions and mental health across person-centered and variable-centered approaches.
