items.title: Lung Restriction From Childhood Is Associated With Obstructive Sleep Apnoea in Middle-Age.
items.abstract: Background and objective Whether lifetime lung function trajectories and spirometry patterns are associated with Obstructive Sleep Apnoea (OSA) is unknown. We aimed to investigate this association to widen the understanding of OSA pathophysiology. Methods We previously identified six FEV 1 /FVC (forced expiratory volume in the first second/forced vital capacity) and five FVC trajectories within a population-based prospective cohort (n = 2422) using spirometry assessed at ages 7, 13, 18, 43, 50, and 53 years. These trajectories were combined into four lifetime spirometry patterns: restrictive-only, obstructive-only, mixed, and reference (normal), which were our exposure variables. Outcomes were medically-confirmed OSA in midlife and probable-OSA defined using the STOP-Bang questionnaire. Associations were assessed using logistic regression models. Results The 'restrictive-only' spirometry pattern was associated with medically-confirmed OSA (OR = 2.5; 95% CI 1.5, 4.3). In addition, restriction-confirmatory low total lung capacity and reduced functional residual capacity were associated with increased odds of medically-confirmed OSA (OR = 1.4; 0.9, 2.1 and OR = 1.7; 1.1, 2.6, respectively, per one SD reduction in volume). The results were similar for probable OSA. These associations held when controlled for BMI and central obesity and were independent of childhood lung function. Neither transfer factor for carbon monoxide (T L co) nor transfer coefficient (Kco) was associated with OSA. Conclusion We provide first evidence that lifetime lung restriction is related to middle-age OSA. While this information may be used to incidentally flag middle-age OSA risk and vice versa, further research is encouraged to confirm the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms.

items.title: Identification of individual animals from position, orientation, and movement sequences in the Morris water task with machine learning: implications for spatial learning.
items.abstract: The Morris water task (MWT) has been the gold standard assessment of place learning and memory for over four decades, yet the processes that contribute to successful navigation are not completely understood. It is generally posited that rats learn to navigate directly to a place; however, navigation is not perfectly direct but contains variation in swim speed and trajectory, resulting in efficient, yet suboptimal paths. Recently, our lab demonstrated that path topography is quantitatively similar across trials within individual rats for a given start location, and dissimilar between rats and different start locations within rat. This suggests rats may take unique paths to the platform from each release point. If the sequences of position and heading changes in the MWT are reinforced based on individual experience, it should be possible to objectively classify (identify) individual rats using machine learning. In the present study, a recurrent neural network was trained to classify 15 rats based on trial-level time-series data of path coordinates, velocity, and orientation. Testing on unseen coordinates or combined features from the same starting locations yielded classification accuracies that were 5.93- to 7.26-fold greater than chance and significantly greater than data from different start locations. Classification using scalar metrics with support vector machines was unable to match these outcomes. Collectively, these observations support the hypothesis that navigation in the MWT involves learning to perform behavioral sequences.

items.title: Cardiorespiratory Fitness in Young Adulthood and Depressive Symptoms Later in Life Among Swedish Men.
items.abstract: ObjectivesThis study investigated whether cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) in young adulthood is associated with depressive symptoms several decades later and if later-life physical activity and self-rated health mediate this association.MethodsThe sample comprised 690 Swedish men completing a CRF test at age 18 and self-reported depressive symptoms around age 61. Unadjusted and adjusted logistic and linear regression models and Bayesian mediation analyses were estimated.ResultsMedium and high CRF at age 18, compared with low CRF, were associated with lower odds of clinically significant depressive symptoms in late adulthood. The odds ratios of clinically significant depressive symptoms were 0.329 (95% CI [0.157, 0.687]) for men with medium and 0.383 (95% CI [0.157, 0.939]) for men with high CRF compared with those with low CRF. No credible mediated associations were observed.ConclusionThese findings suggest that promoting fitness early in life may represent a useful preventive strategy for mental health resilience across the life course.

items.title: Learning to become a tutor: Experiences of adults with intellectual disabilities in peer tutoring for digital skills.
items.abstract: Societies are digitalizing services with a rapid speed. As a result, people, such as adults with disabilities, are at risk of being excluded if they lack appropriate digital skills and have few possibilities to get support in learning these skills. Peer tutoring is seen as an effective way to learn these skills according to research done on peer tutoring with older adults and immigrants, but there remains a gap in research with adults with intellectual disabilities and their preferences for digital skills learning. This article focuses on the experiences of Finnish adults with intellectual disabilities in digital skills peer tutoring courses they attended. The data were collected by conducting semi-structured interviews via Teams with ten participants. The results indicate that digital skills training activities supported the peer-tutor trainees' learning, their skills to support others with technology use, and their social inclusion in Finland's digitalized society.

items.title: Neural Response to Monetary and Social Feedback in Childhood: Processing Reward and Loss in Relation to Peer Outcomes and Anxiety Symptoms.
items.abstract: Anxiety disorders are the most prevalent psychiatric conditions in childhood and are associated with social functioning impairment. How youth process rewards may contribute to the development of social impairment in childhood anxiety. Although aberrant reward processing is a well-established mechanism of psychopathology, associations with anxiety remain inconsistent and limited, especially in childhood. This study investigated neural response to monetary and social reward feedback in relation to anxiety and peer functioning in children. Children (N=106; Age=8.12±.68 years) completed the Doors Task and the Island Getaway Task while electroencephalogram (EEG) recordings assessed event-related potentials (ERPs) to wins and losses. Parents completed questionnaires assessing child anxiety, depression, and peer relations. Contrary to pre-registered hypotheses, we found a significant Valence (reward versus loss) by Condition (monetary versus social) interaction. Specifically, children exhibited greater neural response to monetary loss than reward, but showed the opposite pattern in the social condition, with greater neural response to social reward than loss. Higher child- and parent-reported total and generalized anxiety predicted significantly greater neural response to monetary reward, but not monetary loss or social feedback. As hypothesized, anxiety symptoms significantly moderated the association between neural response and peer relations, demonstrating that for highly anxious children, a greater neural response to social loss predicted worse peer relations. Findings demonstrate differences in neural response to monetary and social feedback processing. Moreover, the distinct vulnerability to social rejection might impair peer functioning in anxious children, suggesting that clinical interventions targeting social rejection processing may effectively improve peer outcomes in childhood anxiety.

items.title: Subjective emotional ratings dissociate brain activation and network patterns during counterfactual outcome processing.
items.abstract: Human decision-making integrates outcome evaluation, counterfactual comparison, and individual traits. We investigated the neural processing of outcome-related emotions during economic decision-making by classifying feedback according to participants' subjective emotional ratings rather than objective gain-loss categories. Participants completed a Wheel of Fortune gambling task during fMRI scanning and provided emotional ratings for feedback outcomes, enabling identification of regret, relief, disappointment, and elation. We also assessed individual differences in regret proneness, maximization tendencies, alternative search, high standards, and decision difficulty. Behaviorally, emotional ratings increased with larger obtained outcomes and decreased as reference outcomes increased, indicating robust modulation of outcome evaluation by counterfactual information Whole-brain analyses revealed greater activation for low-rating than high-rating outcomes, indicating stronger neural responses to negative than positive emotions across feedback types. Complete feedback also elicited greater activation than partial feedback within the same emotional valence. Network-level analyses revealed partially dissociable neural profiles for positive and negative emotions. Positive emotions, including elation and relief, predominantly recruited the somatomotor network, whereas negative emotions, including disappointment and regret, engaged broader distributions across the default mode, dorsal attention, and other large-scale networks. Regret elicited the largest activation extent, whereas elation elicited the smallest. Region-of-interest analyses showed that bilateral orbitofrontal cortex (OFC) responses were significantly greater for negative than positive emotions and for complete than partial feedback conditions. Across all four emotions, right OFC activation was negatively associated with maximization. For elation, relief, and disappointment, right OFC activation was also negatively associated with alternative search and decision difficulty, whereas these associations were absent for regret. Together, these findings demonstrate that subjective emotional evaluation, counterfactual context, and decision-related traits jointly shape the neural processing of decision outcomes, while suggesting relatively trait-independent neural processing of regret.

items.title: Systematic, contextual, and individual influences drive trialists' behaviour relating to greener trial design and delivery - A qualitative study.
items.abstract: Objectives To identify the key behavioural determinants that influence how people working in clinical trials ('trialists') design and deliver greener trials. Study design and setting We conducted semi-structured focus groups and interviews with trialists involved in the design and conduct of clinical trials in the UK. Participants were recruited from a preceding survey, supplemented by purposive sampling through established trial networks and professional groups. Data collection was guided by the Theoretical Domains Framework (TDF) where analysis combined deductive TDF coding with inductive thematic development. Results Three focus groups and nine interviews with a total of 23 participants including diverse roles, such as Clinical Trials Unit (CTU) directors, trial managers, statisticians, Quality Assurance staff, and researchers, were conducted. We identified 34 belief statements across all 14 TDF domains which were synthesised into five overarching themes: 1. Developing and promoting a culture for greener trials; 2. Weighing up the anticipated benefits against the unknowns; 3. Tensions between intrinsic and extrinsic priorities; 4. Degree of control over the enablement of greener trials; and 5. Negotiating gaps to address individual uncertainties. The study found that trialists' actions were shaped by a range of behavioural mechanisms. Cultural and contextual constraints, competing priorities, and limited organisational support were key challenges; while leadership, funders' expectations, and existing sustainability practices were identified as potential opportunities. Conclusion This study provides an in-depth theory-informed behavioural analysis of the challenges and opportunities for making clinical trials greener. These findings provide a basis for designing behaviour change strategies to support trialists' adoption of greener trials.

items.title: Toward a Psychology of Science: A Dynamic Cognitive Model of the Evolution of Scientific Theories.
items.abstract: Responding to a recent call for the development of a psychology of science, we examine how scientists manage empirical anomalies, a routine yet consequential challenge in scientific practice, and how their responses shape theory development. We argue that defensive anomaly-reduction strategies, which allow researchers to preserve an initial theoretical claim, can generate important secondary benefits. During the emergence phase of a theory, they foster auxiliary revisions that may reduce underfitting and place a fragile theory on a growth trajectory. During the exploitation phase of established theories, they help sustain attention to problems derived from the theory and support cumulative research. However, their accumulation may also increase the risk of overfitting, reduce predictive power, and set the theory on a degenerative trajectory. We illustrate these dynamics primarily through examples drawn from psychological theories, with a focus on responses to replication failures. Last, we derive several implications for peer review aimed at fostering scientific innovation. In particular, we propose shifting evaluation away from the consistency of findings, which may penalize emerging research programs and hinder innovation, and toward how inconsistencies are managed, thereby fostering growth trajectories, including for mature programs confronted with anomalies.

items.title: Long-term episodic memory alterations and the role of perceived stress in post-COVID-19 condition.
items.abstract: Post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) is frequently associated with cognitive impairments, but the integrity of long-term episodic memory remains poorly understood. This study examined immediate, short-term, and very long-term episodic memory in individuals with PCC and evaluated whether emotional disturbances predict long-term recognition outcomes. Forty-one participants (30 PCC; 11 non-PCC) completed a verbal cued-recall task and an immersive virtual reality free-recall object-location memory (OLM) task immediately after learning and the following day. Nine months later, three recognition tasks (verbal, word-list of objects, and visuospatial recognition) and questionnaires assessing anxiety, depression, and perceived stress were administered. PCC participants required significantly longer retrieval times than non-PCC participants in the immediate and delayed OLM trials. Nine months later, PCC participants exhibited significant impairments in verbal cued-recall compared to the immediate and one-day recall trials. Performance on the word-list task was poorer in the PCC group, whereas scores in verbal and visuospatial recognition tasks remained comparable between groups. Emotional symptoms were significantly higher in the PCC group. Exploratory regression analyses suggested a negative association between perceived stress and nine-month visuospatial recognition performance in PCC participants. These preliminary findings suggest a potential vulnerability of very long-term verbal episodic memory in PCC, alongside slowed retrieval processes and heightened emotional distress. The observed association between chronic perceived stress and visuospatial recognition suggests a potential role of stress in very long-term memory performance. Overall, the results highlight the need for long-term cognitive follow-up in PCC and identify perceived stress as a potential factor relevant for long-term recognition of visuospatial information.

items.title: Metacognitive monitoring in Kenyan, Chinese, and U.S. children.
items.abstract: Theories of cognitive development propose that cultural values shape metacognitive skills. However, cross-cultural research on metacognition remains limited and often relies on verbal assessments that may lack validity across cultural contexts. The present study examined metacognitive monitoring in Kenyan, Chinese, and U.S. children (N = 95; 6-10-year-olds; 46% female) using a non-verbal problem-solving task in which children assembled objects according to a model. Across all three cultural contexts, children exhibited various monitoring behaviors (e.g., checking the model), and the frequency of these behaviors increased with age. Cross-cultural differences emerged in the specific monitoring strategies children used: Chinese children engaged in more thorough monitoring than Kenyan and U.S. children. These findings highlight both culturally-recurrent and culturally-variable patterns in children's metacognitive monitoring.

items.title: Silhouette-based body dissatisfaction and positive psychological functioning in Uruguayan adults.
items.abstract: Objective This study aimed to analyze the relationship between silhouette-based body dissatisfaction and positive psychological functioning (PPF) in Uruguayan adults, and to explore differences according to sex, body mass index (BMI), and body satisfaction status. Participants completed the Stunkard Figure Rating Scale (SFRS), the Positive Psychological Functioning Scale (PPFS), the General Health Questionnaire-28 (GHQ-28), the Dutch Eating Behavior Questionnaire (DEBQ), and a sociodemographic survey. Results Body dissatisfaction was negatively correlated with PPF total score (r = -0.28, p Conclusions Silhouette-based body satisfaction status was associated with higher positive psychological functioning and lower psychological distress. When age, sex, living situation, BMI, psychological distress, subjective socioeconomic level, and PPF were considered simultaneously, PPF remained independently associated with body dissatisfaction. These findings suggest that silhouette-based body satisfaction status is associated with psychological resources and may be relevant for understanding broader psychological functioning. items.title: Growing into the groove: Developmental changes in the pleasurable urge to move to music.
items.abstract: Groove - the pleasurable urge to move to music - provides a behavioral index of how perceptual, motor, and reward systems are engaged and coupled by rhythm. Although groove has been widely studied in adults, little is known about its developmental trajectory. We examined how groove evolves across early to mid-adolescence using a cross-sectional (N = 290) and longitudinal design (N = 105). Participants aged 11-15 rated their urge to move to music stimuli varying in low, moderate, and high levels of rhythmic and harmonic complexity. Across both studies, groove showed the well-established inverted U-shaped relationship with rhythmic complexity, peaking at moderate levels; however, this pattern varied by age. In the cross-sectional study, groove declined with age selectively at high levels of rhythmic complexity. The longitudinal study revealed a comparable decline over time for high rhythmic as well as harmonic complexity levels. These findings indicate that adult-like groove patterns emerge during early adolescence. More broadly, they suggest two complementary developmental processes: broader predictive priors that drive curiosity for highly complex structures in early adolescence, and increasing engagement with moderately complex structures that facilitate sensorimotor coupling and social coordination in mid adolescence.

items.title: Cognitively demanding motor exercise and subsequent inhibitory control: Behavioral and ERP Evidence.
items.abstract: Purpose Acute exercise can influence executive function, yet conventional exercise prescriptions primarily characterize its physical dose and rarely specify the cognitive operations embedded within the exercise bout. Using a Motor-Cognitive Integrated Task (MCIT) with conditions differing in cognitive demand while involving comparable physical demands, this study examined whether cognitively demanding motor exercise was associated with differences in subsequent behavioral and neurophysiological indices of inhibitory control. Methods Forty healthy young adults completed two counterbalanced sessions separated by at least 24 h. In the experimental session, participants performed the MCIT, which required whole-body responses to flanker stimuli. In the control session, participants performed the same motor task in response to predictable single-arrow stimuli. Heart rate (HR), physical rating of perceived exertion (RPE), cognitive RPE, response time (RT), movement time (MT), and overall response time (RMT) were assessed during the MCIT. Immediately afterward, participants completed a computerized flanker task while electroencephalography was recorded. Results Cognitive RPE, RT and RMT of the MCIT were higher in the experimental session than in the control session, whereas HR, physical RPE, and MT of the MCIT were comparable across sessions. Following the MCIT, participants showed a smaller flanker interference in the experimental than in the control session, accompanied by differences in conflict-related modulation of the N2 and smaller overall P3 amplitude, with no between-session difference in accuracy. Conclusions Cognitive demand may represent a manipulable characteristic of acute exercise prescription beyond physical intensity alone. Motor exercise incorporating greater cognitive demands was associated with reduced subsequent behavioral interference and differences in N2 and P3 modulation. Although these effects cannot be attributed exclusively to any specific cognitive operation, the findings highlight the potential importance of considering the cognitive characteristics of exercise when examining its acute neurocognitive effects.

items.title: Cognitive forecasting: How intuitive theories of attention shape anticipated risk preferences.
items.abstract: How do people forecast their own and others' risk preferences? Although it is well established that affective forecasts shape decision-making, less is known about where these forecasts come from. Five studies demonstrate that people rely on intuitive theories of attention when forecasting future affect-such as dread and savoring while waiting for a risk to be resolved-with these affective forecasts in turn shaping willingness to take such risks. In Study 1, forecasts of the participant's own expectations and attention were systematically related to forecasts of positive and negative affect during a waiting period, which in turn predicted risk preferences. Studies 2a and 2b demonstrate substantial heterogeneity in intuitive attention-affect theories: some participants believed attention amplifies the emotional consequences of expectations, whereas others believed attention is uniformly affectively negative. These differences led to sharply divergent predictions about when attention should increase or decrease risk-taking. Study 3 shows that attention is also informative about expectations: participants differed in whether they believed attention signals optimism or pessimism, producing downstream consequences for affective forecasts and risk-taking. Finally, Study 4 reveals that many people endorse asymmetric causal models, viewing optimism as a cause of risk-taking, but risk-taking as a cause of attention. Together, these findings show that forecasts of risk preferences depend critically on people's intuitive theories about how cognition shapes affect and how affective utility is generated over time. By integrating affective forecasting, attention, and decision-making under uncertainty, this work highlights the role of metacognitive beliefs in shaping economic preferences.

items.title: Mind wandering and executive functions: A conceptual replication of Kam & Handy (2014).
items.abstract: Mind wandering - a spontaneous shift in attention away from a task - has been consistently associated with impaired cognitive task performance, often attributed to disruptions in executive functioning. In this study, we conducted three experiments to replicate and extend previous work (Kam & Handy, 2014) by examining how mind wandering interacts with three core executive functions: Inhibition (Experiment 1: Sustained Attention to Response Task, n = 54), updating (Experiment 2: Random n-back Task, n = 52) and shifting (Experiment 3: Number-Letter Task, n = 54). If mind wandering is closely related to executive functioning, it was expected that mind wandering would impair performance on trials requiring these functions, reflected in lower accuracy and increased reaction time variability. Our findings did not confirm this: Mind wandering was associated with a general negative effect on performance, rather than specifically impairing executive functioning. Accuracy was lower on executive than non-executive trials in the inhibition and shifting tasks, but these effects were not attenuated by mind wandering. In the updating task, where executive and non-executive trials were matched in difficulty, mind wandering reduced accuracy in both executive and non-executive trials. Variability in reaction time was found to be higher during mind wandering in the inhibition and updating tasks, with evidence against such an effect in the shifting task. These findings suggest that the observed performance decrements may be more closely tied to task demands than to executive functions per se.

items.title: Dietary Supplement Use and Beliefs Among Athletes at the 2025 Canada Games.
items.abstract: Dietary supplement use is widespread among athletes; however, limited data exist regarding supplement use and beliefs among Canadian youth athletes. This cross-sectional online study aimed to examine dietary supplement use and related beliefs among athletes competing at the 2025 Canada Games in St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador. A total of 473 respondents participated in the survey. Of the 473 participants, 385 completed responses to the dietary supplement (DS) questions. Among participants who reported their sex, 125 were male and 189 were female. Overall, 36% of participants reported current dietary supplement use. Supplement use was significantly higher among males than females (47% vs. 23%, p < .001) and increased with age (p = .001). The most commonly reported supplements were protein powder (49%), sports drinks (46%), and creatine (45%). Primary reasons for use included maintaining good health (76%), increasing energy (54%), and promoting recovery (50%). Coaches (50%) and healthcare professionals (49%) were the most frequently reported information sources. Supplement users demonstrated significantly stronger positive beliefs regarding benefits of dietary supplements compared with non-users (all p < .001). Ordinal logistic regression showed that supplement users had greater odds of stronger agreement that supplements improve performance (OR = 5.50, 95% CI: 3.31-9.13, p < .001). These findings highlight the use of dietary supplements among Canadian youth athletes and support the need for targeted nutrition education to promote informed decision-making.

items.title: Virtual Reality for Enhancing Self-Compassion and Reducing Burnout Among Mental Health Care Professionals: Protocol for a Pilot Feasibility Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.abstract: Background Mental health care professionals working in high-demand clinical environments are frequently exposed to patient suffering and trauma, placing them at increased risk for burnout and secondary traumatic stress. Compassion-focused cognitive behavioral therapy (CF-CBT) has shown promise in reducing psychological distress and enhancing self-compassion; however, traditional delivery methods may be limited by time, accessibility, and resource constraints. Virtual reality (VR) may provide an immersive and accessible approach for delivering compassion-focused interventions. Objective The primary objective is to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of a self-administered VR-enhanced CF-CBT (VR-CF-CBT) intervention for mental health care professionals. Secondary exploratory objectives are to estimate changes in self-compassion, burnout, and secondary traumatic stress (STS), as well as between-group differences that can inform the design of a future definitive trial. Methods A 2-arm randomized controlled pilot trial will be conducted among mental health care professionals. Participants will be randomized to either a VR-CF-CBT intervention or an active comparison condition consisting of self-guided CF-CBT delivered via digital booklets. Participants will complete 8 brief sessions (approximately 10 minutes each) over a 4- to 6-week period. Exploratory clinical outcomes will include changes in self-compassion, burnout, and STS measured using validated self-report instruments. Primary feasibility and acceptability outcomes will include recruitment, retention, intervention adherence, session completion, participant satisfaction, and scores on the Acceptability of Intervention Measure, Intervention Appropriateness Measure, and Feasibility of Intervention Measure. Results The study was funded in April 2026. As of October 2026, 38 participants had provided consent and enrolled. Recruitment for a second wave of participants is ongoing, and data collection is in progress. Enrollment and data collection are expected to continue through 2026, with data analysis and dissemination of findings anticipated by spring 2027. Conclusions This pilot study will provide information on the feasibility and acceptability of delivering CF-CBT through immersive VR to mental health care professionals. Findings will help identify whether modifications are needed before a larger trial and provide preliminary estimates to inform the design of future efficacy testing. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07666867; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07666867. International registered report identifier (irrid) DERR1-10.2196/105754.

items.title: Practice Effects on Repeated Self-Administered Digital Cognitive Assessments in Cognitively Intact Older Adults from the Framingham Heart Study: Longitudinal Observational Study.
items.abstract: Background Remote, self-administered digital assessments provide scalable approaches for monitoring cognition in older adults. Practice effects (PEs), once viewed as measurement noise, are increasingly recognized as potential markers of cognitive decline. As disease-modifying therapies for neurodegenerative conditions emerge, longitudinal digital assessments may capture subtle cognitive changes. Although the majority of PE studies have focused on memory tasks, it is critical to determine whether PEs occur in other domains. Clarifying the potential presence of PEs across multiple time points on the Food and Drug Administration-cleared Defense Automated Neurocognitive Assessment (DANA) platform remains critical for determining whether PEs can serve as a measure of cognitive decline longitudinally. Objective This study aimed to examine whether PEs occur and whether demographics moderate them across quarterly self-administrations of digital cognitive tasks spanning different cognitive domains in cognitively intact older adults. Methods Cognitively intact older adults from the Framingham Heart Study self-administered DANA tasks at baseline and every 3 months for 1 year (4 assessments: T1-T4). Tasks included Simple Reaction Time (SRT), Go/No-Go (GNG), and Code Substitution (CS). These tasks varied in complexity, from simple motor responding (SRT) to inhibitory control (GNG) and associative learning with working memory demands (CS). The primary outcome was Cognitive Efficiency, a derived measure of speed and accuracy, which are also recorded as secondary measures. PEs were quantified using linear mixed-effects models, and the change in mean score across time points was expressed in pooled SD units as Cohen d . Results A total of 717 participants completed all 4 time points (mean age 64.1, SD 9.5 years; n=469, 65.4% female participants; n=481, 67.1% college-educated). PEs were observed on all tasks, with small effects on CS ( d =0.43) and GNG ( d =0.32) and a below-threshold effect on SRT ( d =0.16). Demographics influenced baseline performance: older age predicted lower baseline scores on all tasks, females scored lower on SRT and GNG, and higher education predicted better performance on all tasks. Age was the only demographic moderator of PEs, with smaller improvements on CS among participants aged 65 years or older (B=-0.39; P Conclusions Quarterly self-administered digital cognitive assessments elicited measurable PEs across processing speed, inhibitory control, and visual scanning, with stronger effects on more complex tasks. Demographics influenced baseline performance, while age moderated PEs on the most demanding task. These findings provide baseline data against which PEs in clinical populations can be compared in future work, complementing prior evidence on other cognitive instruments.

items.title: Comparison of Laboratory- Versus Home-Based Assessments for Infants at Elevated Likelihood for Neurodevelopmental Disabilities.
items.abstract: Objective While many studies pivoted to telehealth and distance methods in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, few studies have directly and systematically compared data obtained from home and lab settings. Our goal was to evaluate the impact of these contextual and methodological differences across multiple developmental domains. Method Participants included 111 infants (33 infants with a family history of autism, 51 with a family history of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), and 27 infants with no family history of either diagnosis) who participated in a laboratory-based assessment and a paired telehealth session at 6 or 9, 12 and/or 18 months of age. Both sessions included multiple measures of infant skills across multiple developmental domains (e.g. receptive and expressive language, play, cognition), and autism- and ADHD-specific measures. Mixed models for repeated measures compared scores across contexts and timepoints and validity was evaluated via multitrait-multimethod matrix. Caregiver ratings of representativeness and acceptability were also evaluated. Results Convergent validity was supported by significant positive correlations between language, social-communication, and developmental measures across the two contexts, ranging from moderate (0.37) to high (0.80). Multilevel models revealed that developmental trajectories were broadly comparable across settings, though significant cross-context differences were observed, particularly for the 18-month timepoint. Conclusions We found broad consistency in scores obtained across the two contexts, suggesting that remote assessments can provide valid and reliable developmental data. The high parent satisfaction ratings also suggest remote assessments are feasible and acceptable to families.

items.title: Comparative Seroprevalence of Brucella Antibodies in Apparently Healthy Sheep and Goats in a Rural District of Central Nigeria.
items.abstract: Background Brucellosis, caused by bacterial pathogens of the genus Brucella , is a chronic zoonotic disease affecting small ruminants such as sheep and goats. This study evaluated and compared the seroprevalence of Brucella antibodies among apparently healthy sheep and goats in Vwang District, Jos South Local Government Area, Plateau State, Nigeria. Methodology A cross-sectional study design was employed from May to June 2024. A total of 140 serum samples collected from goats ( n = 77) and sheep ( n = 63) using systematic random sampling across four administrative wards were screened for Brucella antibodies using the Rose Bengal Plate Test (RBPT) and confirmed via the Complement Fixation Test (CFT). Results Overall, 8 out of 140 samples (5.71%, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.50%-10.95%) were reactive on RBPT screening. Upon confirmatory testing with CFT, 6 samples were validated, yielding an overall CFT-confirmed seroprevalence of 4.29% (95% CI: 1.59-9.09%). Seroprevalence was higher in sheep (6.35%, 95% CI: 1.76-15.47%) than in goats (2.60%, 95% CI: 0.32-9.07%); higher in females (4.95%, 95% CI: 1.63-11.18%) than in males (2.56%, 95% CI: 0.06-13.48%); and restricted to animals older than 18 months (6.74%, 95% CI: 2.51-14.10%) compared with younger ones (0.00%, 95% CI: 0.00-6.98%). Geographically, the Turu B Ward recorded the highest seroprevalence (5.88%, 95% CI: 0.72-19.68%). None of the demographic associations reached statistical significance ( p > 0.05). Conclusion This study provides serological evidence of Brucella exposure among apparently healthy sheep and goats in Vwang District, Central Nigeria. Although seroprevalence differences across species, sex, age, and location were not statistically significant, the detection of antibodies in nonvaccinated, clinically healthy livestock highlights the value of routine serological monitoring in rural agrarian communities.

items.title: Life's Essential 8, Genetic Susceptibility, and Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease in Chinese Adults.
items.abstract: Background: Limited evidence exists regarding the association of cardiovascular health (CVH) with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) in Chinese adults, and the influence of genetic risk on this association remains unknown. This study aimed to investigate these associations and discern potential variations based on genetic risk. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 17,077 participants from the third resurvey of the China Kadoorie Biobank. CVH was evaluated by Life's Essential 8 (LE8), with the overall score (0 to 100) calculated as the unweighted average of its 8 component scores and categorized as low (0 to 49), moderate (50 to 79), or high (80 to 100). Polygenic risk score (PRS) for MASLD was generated by meta-analytic approach and large genome-wide association data of liver steatosis and related traits. Genetic risk for MASLD was categorized into low, intermediate, and high based on quintile of metaPRS. The multivariable logistic regression model was used to evaluate the associations of CVH with MASLD and advanced fibrosis in MASLD, subsequently stratified by metaPRS. Results: High CVH was associated with over 90% lower risk of MASLD and advanced fibrosis in MASLD, with odds ratios of 0.07 (0.06 to 0.08) and 0.04 (0.02 to 0.05) compared to low CVH, respectively. Interactions of metaPRS were observed for the impacts of LE8 on both prevalent MASLD and advanced fibrosis in MASLD ( P value for interaction Conclusion: In Chinese adults, adhering to a high CVH was associated with lower odds of prevalent MASLD and advanced fibrosis in MASLD, particularly among individuals at high genetic risk.

items.title: Improving cardiovascular care in a resource-limited setting through the HEARTS initiative in Suriname, 2022 to 2025.
items.abstract: Objective To evaluate early implementation of the HEARTS initiative in Suriname (2022-2025), identify key barriers and facilitators, and assess initial program performance. Methods A mixed-methods implementation evaluation was conducted using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) and the Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance framework (RE-AIM). Qualitative data were collected through structured monitoring, training and workshop feedback, and stakeholder consultations from December 2021 to December 2025, and analyzed deductively using predefined CFIR constructs. Quantitative indicators were assessed across RE-AIM domains, including reach, adoption, implementation fidelity, and early maintenance. Results HEARTS was implemented in 56 primary health care facilities, involving 460 health care workers and 11 187 patients. Scale-up was rapid, with facilities increasing from 21 to 56 over six semesters. Among patients with follow-up measurements, blood pressure control improved from 47.0% to 56.2%. However, only 52.6% had at least one follow-up visit, indicating suboptimal continuity of care. Key facilitators included strong political commitment, standardized treatment protocols, and a real-time digital monitoring system. Major barriers were limited workforce capacity, infrastructure variability, and financial constraints affecting access to essential medications and equipment. Conclusions Early HEARTS implementation in Suriname shows that rapid scale-up of standardized cardiovascular care is feasible in a mixed public-private system. Strengthening follow-up, workforce capacity, and sustainable financing are essential to achieve long-term effectiveness and population-level impact.

items.title: Association between atherogenic index of plasma at 11-20 weeks of gestation and gestational diabetes risk: A prospective cohort study in China.
items.abstract: Background Recent studies have linked insulin resistance and the onset of type 2 diabetes mellitus to the atherogenic index of plasma (AIP). This integrated lipid marker reflects cardiovascular risk and atherogenic dyslipidemia. However, its relationship with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is not completely understood. This study aimed to evaluate the association between AIP measured at 11-20 weeks of gestation and the subsequent risk of GDM and to identify the optimal AIP threshold for GDM prediction. Methods A total of 2068 women with singleton pregnancies were included in this prospective cohort study from the Tongji Maternal and Child Health Cohort. AIP was calculated from fasting triglycerides and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) measurements obtained at 11-20 weeks of gestation, before GDM diagnosis by 75-g oral glucose tolerance test at 24-28 weeks of gestation. Subgroup analysis, restricted cubic spline models, and multivariable logistic regression were used to assess the relationship between GDM and AIP. The predictive performance of AIP alone and in combination with maternal age, pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI), and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) was compared via receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. Results Gestational diabetes mellitus was diagnosed in 252 participants (12.3%). Women in the highest AIP quartile demonstrated a substantially higher risk than those in the lowest quartile (adjusted odds ratio 2.56; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.63-4.01; P Conclusion Elevated AIP levels at 11-20 weeks of gestation were independently associated with an increased risk of GDM. Importantly, the inclusion of AIP alongside established maternal risk factors enhanced predictive accuracy. The findings of this study indicate that AIP might serve as a useful adjunctive biomarker in early antenatal screening to identify women at heightened risk for GDM.

items.title: Beyond the silo: Single-disorder ADHD clinics and the case for more integrated care.
items.abstract: ObjectiveThe rapid growth of ADHD assessment and prescribing in Australia reflects a gap between demand and service availability. Workforce shortages, restrictive stimulant regulations and limited adult ADHD care within public mental health services have contributed to this gap. ADHD-focused clinics have emerged in response. Using two de-identified clinical scenarios, this paper examines the drivers of this model and its potential harms.ConclusionFocused clinics can improve access and provide expertise. However, a narrow scope and fee-for-service model may also encourage transactional and fragmented care. We describe this risk as organisational iatrogenesis. Potential harms include incomplete formulation, uncoordinated prescribing and missed psychiatric, neurodevelopmental or neurocognitive comorbidity. Broader concerns include inequity, cost, discontinuity of care and erosion of generalist skills. The solution is not to restrict focused practice, but to integrate it more effectively with mainstream care. Priorities include nationally consistent prescribing rules, stronger shared-care arrangements with general practitioners, greater adult ADHD capacity within public services and clearer standards for scope-restricted practice. These issues are also relevant to other single-disorder models of psychiatric care.

items.title: Characterizing Heat Health Hazards and Receptivity of Cooling Interventions Among Indoor Lumber Mill Workers in Southern Thailand.
items.abstract: Objective To evaluate the effectiveness and feasibility of two workplace cooling strategies and identify priorities for future mixed-methods research and practical solutions. Methods A pilot randomized crossover field trial was conducted among 12 sawmill workers in southern Thailand under three conditions: no cooling (CON), a phase change cooling vest (VEST), and a combined cooling oasis (OASIS: hydration, fans, water dousing, cooling towels). Core temperature and heart rate were continuously monitored. Worker perceptions were explored through post-intervention focus group discussions. Results Compared with CON, OASIS reduced core temperature (-0.24°C; 95% CI: 0.23, 0.25) and heart rate (-7 bpm; 95% CI: 6, 9), while VEST reduced core temperature (-0.17°C; 95% CI: 0.17, 0.18) and heart rate (-5 bpm; 95% CI: 4, 6). Despite greater physiological benefits from OASIS, most workers preferred VEST due to ease of use and caused minimal disruption to workflow. OASIS was perceived as effective but interruptive. Conclusions Combined cooling strategies can reduce heat strain in indoor industrial settings; however, the adoption of interventions is strongly influenced by practicality and economic considerations. Hybrid approaches and structural improvements are recommended. A full mixed-methods study is needed to evaluate effectiveness, productivity, and cost-effectiveness to inform scalable occupational heat policies.

items.title: Metal Accumulation, Liver Histopathology, and Human Health Risk Assessment Across Different Trophic Guilds in a Mining-Affected Neotropical River.
items.abstract: Metal pollution in aquatic environments represents a recurring global concern; however, traditional paradigms often assume linear bioaccumulation patterns that may fail under catastrophic contamination scenarios. This study evaluated metal concentrations in water, sediment, and tissues of 10 fish species from different trophic guilds in the Paraopeba River after the Brumadinho dam collapse. Multivariate analyses (principal component analysis [PCA], generalized linear model [GLM], and PERMANOVA) were used to explore associations between metal concentrations, ecological traits, and body size integrated with liver histopathology (Histopathological Alteration Index) and Human Health Risk Assessment. Results revealed that metal concentrations in water and fish tissues exceeded regulatory limits, whereas sediment acted as the main reservoir of metals, exhibiting higher concentrations than water. High-severity liver damage was concentrated in benthic piscivores and benthopelagic detritivores, exposing a complex interplay between biomagnification and direct substrate contact. Human Health Risk Assessments indicated unacceptable noncarcinogenic risks driven by aluminum (Al), along with elevated carcinogenic risks for chromium (Cr) and cadmium (Cd) for both adults and children in the region analyzed. These findings demonstrate that ecological traits were associated with differences in metal accumulation, liver damage, and public health threats, reinforcing the need for nonlinear models in postdisaster regulatory frameworks.

items.title: Evaluation of Clinical Outcomes of Selective Versus Nonselective Beta-Blockers Among Patients With Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction Receiving Sacubitril/Valsartan.
items.abstract: Background Beta-blockers, selective (metoprolol succinate or bisoprolol) and nonselective (carvedilol), and angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors (ARNIs) are the first-line guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). Concomitant use of carvedilol and ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan) may result in additive vasodilatory effects, which may increase the risk of hypotension and limit dose titration of sacubitril/valsartan. Objective This study examines differences in clinical endpoints between selective and nonselective beta-blocker therapy among patients with HFrEF receiving sacubitril/valsartan. Methods This retrospective cohort study utilized TriNetX Research Collaborative real-world data. Patients receiving sacubitril/valsartan concomitantly with carvedilol were identified as the intervention cohort, while those receiving metoprolol succinate or bisoprolol served as controls. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality or all-cause hospitalization during the 3-year follow-up. Propensity score matching (PSM) balanced confounders. Kaplan-Meier analyses were used to estimate event-free survival, and hazard ratios (HRs) were calculated using Cox proportional hazards models for time-to-event outcomes. Sensitivity analyses were conducted to evaluate the robustness of the findings. Results Overall, 75 230 patients received carvedilol and 21 587 received metoprolol/bisoprolol. After PSM, 20 939 patients were included in each group. Carvedilol was associated with a higher risk of the primary composite endpoint compared with those taking metoprolol or bisoprolol (52.32% vs 46.29%; HR: 1.21; 95% CI, 1.17-1.24; P P P = .0011). In addition, carvedilol was associated with higher risks of hypotension, end-stage renal disease, and bradycardia. Sensitivity analysis results were consistent for the primary endpoint. Conclusion and relevance Our results suggest that carvedilol may be associated with a higher risk of the composite endpoint, health care utilization, and adverse events but lower all-cause mortality compared with metoprolol or bisoprolol in patients with HFrEF taking sacubitril/valsartan.

items.title: Longitudinal associations of trajectories of physical activity and sitting time with depression during middle-to-older adulthood.
items.abstract: Objectives Vulnerability to depression symptoms often increases from late middle adulthood into older adulthood and can significantly impact daily functioning. Modifiable lifestyle behaviours may support mentally healthy ageing, but changes in physical activity, sitting time, and depression symptom trajectories across middle-to-older adulthood are not well understood. Understanding whether these trajectories change together may identify modifiable behavioural patterns linked with depression symptoms over time. Method Using data from a subset of community-dwelling middle-aged and older adults from a larger study (mean age = 57.8 years at baseline; N = 1190), assessed on three occasions spanning 11 years, this study examined associations between trajectories of physical activity, sitting time, and depression symptoms using latent growth modelling. Results Trajectories of increasing physical activity were associated with trajectories of decreasing depression symptoms over time. However, change in sitting time was not associated with change in depression symptoms. Conclusion Findings contribute to the limited evidence on longitudinal associations between modifiable lifestyle behaviours and mental wellbeing among middle-aged and older adults and may inform research examining causal pathways linking physical activity and depression. If replicated in studies designed to test causal mechanisms, these findings may have implications for future physical activity guidance and clinical or public health approaches.

items.title: The Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Oral Cancer Screening: Real-World Data From Taiwan.
items.abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted cancer screening services worldwide, but its impact across multiple screening indicators remains unclear. Methods This population-based interrupted time series study evaluated the impact of COVID-19 on oral cancer screening in Taiwan. Two intervention points were defined: January 2020 and May 2021. Four indicators were assessed: screening rate, screening positivity rate, incidence, and mortality. Segmented regression analyses were performed across six National Health Insurance divisions, and changes in stage at diagnosis (2018-2022) were examined. Results At baseline, screening rates declined, screening positivity rate and mortality increased modestly, and incidence remained stable. After the first outbreak, screening positivity rate showed a significant immediate decrease (OR = 0.86, 95% CI: 0.81-0.92, p Conclusions The first outbreak had the greatest impact on screening-related indicators, with findings consistent with possible delays in cancer detection. Maintaining organized screening services during public health emergencies is essential to minimize delayed cancer detection.

items.title: Suicide and Overdose Mortality Among Victims and Defendants in Felony Domestic Violence Criminal Cases.
items.abstract: Domestic violence (DV), death by suicide, and death by overdose are major public health concerns in the United States. While existing studies have documented associations of DV with both suicide and overdose, most studies utilize nonfatal outcomes and lifetime DV exposure. In this population-based case-control study, we aimed to estimate the association of both suicide death and overdose death with involvement in a DV case, either as a victim or alleged perpetrator, referred for felony charges in the year prior to death. All deaths in King County, Washington, United States or deaths occurring elsewhere among King County residents were included ( N = 113,388), as were all felony DV referrals to the King County Prosecuting Attorney's Office. Suicide deaths ( n = 2,243) and overdose deaths ( n = 3,578) were separately matched to deaths of all other causes, and conditional logistic regression was used to determine associations of case status with DV referral in the year prior to death. We found an association of DV referral as a defendant with both suicide (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 3.68, 95% confidence interval [CI] [2.33, 5.81], p p p p = .42). These findings highlight a need for suicide and overdose prevention efforts among people involved in DV cases. Future research could evaluate prevention strategies and examine mediating links between DV and both suicide and overdose.

items.title: Developing scenario-based, near-term iterative forecasts to inform water management
items.abstract: Near-term, iterative ecosystem forecasts with scenarios representing alternate management decisions have high potential for providing valuable insights on how decisions may impact future ecological conditions. Scenario-based forecasts may be particularly useful for informing the decision-making around freshwater ecosystems managed for multiple objectives. We applied a near-term, iterative forecasting system at Lake Alexandrina, Australia, which is located at the nexus of one of the world’s largest catchments and a protected coastal wetland. Lake Alexandrina is highly managed through multi-gate barrages to optimize catchment, lake, and outflow targets, providing an unparalleled opportunity to investigate the value of scenario-based probabilistic forecasting for decision-makers. We co-developed the forecasting system with managers to generate automated 1-30 day-ahead barrage operation scenario forecasts. Over ~2 years, forecasts accurately predicted lake water level, water temperature, and salinity and outperformed null baseline models up to 10-30 days ahead. Alternative barrage scenarios were particularly important during drier hydrological conditions and resulted in substantive changes to lake level and salt export from the lake. Lake temperatures and salinity were less sensitive to barrage operations and generally more dependent on variability in lake inflow discharge. Overall, our study provides a framework for forecasting lake water quantity and quality variables for anticipatory decision-making.

items.title: Functional diversity complements taxonomical diversity in productivity-biodiversity relationships in freshwaters
items.abstract: Abstract Productivity is widely considered a key driver of biodiversity, yet whether taxonomic and functional diversity respond similarly to productivity gradients remains unclear. Using phosphorus as an indicator for productivity gradient, we compiled 78 freshwater datasets spanning > 30,000 sites globally to test how productivity–biodiversity relationships (PBRs) vary across diversity dimensions, trophic groups, and ecosystems. We show that PBRs are predominantly unimodal across taxonomic and functional dimensions, with slightly weaker curvature for functional diversity. Unimodal PBRs are more pronounced in producers than in consumers and show stronger curvature in lakes than in rivers. Functional reorganization also varies along the phosphorus gradient, with the clearest contraction in resource-related trait space and marked shifts in community functional centroids. Climatic, geographic and human land-use gradients further modify PBR shape. These findings indicate that predicting biodiversity responses to productivity benefits from considering functional diversity, ecological context, and broad-scale environmental gradients.

items.title: Lattice Boltzmann Methods for Compressible Magnetohydrodynamics
items.abstract: Abstract Compressible, magnetised plasma flows pervade astrophysics, from stellar winds to planetary magnetospheres and the interstellar medium. Their high-fidelity simulation at scale is limited by the non-local operations that conventional solvers require for flux reconstruction, gradient and stress evaluation, and magnetic-divergence control, which bottleneck communication on heterogeneous supercomputers. We present a novel class of fully local Lattice Boltzmann Method (LBM) schemes for compressible magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) in which all nonlinear operations are point-wise. The approach exploits the kinetic structure to transport each state variable of the Strang-split conservation laws alongside its characteristics, recovering the compressible macroscopic fluxes, gradients, and viscous stresses through local relaxation rather than finite-difference stencils. Divergence control enters as a local source term within the same kinetic update, with no separate global solve. The formulation is partial-differential-equation agnostic and encompasses hydrodynamic limits such as the compressible Euler and incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. We discretise both ideal compressible and resistive incompressible MHD, and validate the scheme across multiple resolutions against the canonical astrophysical MHD test suite: the Brio-Wu shock tube resolves compound waves and slow-fast shocks, the MHD rotor captures strong torsional Alfvén waves, and the Orszag-Tang vortex reproduces current-sheet formation and the transition to MHD turbulence. Implemented in the performance-portable framework OpenLB, the scheme reaches up to 98.9 per cent of the hardware roofline on GPU. Finally, as a capability demonstration, we simulate a rotating, surface-resolved magnetised body modelled after 16 Psyche in a supersonic early solar wind, yielding an emergent bow shock, flux-rope magnetosheath, and reconnecting magnetotail.

items.title: Spectator axions in string inflation and primordial black holes
items.abstract: A bstract We study the impact of light spectator axions on the seeding of primordial black holes (PBHs) during inflation in string theory. Primordial black holes exhibit unique and novel phenomenology, and may constitute the observed dark matter. Cosmic inflation provides a mechanism for producing them, but such inflation models typically feature Planckian field excursions, necessitating an ultraviolet completion into quantum gravity. String theory provides a natural framework for doing so, and indeed Fibre Inflation has been shown to produce PBHs while satisfying constraints from cosmic microwave background data. In this work we study the dynamics of axions during Fibre Inflation, and find a diverse and rich set of possibilities, including turns in field space and enhancement of primordial perturbations. We find that across most of parameter space, notably an axion with a far sub-Planckian decay constant f ≪ M Pl , there is a negligible impact on the power spectrum of curvature perturbations, indicating an overall robustness of the model. On the other hand, an axion with a larger but still sub-Planckian decay constant, f ≳ 𝒪(0 . 1) M Pl , and an exponentially small prefactor of its non-perturbative potential, can enhance the growth of perturbations, making it easier to achieve the amplification needed to seed PBHs, effectively realizing axion-assisted PBHs in string theory.

items.title: Constraining lunar lower-mantle attenuation using ScSH-SH amplitude ratios
items.abstract: Summary Seismic attenuation in lunar lower mantle can provide critical constraints on thermal state and composition of the deep interior; however, previous estimates based on path-integrated amplitudes are strongly influenced by near-surface scattering, especially for narrow-band waveforms recorded by Apollo’s sparse seismic stations. Here we show that the amplitude ratio between ScSH and SH from the same station can mitigate this limitation. We measure these ratios from narrow-band records and invert for lower-mantle Q by matching them with synthetic predictions that account for geometric spreading, source radiation, and interface transmission. Synthetic tests verify that the method recovers Q within 10 per cent for SNR ≥ 10 and remains robust to scattering and source mechanism uncertainties. Application to a terrestrial deep earthquake recovers Q = 308 (IQR: 280–340), consistent with the PREM reference value (Q ≈ 312), confirming its feasibility on real data. Application to Apollo deep moonquake records (10 stacked records) shows that the amplitude ratios exhibit the expected single-peak distance trend and yield broadly consistent Q estimates across narrow bands, though the limited data warrant interpreting these results as a feasibility demonstration. This framework provides a practical and complementary constraint on lunar lower-mantle attenuation and is transferable to other planetary datasets with similar data limitations.

items.title: Dynamic Optical Alignment Method for AIMS
items.abstract: Abstract The Accurate Infrared Solar Magnetic Field Measurement System (AIMS) is a mid-infrared telescope designed for high-precision solar magnetic field observations. Due to its open-truss structure and off-axis optical configuration, the system is prone to gravityinduced misalignment between the primary and secondary mirrors, which degrades image quality. To address this issue, this paper proposes a dynamic image quality alignment method based on a Shack–Hartmann wavefront sensor and a hexapod-mounted secondary mirror. The method uses nighttime point-source observations to measure system wavefront errors at different elevation angles and establishes an elevation-dependent lookup table through iterative optimization. Numerical simulations incorporating atmospheric turbulence and detector characteristics show that multi-frame averaging significantly improves wavefront reconstruction accuracy and stability. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method reduces the system wavefront root mean square (RMS) to within 0.16 λ at 630 nm at different elevation angles, thereby significantly improving imaging performance. During daytime observations, pre-calibrated correction parameters combined with temperature compensation enable dynamic image quality alignment. This approach enhances the operational stability and imaging capability of AIMS and provides a practical solution for image quality correction in large ground-based telescopes.

items.title: Expression–Cognitive Design Theory: A Unified Framework for Imaginative Lexicon, Critical Periods, and Cognitive Stimulus Mechanisms
items.abstract: Expression–Cognitive Design Theory presents a unified, interdisciplinary framework for explaining how linguistic expressions, narrative structures, and character designs activate deep neurocognitive systems that drive imagination, emotion, and value formation. Integrating cognitive psychology, developmental linguistics, evolutionary psychology, and narratology, the theory formalizes four neurocognitive switches, two critical lexical periods, and eight stimulus mechanisms that systematically induce cognitive completion. The central claim is that imaginative response emerges when simple lexical items are combined with deep-psychology triggers and structured meaning gaps. This interaction engages shared cognitive hardware shaped through evolutionary pressures, enabling expressive stimuli to function universally across individuals. The theory further explains why childhood emotional vocabulary and adolescent identity-related vocabulary retain privileged access to adult cognition, and why simple lexicon maximizes decoding efficiency and imaginative simulation. The paper includes a formal system definition (Appendix A) and a practical lexicon/stimulus template set (Appendix B), providing operational tools for experimental design, narrative construction, media analysis, and expressive design. This work establishes Expression–Cognitive Design Theory as a foundational interdisciplinary framework for the scientific study of imagination and expressive impact.

items.title: Deleting, generalising and constructing: How undergraduate ESL learners explain and exemplify van Dijk’s macrorules
items.abstract: Van Dijk’s (1980) macrorules of deletion, generalization and construction define the mechanisms via which readers reduce a text to its global meaning. These have long inspired the teaching of summary writing. The study explored how undergraduate ESL learners, being taught the macrostructure theory in a Discourse Analysis course, described and exhibited the three macrorules. The examination responses of thirty-one students of a public university in Pakistan were coded on a four-point scale (0 to 3) for each macrorule and the scores were analyzed through descriptive statistics, competence bands, Friedman test and Spearman correlations along with qualitative analysis of the responses. Average scores were similar for deletion (M = 1.77), generalization (M = 1.71) and construction (M = 1.84) and did not differ significantly (χ²(2) = 1.20, p = .549). The rules had different distributions: deletion and construction were dispersed over the scale, while 77.4% of learners scored at the appropriate level for generalization and no one scored at the high level. The three measures were substantially intercorrelated (ρ =.661 to.775, p <.001). The composite scores revealed 19.4% of learners in the low band, 45.2% in the intermediate band and 35.5% in the high band. The qualitative analysis produced three patterns: non-engagement with the macrostructure item, definitional treatment without operational illustration, and functional application supported by worked instances. In the strongest answers the functional application was expanded to critical discourse analysis. Instruction should take learners from textbook examples of generalization to independent abstraction.

items.title: Mental Workload: Physiological Assessment and Validation Using Visual Stimuli
items.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper provides a notion for the use of electroencephalography (EEG) in the field of cognitive science. In particular, we investigated the brain activity of operators while spotting the differences in similar‐looking pictures at three levels of difficulty. As many practical loads are fundamentally intrinsic, the task was designed to specifically induce intrinsic workload (the productive load as per Cognitive Load Theory (CLT)). The experiment used the task: Spot the Difference to create a workload scenario comprising three difficulty levels: spotting five differences, three more differences, and two more differences (along with retaining the previous differences from working memory). The task was designed intrinsically as the operators are generally occupied with tasks involving working memory and requiring attention towards the varying number of resources. By utilising the brain signatures a mental workload model was developed employing a Support Vector Machine (SVM) as the classifier. The workload levels were classified within an accuracy range of 84% to 98% ( p < 0.05). Moreover, using subjective ratings about the workload on NASA's Task Load Index (NASA‐TLX) rating scale, workload scores were obtained for validation corresponding to the difficulty levels. Finally, a correlation study showed the association of different EEG features with the workload score within a correlation coefficient range of 0.306 to 0.748 ( p < 0.05 2‐tailed). The reported results can also provide new insights into the cognitive workload assessment of the operators at various phases of task loads. Findings of this type may lead to the industrial and professional measurement and improvement of cognitive aptitude soon.

items.title: Beyond Physical Performance: Integrating the Psychology of Religion, Embodied Cognition, and Psychospiritual Development in Athletic Achievement
items.abstract: Athletic achievement is commonly evaluated through competition results, yet the processes that sustain participation, learning, bodily adaptation, identity, and psychological well-being extend beyond physical performance. This critical integrative narrative review develops a research framework linking psychology of religion, grounded and embodied cognition, and psychospiritual development in sport. It differentiates religious affiliation from situation-specific coping, bodily signal detection from interpretation, and developmental change from short-term performance fluctuations. Published scholarship on religion and spirituality in sport, meaning-making, self-determination, interoception, resilience, and athlete mental health provides the conceptual foundation. The proposed context-meaning-embodiment-development framework describes conditional paths from personal values and social environments through bodily appraisal, motivated action, reflection, and longer-term adaptation. Its potential benefits include coherent purpose, flexible coping, and sustained participation; adverse pathways include spiritual struggle, externally imposed identity, compulsive ritual, and delayed health care. No new participants, original empirical results, meta-analytic estimates, or validated assessment instrument are presented. The article proposes preregistered longitudinal and mixed-method investigations incorporating repeated observations, comparisons with secular meaning systems, carefully defined behavioral and performance outcomes, measurement-equivalence checks, and athlete autonomy safeguards. The current evidence supports examination of these interacting domains but cannot establish a unique causal contribution of religious belief to sporting success. A scientifically useful account must demonstrate incremental explanatory value, remain open to null findings, and preserve the distinction between excellence, well-being, and personal meaning. psychology of religion; embodied cognition; psychospiritual development; athletic achievement; interoception; athlete well-being

items.title: From possession conditions to the genesis of concepts: Peacocke and Cognitive Psychiatry
items.abstract: Christopher Peacocke proposed that a concept is individuated by the conditions a subject must meet to possess it, bringing the philosophy of concepts closer to cognition, but he left unexplained how those conditions arise. This article aims to propose, from the standpoint of Cognitive Psychiatry, a genetic and communicational theory of conceptualization that completes Peacocke’s theory of possession conditions. It is a theoretical proposal essay supported by a narrative review of recent literature (2021–2026) in philosophy of mind, cognitive science, developmental psychology and neuroscience. A possession condition describes a state; a formation condition describes the history that produced it. Conceptualization begins in bodily praxias coupled to processes in the world, whose integration sediments a processuality that organizes later experience as a genetically constituted processual a priori: functionally prior, genetically acquired. A blind person who possesses DOG shows that conceptual identity depends on sufficient processual convergence, not on a shared sensory modality. Peacocke’s method works as reverse engineering of the adult concept, whereas Cognitive Psychiatry proposes an embryology of the concept. Since concepts have different formation routes, a differential genetics and a differential clinic of conceptualization are required, informed by clinical dissociations. Communication takes part in conceptual genesis, so publicity becomes cognitive-communicational interoperability, and supra-individual objectivity is explained historically, without a Platonic realm. At both levels, the constituted becomes constituent. A three-level integration is proposed: formation, possession and development. Objections are answered and testable predictions derived. Peacocke is not wrong, but genetically incomplete.

items.title: Embodied Faith and Athletic Cognition: Interoception, Religious Meaning-Making, and Self-Regulation in Sport Başlığı kopyala
items.abstract: Athletic cognition is shaped not only by explicit goals and strategic decisions but also by bodily sensations, expectations, attention, and culturally grounded interpretations of experience. This critical integrative review considers whether religious and spiritual meaning-making may alter how athletes interpret effort, arousal, fatigue, uncertainty, and setbacks, without presuming that religious commitment improves objective performance. It connects research on interoception, embodied cognition, attentional regulation, stress appraisal, religious coping, and sport resilience. The synthesis distinguishes sensory detection from appraisal, deliberate contemplative practice from automatic motor skill, and personal faith narratives from experimentally supported mechanisms. A conditional embodied-meaning framework is developed in which bodily signals and contextual expectations interact with identity and coping strategies to influence interpretation, behavioral choices, and participation. Potentially beneficial processes include flexible attentional reorientation, acceptance of transient discomfort, and value-consistent persistence; adverse pathways include hypervigilance, shame, ritual dependence, and misinterpretation of medically significant symptoms. No new participants, original quantitative data, or experimental effects are reported. The article proposes longitudinal and mixed-method studies comparing religious and secular meaning frameworks, using preregistered outcomes, matched interventions, measurement-invariance testing, and ethical safeguards. Existing literature establishes the relevance of bodily perception and meaning-making as separate domains, but their specific interaction in athletic performance remains insufficiently tested. The framework is intended to generate falsifiable questions, not a new diagnostic or performance assessment tool. embodied cognition; interoception; religion and spirituality; sport psychology; cognitive appraisal; self-regulation

items.title: Lived Experiences of Bureau of Jail Management and Penology Escort Personnel in Selected City Jails in the Province of Cebu
items.abstract: This study addressed the limited qualitative attention given to the lived experiences of Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) escort personnel in the Philippine correctional context, particularly the operational demands of escorting persons deprived of liberty outside controlled jail environments. It explored the experiences of BJMP escort personnel in performing their duties, the ways they cope with challenges, and their aspirations for improving service delivery. A qualitative transcendental phenomenological design was employed. Ten BJMP escort personnel assigned to selected city jails in Cebu Province participated through four in-depth interviews and one focus group discussion involving six participants. Participants were purposively selected using criteria requiring non-commissioned officer status, at least three years of escort-related experience, and current assignment in the selected city jails. Data were gathered through a validated semi-structured interview guide, audio recording with consent, and note-taking, then analyzed using Colaizzi’s phenomenological approach. Forty-one cluster themes were synthesized into ten emergent themes. Positive experiences were represented by Honor Behind the Uniform, Guarding Through Unity, Discipline Beyond Duty, and Strength in Shared Experience, while challenges were reflected in Bearing the Weight of Responsibility and Enduring Amid Constraints. Coping was expressed through Standing Firm in Uncertainty and Anchored by Faith and Family, while aspirations centered on Pursuit of Professional Excellence and Preparedness Through Collective Support. The findings indicate that escort personnel derive fulfillment from competence, teamwork, discipline, and successful mission completion while simultaneously managing operational risks, resource limitations, and unpredictable field conditions. The study concludes that effective escort operations require sustained professional development, adequate logistical and personnel support, functional safety resources, teamwork, and institutional mechanisms that recognize personnel welfare and field-based needs.
