items.title: From Trust to Loyalty in Fashion Retail: The Mediating Role of Customer Satisfaction in an Emerging Philippine Market
items.abstract: This study examines how customer trust translates into loyalty in an emerging-market fashion retail context, with customer satisfaction tested as the mediating mechanism. Although previous studies have established relationships among trust, satisfaction, and loyalty across retail and service settings, comparatively limited evidence explains how these mechanisms operate in Philippine fashion retail. Integrating the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) and Cognition-Affect-Conation frameworks, trust is conceptualized as a cognitive appraisal of retailer credibility, satisfaction as an affective-evaluative response, and loyalty as conative intention. A cross-sectional explanatory-predictive survey was conducted among 315 customers of a selected international fashion retailer in Angeles City, Philippines, and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Customer trust positively predicted customer satisfaction (β = 0.811, p < .001) and customer loyalty (β = 0.610, p < .001), while satisfaction predicted loyalty (β = 0.240, p < .001). The indirect effect through satisfaction was significant (β = 0.195, p < .001), confirming partial mediation. The model explained 65.9% of the variance in customer satisfaction and 66.7% of the variance in customer loyalty. The findings show that trust strengthens loyalty both directly and through satisfaction, extending trust-based loyalty research in Philippine fashion retail and underscoring the need for credible communication, consistent service, and dependable customer experiences. The findings further demonstrate that integrating the S-O-R and C-A-C frameworks provides a coherent explanation of how cognitive evaluations are translated into affective responses and subsequently into customer loyalty within an emerging Philippine fashion retail context, thereby contributing localized evidence to the growing body of trust-based loyalty research.

items.title: Expression–Cognitive Design Theory: A Unified Framework for Imaginative Lexicon, Critical Periods, and Cognitive Stimulus Mechanisms
items.abstract: Expression–Cognitive Design Theory proposes a unified framework for understanding how linguistic expressions, narrative structures, and character designs activate deep neurocognitive mechanisms that drive imagination, emotion, and value formation. Integrating insights from cognitive psychology, developmental linguistics, evolutionary psychology, and narratology, the theory formalizes four neurocognitive switches, two critical lexical periods, and eight stimulus mechanisms that systematically induce cognitive completion. The central claim is that imaginative response emerges when simple lexical items are combined with deep-psychology triggers and structured meaning gaps. This interaction engages shared cognitive hardware shaped through evolutionary pressures, enabling expressive stimuli to function universally across individuals. The theory further explains why childhood emotional vocabulary and adolescent identity-related vocabulary retain privileged access to adult cognition, and why simple lexicon maximizes decoding efficiency and imaginative simulation. The paper provides both a formal system definition (Appendix A) and a practical lexicon/stimulus template set (Appendix B), allowing researchers, educators, and creators to operationalize the theory in experimental design, narrative construction, media analysis, and expressive design. This work establishes Expression–Cognitive Design Theory as a foundational interdisciplinary framework for the scientific study of imagination and expressive impact.

items.title: Geospatial Assessment of Land Use and Land Cover Change Impacts on Wetland Ecosystem Services in West Arsi Zone, Ethiopia
items.abstract: Human livelihoods and well-being rely heavily on ecosystem services (ESs) provided by natural environments, with wetlands standing out as some of the most biologically diverse and economically valuable ecosystems worldwide. Despite their importance, wetlands face increasing threats from land use and land cover (LULC) changes driven by human activities. This study examines how LULC changes have affected wetland ecosystem service values (ESVs) in the West Arsi Zone of Oromia, Ethiopia, over a 30-year period from 1995 to 2025. Multi-temporal Landsat images were analyzed using cloud-based geospatial tools on the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform, and land cover classification was done with the Random Forest (RF) machine-learning algorithm. Field observations and ground reference data helped improve classification accuracy and identify the main drivers behind land cover changes. Ecosystem service values were estimated using a locally adapted benefit transfer method based on established valuation coefficients. The results show that rapid population growth, agricultural expansion, urban development, and infrastructure construction are the key forces driving LULC changes in the area. Settlement expansion significantly increased cropland-related ESVs from around USD 0.1 million to USD 2.5 million. However, this economic gain came mostly at the cost of wetlands, whose ecosystem service values dropped sharply from USD 1.17 million to just USD 0.05 million. Overall, the total ecosystem service value of the landscape fell by 3.9%, from USD 16.55 million in 1995 to USD 15.91 million in 2025. These findings highlight clear biodiversity loss and declining ecosystem function, emphasizing the urgent need for sustainable land-use planning that balances socio-economic growth with wetland conservation to protect long-term ecological health and human well-being.

Understanding floristic composition and vegetationdistribution is essential for biodiversity conservation, forest management, and sustainableutilization of natural resources. This study highlights the diversity of plant species andexamines the ecological factors influencing vegetation patterns in the hills of MountParasnath.

items.title: Distribution of Arbuscular Mycorrhizae Fungi in the Rhizosphere of Dodonaea viscosa L. from a Semi-Arid Region
items.abstract: In natural habitats, arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) are essential for improving plant growth, nutrient uptake, and stress tolerance.The efficiency of various native fungal species across a variety of host plants in semi-arid climatic circumstances is still insufficiently known, despite having discovered that several studies demonstrate that AMF improves plant drought resistance.In the rhizosphere of Dodonaea viscosa L. in a semi-arid area, this study examined the variety of AMF, spore density, and root colonization.The conventional wet-sieving and decanting procedure was used to isolate AMF spores, and a standard root staining approach was used to measure root colonization.All study locations had consistently low electrical conductivity and low organic carbon content, according to soil physicochemical examination, indicating comparatively homogeneous soil fertility.Despite these circumstances, AMF root colonization was substantial in all studied locations (86.6-93.3%),indicating a robust and well-established mycorrhizal relationship with D. viscosa.Rhizophagus sp., Funneliformis mosseae, and Acaulospora scrobiculata were the most prevalent AMF species in the rhizosphere.These results show how native AMF populations can adapt to semi-arid settings, proving ecologically significant and indicates their potential for the development of bioinoculants aimed to increase crop resilience and production under water scarcity conditions.

items.title: Marine Pharmacognosy: A Revised Review on Bioactive Compounds from Marine Natural Sources
items.abstract: Marine pharmacognosy is the study of bioactive chemical constituents obtained from marine organisms and their application in drug discovery, pharmaceutical development, nutraceutical research, and biotechnology.The marine environment contains exceptionally diverse ecological niches, including coral reefs, intertidal zones, deep-sea sediments, hydrothermal vents, mangroves, and microbial symbioses.Organisms living in these competitive and physically demanding habitats produce secondary metabolites with unusual scaffolds, halogenation patterns, stereochemistry, and mechanisms of action.This revised review summarizes the historical development, major marine sources, chemical classes, clinically important drugs, pharmacological activities, extraction and isolation techniques, biotechnological advances, limitations, and future prospects of marine pharmacognosy.A narrative review method was adopted using standard review-writing principles and transparent literature selection.The evidence indicates that marine-derived or marine-inspired compounds have contributed to anticancer, analgesic, antiviral, antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and neuroprotective drug leads.Successful examples such as cytarabine, ziconotide, trabectedin, eribulin, and marine-toxin-based antibody-drug conjugates demonstrate the translational value of marine natural products.However, ecological sustainability, low natural abundance, structural complexity, dereplication, scalable production, toxicity, and regulatory barriers remain major challenges.Emerging strategies including genome mining, metagenomics, metabolomics, synthetic biology, aquaculture, microbial fermentation, green extraction, nanotechnology, and artificial intelligence can improve the discovery and development pipeline.Marine pharmacognosy therefore represents a scientifically significant and clinically promising field for future therapeutics, provided that exploration is coupled with ethical access, biodiversity conservation, and reproducible pharmaceutical evaluation.

items.title: From topology to biological meaning: why plant family classification matters beyond systematics
items.abstract: Plant family names are routinely used to structure comparative analyses, trait databases, floras, conservation assessments, and teaching. Yet, these names are not neutral labels: changing family boundaries changes the units across which biological patterns are compared, summarized, and interpreted. Modern phylogenetic inference resolves evolutionary relationships with increasing confidence, but it does not by itself determine which monophyletic groups should be recognized as families. We argue that this choice should be guided not only by monophyly, but also by diagnosability, biological interpretability, stability, and practical utility. Recent debates around large-scale consensus classifications show why these criteria must be explicit. Recognizing classification as shared scientific infrastructure means that family delimitation matters not only to systematists, but to all plant scientists who rely on taxonomic units to formulate questions and communicate results.

items.title: The conservation‐extraction nexus in ocean areas beyond National Jurisdiction: Tension or co‐constitution?
items.abstract: Recent years have seen a sharp uptick in efforts to expedite resource extraction in, and expand biodiversity conservation to, Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction (ABNJ), the ~70% of oceans outside state space. In this symposium piece, we explore the co‐constitution of the parallel acceleration of biodiversity conservation and economic exploitation that is unfolding in ways unique to the high seas, but consistent with global patterns wherein this coupling encloses space for capitalist value extraction. These coupled tendencies are part of expanded ocean regulation and, in ABNJ, they form part of state‐capital advancement into one of the remaining world frontiers. We explore this extraction‐conservation nexus in two contemporary ABNJ negotiations: 1) the Implementing Agreement under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction and 2) the International Seabed Authority's development of an exploitation regime for deep‐seabed mining in the Area. Our findings build on insights from agrarian political economy and political ecology that establish the co‐constitution – rather than incommensurability – of conservation and extractive activities in terrestrial spaces and draw out the arenas of this nexus in the ecologically complex, political‐economic grey zone that is the uninhabited (by humans), non‐state space of the planet. This work contributes to placing the high seas and the emergent blue economy within the critical scholarship that describes and explores the conservation‐extraction nexus and its consequences.

items.title: Securing LLM-Agent Long-Term Memory Against Poisoning: Non-Malleable, Origin-Bound Authority with Machine-Checked Guarantees
items.abstract: An agent based on a large language model (LLM) may store an untrusted document and use it weeks later to select a payment destination. Preventing this action requires evidence of authorization that remains valid when stored text changes. We study a policy that requires either endorsements (explicit approvals) from two separately administered sources or explicit user authorization. In an abstract memory model, we prove the policy is preserved under permitted transformations for stores of any size, assuming correct source and authority binding, protected records, and checks on every consequential action. We evaluate the executable monitor, which checks calls before execution, separately from the proof. In 1,152 controlled tool-use episodes, GPT-4o-mini executes attacker-selected actions in 61 of 72 undefended episodes and none of the 72 monitored episodes. Clean-task completion remains 24 of 24 when both endorsers are available. A separate 1,728-episode experiment tests recovery after denial. Returning to signed records instead of rereading a contaminated note raises attacked-task completion from 14/72 to 72/72 for GPT-4o-mini and from 22/72 to 43/72 for Gemini 2.5 Flash, without executing an attacker-selected action. Neither model completes transactions with fewer than two sources. Whole-action tests reject unauthorized combinations of individually approved fields. Extraction probes identify mistaken approvals, and fault analysis shows how shared failures can negate a second domain's benefit. Calibrations using original defense implementations reveal security and task-completion tradeoffs under different policies. These results support conditional enforcement and recovery in constructed workflows, but do not establish that endorsements will be available or correct in deployment.

items.title: CerviDBF-Net: Leveraging Spatial and Temporal Features for Accurate Cervical Cancer Diagnosis
items.abstract: Cervical cancer screening increasingly relies on automated image analysis to support colposcopic assessment and improve the consistency of clinical decision-making. This study proposes CerviDBF-Net, a novel deep learning framework for automated cervix-type classification from colposcopic images. The proposed architecture combines DenseNet121 for spatial feature extraction, a brain-inspired Liquid Neural Network (LNN) for contextual and temporal feature modelling, and a fully connected Softmax layer for final classification. To improve image quality and feature representation, the preprocessing pipeline incorporates bicubic interpolation, Bi-Histogram Equalization with Plateau Limit (BHEPL) for contrast enhancement, Kapur entropy-based thresholding, and the Roberts Cross operator for edge detection. The framework is evaluated on the Intel & MobileODT Cervical Cancer Screening dataset, which contains three cervix types (Type 1, Type 2, and Type 3) defined by the location and visibility of the transformation zone. CerviDBF-Net achieves an accuracy of 98.92%, sensitivity of 99.13%, specificity of 98.38%, precision of 98.69%, and an F1-score of 98.27%, demonstrating strong classification performance compared with the evaluated existing models. The proposed approach provides an automated baseline tool for cervix-type classification that may support triage in colposcopy-assisted screening by helping clinicians assess whether adequate visualization of the squamocolumnar junction has been achieved.

items.title: IntelliMirror: User Evaluation of an IoT Smart Mirror for Health Awareness and Mood Tracking
items.abstract: Objectives: Integrating Internet of Things (IoT) technologies in healthcare creates opportunities to develop intelligent, non-invasive, and user-friendly systems for continuous health monitoring. These advancements can simplify healthcare-related tasks, improve patient monitoring, and enable more personalized healthcare services. This study presents IntelliMirror, an IoT-based smart mirror for mood and health monitoring, which provides an interactive platform for accessing health-related information and mood-related conditions. Method: The experiment is conducted in three phases, comprising a baseline pre-survey, active IntelliMirror design and development, and interaction. Finally, the post -implementation evaluation. The experiment aims to incorporate user’s needs into the design to increase the system's trust and usability. Fifty participants completed the survey-based evaluation. The baseline survey identified user’s perceptions of the system before development, focusing on perceived health benefits, interest in mood monitoring, technological comfort, trust in data handling, and willingness to use the technology. Findings: The evaluation results show that 60% of participants perceived potential health benefits, 70% expressed interest in mood monitoring, and 62% were willing to use an intelligent mirror in a healthcare environment. The evaluation demonstrated generally favourable user perceptions, with positive responses exceeding 80% across the evaluated system features. The results indicate that IntelliMirror has promising potential as a user-centered IoT platform for integrating health and mood monitoring into an interactive smart-mirror environment. Novelty: This study explores user’s perception of an Intelligent Mirror before and after development. Based on pre-survey findings IntelliMirror was designed as a user centered IoT platform integrating healthcare and mood monitoring into a smart mirror environment. Post-development result indicates potential for smart technology adaptation in personalized healthcare. However, the research needs to include technical validation, clinical comparison, and long-term evaluation to ensure reliability and clinical applicability. items.title: EFFECT OF AN INTEGRATED ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT INTERVENTION ON MALARIA PARASITAEMIA PREVALENCE AMONG ADULTS IN THE ADA WEST AND NORTH TONGU DISTRICTS, GHANA: A CLUSTER-RANDOMISED CONTROLLED TRIAL WITH PRE- AND POST-INTERVENTION SURVEYS
items.abstract: Malaria control in Ghana's coastal savannah is constrained by outdoor biting and insecticide resistance, yet controlled evidence on environmental management is scarce. This study estimated the effect of an integrated environmental management (IEM) package on malaria parasitaemia among adults. A parallel two-arm cluster-randomised controlled trial was conducted from July to December 2024, with randomisation stratified by district: three sub-district clusters in Ada West District received the intervention, and four in North Tongu District served as controls. The six-month package combined habitat modification, habitat manipulation, targeted larviciding with Bacillus sphaericus, and community health education, while control clusters continued routine malaria control. Independent samples of 700 adults per arm were tested with an HRP2/pLDH rapid diagnostic test at baseline and end-line. The primary contrast was the difference-in-differences (DiD) in prevalence. Parasitaemia fell from 51.9% (95% CI 48.2–55.5) to 42.6% (39.0–46.3) in the intervention arm and rose from 62.3% (58.6–65.8) to 65.1% (61.5–68.6) in the control arm. The DiD was −12.1 percentage points (95% CI −19.4 to −4.9; p = 0.001), and the ratio of odds ratios was 0.61 (0.45–0.82). The effect remained statistically significant when variances were inflated for intra-cluster correlation coefficients below 0.009, but not above. The IEM package was associated with a substantial reduction in adult parasitaemia against a rising control-arm trend. Because only two district strata were randomised and the control district had recent flood exposure, the estimate is best regarded as an upper bound to be confirmed in trials with more clusters.

items.title: CONTEXT-AWARE DIGITAL TWIN ARCHITECTURES FOR REAL-TIME TRANSPORTATION AND WAREHOUSE OPTIMIZATION IN CLOUD-NATIVE SUPPLY CHAIN PLATFORMS
items.abstract: Context-aware digital twins are emerging as enabling architectures for coordinating responses to disruptions across inventory, warehouse, and transportation operations in cloud-based supply-chain platforms. They are important because they can be used to link continually evolving operational representations with optimization services that are able to react to traffic conditions, order arrivals, equipment status, changes in inventory, and facility constraints. This article reviews peer-reviewed journal literature on digital supply-chain twins, warehouse intelligence, dynamic vehicle routing, Internet of Things-enabled logistics, microservice architectures, and computational modelling. Some studies indicate that digital-twin approaches can improve visibility, scenario evaluation, and decision coordination in specific settings, but there is very little evidence of fully integrated real-time optimization of transportation and warehouse operations. Closed-loop orchestration has not been a primary focus of existing implementations, which tend to focus on warehouse simulation or monitoring, route adjustment, or resilience analysis across logistics domains. Other limitations include insufficient semantic interoperability, inadequate model fidelity, inconsistent latency assessment, deployment evidence, and consideration of cybersecurity and human intervention. The field therefore needs architectures that integrates event-driven context management, federated twin models, scalable optimization, auditable decision services, and explicit uncertainty handling.

items.title: Who Benefits from Immersion? Experimental dataset on immersive versus traditional task formats in organizational metaverse environments (N = 519)
items.abstract: Dataset supporting the article "Who Benefits from Immersion? Prior 3D Experience, User Experience, and Human-Centered Personalization in the Metaverse" (submitted to the International Journal of Human–Computer Interaction). Design. Mixed factorial 3 × 2 × 2 experiment with 519 participants. Between-subjects factors: experimental profile (virtual team leadership, digital marketing, innovation and entrepreneurship) and condition (traditional format vs. immersive multiuser metaverse environment). Within-subjects factor: measurement time (pre-test, post-test). Data were collected in the first semester of 2026 during undergraduate classes at a Brazilian university. Participation was voluntary, with informed consent; no personally identifying information was retained. Contents. One Excel workbook with two sheets: a long-format sheet (1,038 rows = 519 participants × 2 measurement times) and a wide-format sheet (519 rows, pre-test and post-test variables side by side). Variables include participant and cell identifiers, demographic and technological-background items, single items and composite scores for the metaverse-experience constructs (presence, experience fluidity/seamlessness, interoperability, real-time concurrency, economic flow), the technology-adoption constructs (intention to participate, perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, perceived value), baseline enjoyment, and procedural indicators. items.title: Role Of Social-Media In Social Inclusion And Self-Reliance Of Disabled People – A Sociological Study Based On Mentally And Physically Disabled Adults Of Kanpur Nagar
items.abstract: For centuries, disability has been misunderstood in multifarious cultures.People with disabilities often face stigma, exclusion, and stereotypes that prevent them from fully participating in society.In traditional communities, where physical ability is closely tied to social status, these challenges have been even greater.However, the rise of social media has started to change this narrative.Digital platforms like Instagram, YouTube etc., have given people with infirmities a space to tell their own stories, break down stereotypes, and build supportive communities.Instead of being defined by outdated cultural beliefs, individuals with disabilities can now control how they are seen by the world.Social media is not just a tool for entertainment-it is a powerful force that is shifting attitudes, raising awareness, and advocating for change.This research paper examines how social media may contribute to social inclusion and self-reliance among young adults with disabilities.It assumes a sample of 100 respondents from Kanpur Nagar comprising 50 mentally disabled adults and 50 physically disabled adults aged 18-25 years.The paper argues that accessible digital platforms can strengthen social participation, peer interaction, access to education, employment information, entrepreneurship, and civic engagement while also highlighting barriers such as affordability, digital literacy and accessibility.

items.title: Inclusive Culture in Higher Education: University Teacher and Student Perceptions
items.abstract: The objective of this study was to analyse the inclusive culture in the Faculty of Engineering of a private university in Lima. The research focused on teaching staff and student perceptions regarding the value of student diversity and the barriers that hinder academic performance. The approach was qualitative with a phenomenological design and included a sample of 10 university teachers and six students. The instruments used were a semi-structured interview guide for university teachers and a focus group guide for students. The data analysis procedure was conducted using ATLAS.ti (version 23). The results demonstrate a gap between the valuation of diversity and inclusive practice, whereby Universal Design for Learning (UDL) is not incorporated into session planning. Likewise, a lack of learning supports is recognised as a result of institutional deficiencies.

items.title: Corporate Governance Practices in Ai-Powered Technologies: A Perspective of Engineering Students
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become increasingly integrated into educational, professional, and technological environments, creating opportunities for innovation while raising concerns regarding transparency, accountability, ethical responsibility, privacy, and governance. Despite the growing use of AI-powered technologies among university students, limited research has examined how engineering students perceive corporate governance practices associated with these technologies. This study explored the perceptions of undergraduate engineering students regarding corporate governance in AI-powered technologies. A descriptive quantitative research design employing a cross-sectional survey approach was utilized. Data were collected from ninety-two (92) undergraduate engineering students at Cebu Institute of Technology–University (CIT-University) using a structured questionnaire. Frequency counts, percentages, weighted means, and ranking procedures were used to analyze the data. The findings revealed that respondents demonstrated positive awareness of corporate governance principles in AI systems, particularly regarding ethical responsibility, accountability, transparency, and data governance. The respondents also expressed a generally favorable level of trust in organizations utilizing AI-powered technologies, although concerns regarding privacy protection, data security, and responsible AI implementation remained evident. Among the governance dimensions examined, accountability received the highest rating, followed by ethical governance and transparency. Furthermore, the results showed that engineering students generally practiced responsible AI use, particularly in avoiding technologies that violate ethical and privacy standards. Large Language Models (LLMs), such as Gemini, ChatGPT, and Claude, were identified as the most commonly used AI-powered technologies among the respondents. The study concludes that engineering students recognize the importance of responsible AI governance and view accountability, ethical responsibility, and transparency as essential components of trustworthy AI systems. These findings may contribute to the development of governance policies, educational initiatives, and responsible AI practices within academic and technological environments.

items.title: Sürdürülebilir Tüketimde Yapay Zekâ
items.abstract: İklim krizi ve çevresel bozulmaların yaşandığı günümüzde, yeşil dönüşümün en güçlü teknolojik kaynağı olan yapay zekânın pazarlama süreçlerine ve tüketici davranışlarına etkileri önemli bir araştırma konusu olarak karşımıza çıkmaktadır. Bu doğrultuda kitap; işletmelerin sürdürülebilirlik vizyonları ile tüketicilerin çevre dostu kararları arasındaki köprüyü yapay zekâ teknolojileriyle yeniden inşa etmeyi amaçlamaktadır. Ayrıca, teknolojinin yıkıcı gücünü canlıların ortak geleceği için yapıcı bir güce dönüştürmenin yollarını aramaktadır. Kitabın birinci bölümünde; geleneksel pazarlama paradigmalarının evrimini ve yapay zekânın bu evrimdeki rolünü ele almaktadır. Sürdürülebilir pazarlama artık sadece bir imaj çalışması değil, yapay zekânın veri işleme gücüyle desteklenen stratejik bir zorunluluk olduğu vurgulanmaktadır. İkinci bölümünde; teoriyi pratiğe dökerek yapay zekânın doğrudan tüketiciyle temas ettiği dijital ekosistemleri analiz etmektedir. Tüketicilerin çevre bilincine sahip olmalarına rağmen satın alma anında bu bilinci eyleme dönüştürememeleri sorununa odaklanmaktadır. Son bölümde ise; davranışsal iktisat ile ileri teknolojinin kesişimi olan özgün bir kavramsal model inşa edilmektedir. İnsanları zorlamadan, seçenek özgürlüklerini kısıtlamadan çevre dostu tercihlere yönlendirmeyi amaçlayan "Dürtme Teorisi", yapay zekâ eliyle kişiselleştirilmiş bir boyuta taşınmaktadır. Yapay zekânın sadece endüstriyel bir verimlilik aracı olmadığını, aynı zamanda tüketim kültürünü kökten değiştirebilecek toplumsal bir dönüştürücü olduğunu kanıtlayan bu kitap; pazarlama yöneticileri, veri bilimciler, akademisyenler ve sürdürülebilirlik profesyonelleri için nesnel bir kaynak niteliğindedir.

items.title: Simulating Infant Senses with Age-Tuned Networks
items.abstract: What a newborn sees, hears and feels, and how this changes month by month, has been measured sense by sense, with different methods and in different units. We bring these measurements together for the first two years of life and ask whether small neural networks tuned to a given age can turn them into a quick, inspectable simulation of sensory perception. Each sense's immaturity is written as a fixed, age-indexed filter on the input, and a small prediction network learns behind it over the first year. The filters alone reproduce the order in which the senses mature, by construction. The networks add what filters cannot: in vision they extract far less than their input allows at early stages (at the newborn stage a toy's position cannot be read out, $R^2 = 0.00$, against 0.57 for a network trained directly on the same input), and a critical period and perceptual narrowing emerge without being built in; in hearing they track what their input allows. The same filters drive the Baby Senses Lab, a free website that shows a user's own images and sounds as a baby of a chosen age might sense them. It is a research and teaching tool, not a diagnostic test.

items.title: Spontaneous brain-wide rotational dynamics constrain cue-evoked behavior
items.abstract: Uncovering low-dimensional representations of brain-wide neural dynamics and their relationship to behavior remains a central challenge. Here, we show that spontaneous brain-wide rotational dynamics constrain cue-evoked behavior and learning. To systematically establish these findings, we developed a dimensionality-reduction technique called Rotational Component Analysis (RCA) that optimizes the detection of low-variance rotational modes even within individual trials. We applied RCA to motor-cortical spike-train data from monkeys and humans, mouse cortex-wide calcium imaging, and human functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and magnetoencephalography (MEG). In mice, a rotational mode identified from activity recorded at rest predicts cue-evoked behavior: the phase of rotation when a randomly timed cue arrives predicts whether the animal subsequently pulls the lever. We explain this surprisingly strong correlation using both a recurrent neural network (RNN) and a minimal two-dimensional model of response learning, in which the intrinsic rotational mode serves as a dynamical constraint on response and learning. We further identify double-rotation modes containing two centers of rotation that separate preparatory from task dynamics in both mouse and human data. Remarkably, corresponding modes also organize neural dynamics during a non-motor human task, and rotational irreversibility captures early psychosis even when principal component analysis shows no group difference. Our work establishes rotational dynamics as low-dimensional coordinates that constrain how ongoing brain states are converted into behavior. More broadly, RCA provides a versatile tool for detecting hidden nonreciprocal dynamics in biological and physical datasets.

items.title: Dynamical response of a protoplanetary disk to an FU Ori-type outburst
items.abstract: Episodic accretion events onto young stars can significantly change the global structure of their surrounding protoplanetary disks. Using radiation hydrodynamical simulations with the HURAKAN code, we study the response of the outer passive disk to a powerful FU Ori-type outburst. Disk heating initiates a factor-of-two increase in the vertical scale-height, which develops on a local keplerian timescale. This effectively launches an outward travelling wave with a bump whose radial position changes with time as $r_{b}\sim t^{2/3}$. After the outburst ends, new waves are launched as the disk structure re-equilibrates toward a quiescent state. The vertical expansion of the disk introduces significant time-variable extinction of the central source emission. Disks with inclinations in the range $40^{\circ}<i<60^{\circ}$ go from weakly ($A_{V}<1$) to a strongly embedded state ($A_{V}\sim10^2$), with the extinction decaying on a $\sim10^2$ yr timescale after the outburst. A fingerprint of the outburst-launched shadowing wave is a long-lived drop or a transient dip in the luminosity curve occurring several years after the outburst begins. This apparent luminosity variation is relatively large, up to $1^m-3^m$ in the V band, and is not related to the intrinsic accretion variability.

items.title: Negative partisanship drives anti-frontrunner volatility in election dynamics
items.abstract: Negative partisanship---where voter mobilization is driven primarily by aversion toward an opposing candidate rather than positive alignment---profoundly reshapes modern electoral dynamics. Here, we formulate a two-dimensional piecewise map to model campaign opinion dynamics, where voter abstention arises endogenously from a latent spectrum of voter activation barriers. We show that cross-candidate rejection sensitivity triggers a non-smooth collapse of abstention, dividing the phase space into an under-mobilized regime and a fully mobilized campaign regime. In symmetric elections with radicalized voter bases, spontaneous symmetry breaking via a pitchfork bifurcation gives rise to asymmetric polling attractors partitioned by mirror-symmetric basins of attraction, where early public perceptions---encoded in initial campaign conditions---act as a deterministic catalyst selecting candidate lead lock-in long before election day. For elevated cross-rejection, the symmetric equilibrium destabilizes via a period-doubling flip bifurcation, driving persistent anti-frontrunner polling swings. Rather than predicting static candidate hegemony, our model reveals that high negative partisanship turns elections into time-sensitive dynamical systems, where final election outcomes reflect discrete sampling snapshots of an oscillating campaign trajectory.

items.title: Companions of Hot Jupiters: two decades of radial velocity monitoring with CORALIE
items.abstract: Hot Jupiters are thought to form through multiple pathways, some of which can leave observable signatures in the architecture of their planetary systems. Massive outer companions, in particular, can provide important constraints on the dynamical histories of hot Jupiters. We aim to characterize the occurrence rate and orbital properties of additional giant companions in hot Jupiter systems, and to investigate whether these companions provide evidence for the role of dynamical interactions in shaping the hot Jupiter population. We perform a homogeneous long-term radial-velocity analysis of 147 WASP hot Jupiter systems observed with the CORALIE spectrograph between 2007 and 2025. We identify or refine 13 outer giant companions and use individual radial-velocity posteriors within a Bayesian occurrence-rate framework to measure the frequency of giant companions over orbital periods of 10--6250 days. The occurrence rate of additional giant companions increases strongly with orbital period, from {2}lt;0.01$ and 0.02 at 10--50 and 50--250 days to 0.05 and 0.17 at 250--1250 and 1250--6250 days, respectively, in agreement with the giant-planet occurrence of the general FGK population and with previous estimates of outer companions to hot Jupiters. Hot Jupiters with detected companions have longer orbital periods and higher eccentricities than those without. We also find that companion eccentricity decreases with hot Jupiter period, and that the companion-to-hot-Jupiter mass ratio increases with period ratio, both consistent with expectations from high-eccentricity migration (HEM). Our results support HEM as the mechanism shaping hot Jupiters with outer companions. Combining long-baseline radial velocities with future Gaia astrometry will further constrain companion masses, mutual inclinations, and dynamical histories.

items.title: Moser Regularization of the CR3BP for Symmetric Orbits: Bifurcation Networks of Lunar Orbits
items.abstract: We develop a computational framework based on Moser regularization for the analysis of symmetric periodic orbits in the spatial Circular Restricted Three-Body Problem (CR3BP). The formulation enables the numerical continuation of periodic orbit families through collision with either primary, together with the computation of Floquet multipliers and stability indices entirely in regularized coordinates. We further provide a characterization and numerical detection scheme for symmetric periodic collision orbits. We apply this framework to the Earth-Moon CR3BP and uncover bifurcation networks connecting several classical lunar periodic orbit families. Higher-period vertical bifurcations of the planar $L_1$ Lyapunov family generate spatial bridges reconnecting different regions of the same family across its collision with the Earth, while corresponding bifurcations of the $L_2$ Lyapunov family form bridges to planar families associated with retrograde comet orbits. Furthermore, period-multiplying bifurcations of Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit (NRHO) families produce a systematic network connecting to planar prograde and retrograde families. These bifurcation connections in the near-Moon dynamics retain the characteristic organization by covering multiplicities of the corresponding bifurcation network in the limiting Hill problem. Conley-Zehnder indices and related symplectic invariants complement the numerical continuation and provide a topological organization of the results.

items.title: Spectroscopic Studies of Meteors within the Skytinel Network
items.abstract: We present 12 low-resolution meteor spectra recorded at four stations of the Skytinel network in Poland, focusing on consistent reduction and comparison of Fe, Mg, and Na emission features. Spectra spanning approximately 350--850 nm were extracted, background-subtracted, and wavelength-calibrated using IRAF. Corrections accounted for the wavelength-dependent quantum efficiencies of Sony IMX249 and IMX273 detectors and atmospheric attenuation as a function of observing geometry. The corrected spectra were decomposed into Fe, Mg, and Na components using selected atomic transitions, temperature-dependent emissivities, and pseudo-Voigt line profiles. Integrated Fe~I-15, Mg~I-2, and Na~I-1 intensities were compared in a ternary diagram. Most spectra overlap with or lie near the normal-meteor distribution in reference samples, while some extend toward Fe-rich or Na-rich regions. The most Fe-dominated event assigns approximately 81\% of the summed emission to Fe~I-15. These ratios characterize relative emission, not elemental abundances or bulk composition. Combined with trajectory and photometric data, spectral classification may help constrain plausible material properties in dark-flight models and refine predicted meteorite search areas.

items.title: A Call to Action: Challenges and Future Directions for Sleep Health in Europe.
items.abstract: Sleep is fundamental to physical, cognitive, and emotional health and wellbeing. However, it is increasingly threatened by environmental, social, technological, and cultural pressures. To identify key priorities for improving sleep health across Europe, the European Sleep Research Society (ESRS)'s Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Committee (EDIC) and Early Career Network (ECN) convened a joint taskforce to review current challenges and develop strategic recommendations. Through a scoping review of the literature, iterative consensus meetings, and collaborative synthesis, the taskforce identified five overarching challenges: (1) environmental and climate-related threats to sleep; (2) inequitable access to sleep medicine and care; (3) the rapid expansion and potential of digital health technologies; (4) widespread sleep misinformation and misconceptions surrounding sleep health; and (5) societal change, constant technological connectivity, and the emergence of a 24/7 culture. These interconnected challenges disproportionately affect vulnerable groups and risk exacerbating existing health inequalities. In response, we propose a coordinated set of recommendations structured according to the PESTEL framework (Political, Economic, Sociological, Technological, Environmental and Legal). Collectively, these recommendations advocate for integrated and equity-focused approaches to strengthen the structural and organisational conditions that support sleep health, improve sleep health literacy, regulate emerging technologies, and ensure that healthy sleep becomes an achievable public health priority across Europe.

items.title: Neuro-Immune Interactions in the Tumour Microenvironment: Implications for Cancer Progression and Treatment.
items.abstract: The nervous and immune systems, once viewed as distinct biological networks, are now understood to be closely linked in regulating cancer development, progression, and responses to therapy. Neural structures infiltrate the tumour microenvironment and communicate with immune cells, influencing key processes such as tumour growth, invasion, and metastatic spread. Through neurotransmitters, neuropeptides, and continuous signalling between peripheral tissues and the brain, nerves affect immune cell recruitment, activity, and overall immune balance. Factors including psychological stress, circadian rhythm disturbances, and gut-brain communication further shape antitumour immune responses, highlighting the complexity of these interactions. Research suggests that neuronal signalling not only contributes to cancer-associated symptoms, such as pain, but also affects the efficacy of chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and immunotherapy. Neural biomarkers may provide prognostic value, while interventions targeting neural pathways could strengthen anticancer immunity. Nevertheless, major challenges remain, including cellular heterogeneity, dynamic spatial and temporal interactions, and the limitations of existing experimental models. Continued progress in molecular techniques, bioinformatics, and cross-disciplinary research will be crucial for clarifying these mechanisms. Investigating the neuro-immune-cancer interface offers significant potential for developing innovative treatment approaches that combine neuroscience, immunology, and oncology to enhance patient survival and quality of life.

items.title: Zona incerta circuits in cognition and the regulation of sleep and wakefulness: potential relevance to Alzheimer's disease.
items.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by progressive cognitive decline and prominent disturbances in sleep and wakefulness, reflecting dysfunction across distributed neural networks. The zona incerta (ZI) is a highly heterogeneous subthalamic structure whose organization is defined by spatial location, molecular identity, neurochemical phenotype, and circuit connectivity. Recent studies demonstrate that distinct ZI cell populations and projections contribute to memory processing, novelty seeking, cortical plasticity, sleep promotion, rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, transitions to wakefulness, and sleep homeostasis. Together, these findings suggest that the ZI is better viewed as a state-dependent subcortical regulatory platform than as a unitary cognitive or sleep center. Emerging pathological evidence further raises the possibility that the ZI may be relevant to neurodegeneration. Amyloid-β deposition has been reported in the ZI of 5xFAD transgenic mice, while experimental tau propagation, human tauopathies other than AD, and studies of other neurodegenerative disorders indicate potential cellular and circuit vulnerability. However, direct evidence from human AD remains lacking, and no study has established a causal pathway from AD pathology to selective ZI dysfunction and subsequent cognitive or sleep impairment. We therefore propose two testable models in which the ZI contributes to AD phenotypes either as a shared circuit node or through parallel, selectively vulnerable functional modules.

items.title: CAG repeat length shapes bidirectional functional connectome alterations in spinocerebellar ataxia type 3: a multimodal MRI study.
items.abstract: The ATXN3 gene is the primary driver of brain damage in spinocerebellar ataxia type 3 (SCA3). We aimed to elucidate the patterns of connectome alterations shaped by cytosine-adenine-guanine (CAG) repeat length in SCA3. Eighty-nine genetically confirmed patients with SCA3 and 89 age-, sex-, education-matched healthy controls underwent multimodal MRI and comprehensive clinical assessments. Connectome-based predictive modeling (CPM) was used to identify functional connectivity patterns associated with CAG repeat length. Structural brain damage was assessed using voxel-based morphometry. Mediation analysis was performed to examine the role of structural impairment in connectivity changes. CPM identified a positive and a negative network, whose connectivity strength increased or decreased with CAG repeat length. The positive network (r = 0.397, P < 0.001) was mainly localized within the cerebello-motor circuit and was positively associated with ataxia severity and functional disability. The negative network (r = 0.243, P = 0.022) was distributed across large-scale networks, with selective vulnerability of interhemispheric connectivity, and was associated with motor dysfunction. Besides the canonical motor pathways, limbic-related connectivity was related to motor impairment. Structural analyses revealed widespread gray matter atrophy centered on the cerebellum. Cerebellar atrophy statistically mediated the association between CAG repeat length and connectivity decreases. CAG repeat length is associated with a bidirectional connectopathy in SCA3. Cerebellar atrophy may mediate the connectivity decreases. Future longitudinal studies are required to examine the underlying causal pathway.

items.title: Comparison of Lateral Decubitus versus Prone Lateral Lumbar Interbody Fusion Using Impact Scores: A Method to Quantify Intraoperative Supply Cost and Variability in Surgery.
items.abstract: Surgical value metrics report intraoperative supply costs as aggregate institutional dollars, which do not identify which supply categories drive cost. To introduce the Impact Score, each supply category's percentage share of total intraoperative supply cost, as a descriptive framework and, using lateral decubitus (LD-LIF) versus prone lateral (PL-LIF) lateral lumbar interbody fusion as a proof of concept, to determine whether impact scores differ by supply category and align with median-cost rankings, whether exploratory outcome-based value metrics differ between approaches, and whether meaningful inter-surgeon variability exists. Retrospective single-center cohort study at a tertiary center. Seventy-eight single-level L4-5 lateral lumbar interbody fusion cases performed from 2021 to 2026 (32 LD-LIF, 46 PL-LIF). Category-level impact score (percentage of total intraoperative supply cost), supply and total intraoperative cost, exploratory value metrics based on the Oswestry Disability Index and PROMIS-10-derived quality-adjusted life years (including the operative value index and unit price per outcome), and 90-day readmission. Itemized intraoperative supply records were mapped to 33 standardized categories, and each category's impact score was computed as its percentage of total intraoperative supply cost. Time-driven activity-based costing provided staff costs. Category-level impact scores and costs were compared with unadjusted Wilcoxon rank-sum tests. Impact-score and median-cost rankings were broadly concordant. LD-LIF showed higher impact for interbody, screw, biologic, and retractor/dilator, and PL-LIF for neuromonitoring and positioning (all p < 0.01). Navigation and rod did not differ. Total intraoperative cost did not differ between approaches (PL-LIF $17,206 vs LD-LIF $16,404, p = 0.462), nor did staff cost (p = 0.607), and exploratory value metrics did not establish a cost-effectiveness difference, whereas the impact score localized the between-approach difference to supply composition. Biologic impact varied most, with a more than two-fold range among the three surgeons (median approximately 5% to 19%) and higher biologic impact in LD-LIF within individual surgeons. The impact score describes how intraoperative supply costs are distributed across categories. In this single-center, three-surgeon cohort, it identified a potentially modifiable cost driver that neither total cost nor exploratory value metrics revealed. Its use for cross-institutional benchmarking will require a multicenter study of how impact scores vary between institutions with differing vendor pricing and contracting. Because it reflects only the intraoperative phase, it complements, rather than replaces, episode-of-care and outcome-based value assessment. Level III, retrospective comparative study.

items.title: Twenty-five years of the NIDA clinical trials network and the future of addiction research.
items.abstract: The National Institute on Drug Abuse Clinical Trials Network (CTN) was established in 1999 to bridge the persistent divide between addiction research and clinical practice through partnerships between researchers and community treatment providers. This editorial examines the evolution of the CTN over its first 25 years and considers priorities for its future. Drawing on the historical development of the Network and articles in this 25-year special collection, we examine changes in the populations and settings represented in CTN research, the incorporation of implementation science, the evolution of community partnerships, the scientific value of accumulated CTN data and experience, and emerging clinical and methodological priorities. Over 25 years, the CTN has developed from a network focused principally on clinically relevant effectiveness trials into a broader national infrastructure for clinical trials and translational addiction research. Its research has expanded beyond specialty addiction treatment programs into primary care, emergency departments, hospitals, community health centers, pharmacies, and other settings in which people with substance use disorders receive care. The Network has also increasingly addressed populations historically underrepresented in addiction research, incorporated implementation questions into clinical research, strengthened community engagement, and used accumulated trial data and emerging analytic methods to generate new scientific knowledge. These developments demonstrate that the value of a clinical research network extends beyond individual trial outcomes. Clinical trials should remain at the core of the CTN's scientific mission. However, trial designs and complementary research methods should be determined by the scientific questions being addressed. The CTN's future impact will depend on its ability to conduct rigorous multisite trials while incorporating implementation, representation, community partnership, and accumulated data and responding rapidly to changes in the drug supply and addiction care environment. These capabilities can help the Network generate evidence that is rigorous, relevant, timely, and more likely to improve addiction care.

items.title: Altered intrinsic neural timescales in cocaine use disorder.
items.abstract: Cocaine use disorder (CUD) is a major public health challenge, but its neurodynamic and molecular mechanisms remain unclear despite evidence of structural and functional abnormalities. This study mapped whole-brain intrinsic neural timescales (INTs), reflecting temporal integration of neural activity, using resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging in 44 CUD patients and 44 healthy controls. In the primary analysis with global signal regression (GSR), CUD showed increased network-level INTs in the visual, somatomotor, dorsal attention, frontoparietal control, and default mode networks compared with HC. In the sensitivity analysis without GSR, the visual and somatomotor network differences remained significant. Within the CUD group, regional and network-level INT variation was associated with individual differences in flanker-task performance, despite the absence of significant between-group differences in behavioral performance. Notably, the spatial distribution of INT differences was associated with normative maps of gamma-aminobutyric acid type A receptors and the noradrenaline transporter. Atlas-based models showed modest discrimination and limited validation, while outcome-informed cluster-based models yielded higher but exploratory estimates. Importantly, classification performance in a mixed-source evaluation sample was close to chance, indicating limited generalizability. Together, these findings reveal widespread alterations in intrinsic neural timescales in CUD and highlight the relevance of spatiotemporal brain organization to addiction.

items.title: Should I "stay" or should I "go"? Influence of an anticipated stop on cortical correlates of overground walking.
items.abstract: Real-world walking frequently requires pedestrians to maintain proactive inhibition to safely navigate unpredictable environments. While cortical modulations occurring during locomotion under environmental uncertainty are well-established, the specific proactive mechanisms underlying this state of inhibitory anticipation remain unexplored. This study aimed to investigate the behavioral and cortical shifts associated with anticipating a stop during overground walking. Fourteen healthy young adults performed fluent and cautious walking tasks with an expected stop. Cortical activity and trunk acceleration were recorded using a 32-channel mobile electroencephalography and an integrated accelerometer. Step-1 latency and step-interval variability were calculated via heel strike detection. Gait-phase-related power modulations were computed, and spectral principal component analysis was applied to attenuate artifacts. The results revealed that cautious walking significantly increased step-interval variability, whereas step-1 latency remained unaffected. At the cortical level, left frontotemporal areas exhibited an attenuated and delayed theta desynchronization during the swing phase. Furthermore, centroparietal regions demonstrated an altered temporal profile of alpha and beta synchronization, characterized by enhanced late-stance synchronization and reduced swing-phase synchronization. The present findings suggest that anticipating a potential stop may alter the rhythmic consistency of gait and reorganize phase-specific cortical dynamics. Being prepared to stop may shift the neural control of automated locomotion toward active monitoring, highlighting the relevance of proactive inhibition during everyday mobility.

items.title: Impact of previous acute and chronic stress on negative glucocorticoid feedback in laboratory animal: theoretical background and methodological concerns.
items.abstract: Chronic stress or acute severe stressors have been extensively used as putative animal models of psychiatric diseases, particularly depression and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), respectively. The hypothalamus-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis not only represents a prototypical stress response system, but also mediates or modulates a wide range of the behavioral and physiological consequences of stress exposure. Therefore, particular attention has been paid to the parallelisms between stress-induced alterations of the HPA axis in animal models and the alterations observed in PTSD and depression. The canonical views suggest that PTSD patients are characterized by hypocortisolemia and an enhanced negative glucocorticoid feedback (nGF), whereas major depression patients typically show hypercortisolemia and impaired nGF. Here, we critically review studies on the effects of different stress models on nGF, distinguishing between nGF under resting and stress conditions. The evidence that chronic stress exposure is associated with impaired nGF is weak, except for HPA activity under resting conditions. The evidence that a single exposure to severe stressors leads to enhanced nGF under stress conditions is controversial, and the studies supporting this present important limitations. In general, the major limitations of nGF studies are the lack of plasma ACTH data, the assessment of nGF using exposure to a stressor with which animals have prior experience, and the predominant use of dexamethasone instead of natural glucocorticoids. At the dexamethasone doses typically used, this drug acts mainly at the anterior pituitary rather than at the brain level, making it difficult to relate altered nGF with changes in brain corticosteroid receptors.

items.title: Magnetic resonance imaging vs computed tomography for baseline imaging evaluation in acute basilar artery occlusion.
items.abstract: The optimal imaging modality, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT), for identifying good treatment candidates among patients with acute basilar-artery occlusion (BAO) remains unclear. This was a post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION trial. Patients were categorized into MRI or CT groups according to the baseline imaging modality. The primary outcome was mRS 0-3 at 90 days. The secondary outcomes included mRS score shift on an ordinal scale, early neurological deterioration, time from stroke onset to arterial puncture, and time from onset to randomization. The safety outcome was mortality within 90 days. Clinical outcomes and workflow times were compared between the two groups. Among 340 patients (CT: n = 277; MRI: n = 63), baseline imaging was not significantly associated with 90-day mRS 0-3 in the overall cohort (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.50-1.95; P = 0.976). It remained highly consistent across both the endovascular treatment and best medical management subgroups. Baseline MRI assessment was not associated with significant workflow delays compared with CT, including time from stroke onset to randomization (mean difference [MD] 5.23 min; P = 0.843) and time to puncture (MD 13.16 min; P = 0.701). Furthermore, the association between imaging modality and outcomes was consistent across different time windows. In patients with acute BAO, we did not observe evidence supporting the preferential use of MRI over CT as the primary imaging strategy for patient selection. Conventional imaging appears sufficient as a first-line tool for selecting patients in clinical practice.

items.title: Harnessing the ion transportome to treat cancer.
items.abstract: Despite significant advances in early detection and therapeutic opportunities, cancer remains a critical global health challenge. The greatest barrier to reducing cancer-associated mortality is the persistent problem of therapeutic resistance and metastasis. Standard treatment approaches, including surgery combined with chemotherapy and radiation, are effective for many patients with localised disease. However, a substantial proportion of patients will experience recurrence and therapy resistance, leading to treatment failure and poor outcomes. This adverse prognosis for patients highlights the critical need to identify new therapeutic targets capable of improving long-term survival. The ion transportome comprises ion channels, solute transporters and pumps that regulate controlled movement of sodium (Na+), potassium (K+), calcium (Ca2+), chloride (Cl-) and hydrogen (H+) across cell membranes. Ion transport is central to many cellular processes, including cell growth, volume regulation, proliferation and migration. In many solid tumours, the finely tuned ionic balance becomes dysregulated, with aberrant expression or activity of membrane transport proteins being closely linked to many of the hallmarks of cancer. Ion channel modulation using pharmacological agents designed to treat channelopathies has demonstrated promise in suppressing cancer progression in preclinical models. Thus, targeting ion-driven vulnerabilities within solid tumours may complement existing therapies to overcome resistance and improve patient outcomes. The dynamic nature of ion transport mechanisms means that addressing critical research questions regarding their suitability as pharmacological targets is challenging, highlighting the need to develop innovative approaches to study these processes in oncology.

items.title: Lumbar Facet Joint Morphology and Degenerative Lumbar Spondylolisthesis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Study DesignSystematic review and meta-analysis.ObjectivesTo evaluate the associations between lumbar facet orientation, facet tropism, and degenerative lumbar spondylolisthesis (DLS), while assessing sex-specific differences in facet morphology.MethodsA PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261417450). PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Web of Science were searched through June 2026. Studies evaluating lumbar facet morphology in adults with DLS were included. Random-effects meta-analyses using restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp adjustment were performed. Risk of bias and evidence certainty were assessed.ResultsThirty-nine studies met the inclusion criteria. Sixteen studies (3,321 participants) were included in the facet orientation meta-analysis. Patients with DLS demonstrated more sagittally oriented facet joints than controls (SMD 1.30, 95% CI 0.78-1.82; p < 0.0001; I2 = 97.2%). Nine studies (1,913 participants) showed greater continuous facet tropism in DLS patients (MD 2.72°, 95% CI 2.07°-3.38°; p < 0.0001; I2 = 47.2%). Binary facet tropism was not statistically significant (OR 2.20, 95% CI 0.85-5.66; p = 0.0817). Sex-specific, severity, and instability data were insufficient for quantitative synthesis.ConclusionDLS is associated with more sagittally oriented facet joints and greater continuous facet tropism than controls. Limited sex-specific data and heterogeneity highlight the need for standardized measurement techniques and prospective longitudinal studies to clarify causality and sex-related effects.

items.title: Molecular Signatures of HIV-Induced Neuroinflammation and Neurodegeneration in Human Cerebral Organoids: Identification of Therapeutic Targets for NeuroHIV.
items.abstract: HIV-associated neurological complications remain a major concern in people living with HIV (PWH), even under effective viral suppression with combination antiretroviral therapy (cART), underscoring unresolved mechanisms driving HIV-related neurodegeneration. To address this gap, we used HIV-1-infected human cerebral organoids (hCOs) containing microglia as a physiologically relevant three-dimensional model of the central nervous system (CNS) and validated key findings in the brain region of simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV)-infected, cART-treated rhesus macaque model. Integrated single-nucleus RNA sequencing with ATAC-seq (multi-omics), identifies cell-type-specific alterations in dual innate immune-driven inflammatory signaling pathways across neural and glial populations in hCOs. Microglia were preferentially infected and activated, initiating IL-17A-mediated cascades involving IFN-γ/STAT1, CEBPB, and NF-κB signaling. These pathways converged with cGAS-STING and Notch-NEURL1 signaling, both associated with neuroinflammation and synaptic dysfunction. cART suppressed viral replication, reduced IL-17A-mediated neuroinflammation, improved mitochondrial function, and restored synaptic gene expression. Collectively, these findings identify dysregulation of IL-17A, STAT1, CEBPB, and cGAS-STING signaling as key molecular drivers of HIV-associated neuroinflammation. They also establish a potential mechanistic link between IL-17A signaling and microglial remodeling, providing a translational framework for the development of CNS-targeted therapies in PWH.

items.title: Putative predictive power of baseline cerebrospinal fluid dipeptidyl peptidase-4 on the conversion to secondary progressive multiple sclerosis.
items.abstract: Dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP4) has many inflammation-related functions such as T cell activation, and complement activation and is recognized as a putative pathogenic factor in multiple sclerosis (MS). Our aim was to analyze whether baseline cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) levels of DPP4 and DPP4-induced complement breakdown byproducts might predict MS progression. Levels of DPP4, factor C3a (C3a), factor C4a (C4a), factor Ba (Ba) and soluble membrane attack complex (sMAC) were measured by ELISA in CSF obtained during the first clinical attack of 80 MS patients. The association between CSF markers and disability progression was assessed by regression analyses. Fourteen of 80 patients had converted to secondary progressive MS (SPMS) in a follow-up period of 9.4 ± 5.1 years. As compared to patients preserving relapsing-remitting MS (RRMS) status, SPMS-convertors showed significantly higher baseline CSF DPP4 (p = 0.035) and Ba (p = 0.013) levels. Receiver operating characteristic analysis indicated baseline CSF DPP4 level to be associated with increased risk of SPMS conversion (p = 0.026, AUC = 0.691, 95% CI = 0.6-0.8). Cox regression analysis showed that after adjustment for onset age and duration of disease, DPP4 levels were associated with increased risk for conversion to SPMS (p = 0.040), and baseline CSF Ba levels were associated with time to disability progression (EDSS 3.0) (p = 0.031). Baseline CSF DPP4 levels may predict the emergence of SPMS at the early stage of disease, whereas baseline Ba levels appear to be associated with earlier progression of MS.

items.title: Taxus wallichiana zucc. (Himalayan yew): phytochemistry, therapeutic potential, biotechnology, and conservation perspectives.
items.abstract: Taxus wallichiana Zucc. (Himalayan yew) is an endangered conifer of the Indian Himalayan Region and adjoining countries, recognised as a natural source of paclitaxel (Taxol ® ) and its precursor 10-deacetylbaccatin III (10-DAB). This review comprehensively synthesises current knowledge of its phytochemistry, pharmacological potential, biotechnology, and conservation, highlighting recent advances, research gaps, and future directions. Phytochemical investigations have identified diverse bioactive compounds, including taxoids (paclitaxel, cephalomannine, and wallitaxanes), flavonoids, lignans, and phenolic acids, contributing to its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and anticancer properties. Advances in tissue culture, metabolic engineering, and endophytic fungal research offer promising alternatives for taxoid production, potentially reducing destructive bark harvesting. Despite its medicinal and pharmaceutical significance, Taxus wallichiana faces serious threats from overexploitation, poor regeneration, habitat degradation, and grazing pressure. Conservation approaches include ex situ propagation, genetic diversity assessment, habitat restoration, and sustainable utilisation of renewable foliage and endophyte-derived metabolites. By integrating ethnomedicinal knowledge, phytochemical diversity, pharmacological applications, biotechnological innovations, and conservation priorities, this review provides a multidisciplinary perspective on the species' scientific and ecological importance. Future research should strengthen sustainable production systems, clarify therapeutic potential of its bioactive compounds, and integrate traditional ecological knowledge with modern biotechnology and conservation biology to support the long-term survival and sustainable utilisation of this valuable Himalayan medicinal conifer.

items.title: Covariation of DOM molecular characteristics and bacterial carbon metabolism potential along a reservoir-agricultural river nutrient gradient.
items.abstract: Agricultural nutrient loading is associated with variation in dissolved organic matter (DOM) composition and microbial communities across reservoir-agricultural river continuums, yet the covariation among nutrient conditions, DOM molecular heterogeneity, and bacterial metabolic potential remains insufficiently understood. This study integrated optical spectroscopy, ultrahigh-resolution mass spectrometry, nitrate dual-isotope tracing, end-member mixing analysis (EMMA), 16S rRNA sequencing, and metagenomic functional profiling to characterize DOM sources and composition and their associations with bacterial communities in a typical reservoir-agricultural river continuum. Our results showed that nitrogen and phosphorus enrichment within agricultural river reaches systematically rearranges DOM source apportionment, with relative abundance of humic-like components (C1, C3) rising alongside elevated abundances of heteroatomic molecular formulas (CHOS, CHONS) relative to oligotrophic reservoirs. Nutrient loading reshaped DOM via exogenous input of heteroatom-rich anthropogenic organics and boosted in-situ microbial humification. EMMA modeling further indicated that anthropogenic sources contributed 37.9% to riverine DOM. Principal coordinates analysis showed that reservoir-river community differentiation coincided with nutrient and fluorescent DOM gradients. Reservoir samples were dominated by Acinetobacter, Exiguobacterium, and Clade_III and showed higher relative abundances of several genes associated with carbohydrate and aromatic compound degradation. In contrast, river communities featured humic-adapted genera (Mycobacterium, hgcl_clade, Limnohabitans, and unclassified_Sporichthyaceae) and showed higher relative abundances of genes associated with lipid utilization and terrestrial-polymer degradation. This study highlighted coordinated spatial variation in nutrient conditions, DOM characteristics, bacterial community composition, and genomic carbon metabolism potential across the reservoir-agricultural river continuum, supplying theoretical guidance for pollution control and carbon cycling regulation in anthropogenic-disturbed inland water catchments.

items.title: Caustic ingestion in children: A prospective analysis of poor outcome key predictors useful for clinical management optimization.
items.abstract: Endoscopic examination is the main diagnostic test to evaluate the extent and severity of any mucosal lesions after caustic ingestion, in order to target the most appropriate treatment and follow-up. Our main aim was to evaluate clinical, biochemical, and instrumental parameters in order to identify possible key predictors of poor outcome and therefore identify possible subgroups of asymptomatic or paucisymptomatic children who may benefit from the endoscopic examination. All children admitted for caustic ingestion were prospectively enrolled. Poor outcome was defined as the presence of mucosal lesions with severe/uncertain prognosis: Zargar score 2b to 4 or severe gastric/duodenal lesions. Two hundred and eighty-three children were enrolled. No asymptomatic patient showed poor outcome (p < 0.01). Children showing hematemesis, drooling, vomiting, oropharyngeal or labial lesions showed a higher risk of developing severe mucosal lesions (p < 0.01). The ingestion of caustic substances inappropriately stored in plastic glasses or bottles was found to be a risk factor for unfavorable outcome (p < 0.01). Asymptomatic children should not undergo endoscopic examination since severe mucosal lesions are associated with the development of at least one sign or symptom. However, this recommendation may not apply to children under 18 months of age or those with delayed psychomotor development or neuropsychiatric pathologies, likely because they are unable to reliably report symptoms.

items.title: The gender gap in math anxiety (and in the link between math anxiety and math achievement) is not so salient when other anxieties are controlled for.
items.abstract: Math anxiety (MA) is considered to affect math achievement and the choice of math-related educational paths, thus contributing to the gender gap in STEM careers. However, despite decades of research, the mechanisms underlying the relationships between gender, MA, and math achievement remain largely unclear. One of the reasons is that different types of anxiety and math achievement levels are rarely controlled for. We tested the associations between gender, MA, spatial anxiety, test anxiety, neuroticism, and math achievement in a sample of 269 adults. We replicated previous findings that spatial anxiety in areas of navigation and mental manipulation, but not imagery, mediates the relationship between gender and MA. Importantly, in light of previous contradictory findings, we found that math achievement significantly mediated this relationship. Crucially, we found that gender, spatial anxiety, test anxiety, neuroticism, and math achievement together accounted for 66% of the variance in MA, with gender uniquely accounting for only 5%. The commonly reported gender gap in MA is less pronounced when other anxieties are controlled for, especially given that we did not observe gender differences in the strength of the relationship between MA and math achievement.

items.title: Pain Management Strategies for Older Adults in Palliative Care: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: With the aging population, the demand for palliative care is expected to increase. Pain management is a critical component of palliative care with unique considerations for older patients. The aim of this scoping review was to map the nature and extent of the evidence on pain management strategies in this population. We searched databases for peer-reviewed studies and grey literature on pain management in older adults receiving palliative care. Strategies were classified as opioid analgesics, non-opioid medications, procedural, non-pharmacological, educational, and multifaceted interventions. Frequencies and proportions were used to describe the strategies, reported improvements, and levels of evidence. We included 117 studies. Most focused on cancer populations (82/117, 71%), and the majority of participants (98/114, 86%) were aged 65-74 years on average. Overall, 68% of the studies yielded moderate to low level of evidence. Opioids and multifaceted interventions were the most frequently evaluated strategies, each examined in 32% (37/117) of studies. Across both high- and moderate/low-evidence studies, pain reduction was most consistently reported for procedural interventions (3/3, 100%; 3/3, 100%), opioids (3/5, 60%; 25/32, 78%), and multifaceted interventions (4/9, 44%; 20/23, 87%). Favourable findings were most often reported for combinations of opioids, opioids for breakthrough pain, nerve blocks or local anesthesia, cannabis, music or massage therapy, exercise, and biopsychosocial or care organization interventions. This review mapped pain management strategies for older adults in palliative care, identified key evidence gaps, particularly among oldest-old individuals and those with non-cancer conditions, and highlighted the need for stronger research.

items.title: Differing subjective and psychophysiological response patterns to a music-based auditory intervention for anxiety.
items.abstract: Anxiety comprises partially dissociable cognitive and somatic components, yet it remains unclear whether brief interventions modulate these systems in parallel. This randomized controlled trial examined subjective and psychophysiological responses to a brief music-based auditory intervention relative to an active auditory control (pink noise) in undergraduate students reporting recent generalized anxiety symptoms. Participants (N = 83) were randomized to the auditory intervention or pink noise. Cognitive and somatic anxiety were assessed before and after the intervention, while salivary cortisol, heart rate variability (HRV), and electroencephalography (EEG) indexed endocrine, autonomic, and neural processes. Cortisol showed a significant Condition × Time interaction, with larger reductions following the auditory intervention. Midline theta power also exhibited a significant Condition × Time interaction, reflecting opposing patterns of change across conditions, although within-condition changes were only significant in the pink noise condition. Cognitive anxiety, somatic anxiety, affective arousal, frontal alpha lateralization, and HRV did not show significant differential baseline-to-post change. During listening, HRV increased across conditions, but the Condition × Epoch interaction observed in the primary growth model was not retained when participant-specific slopes were included. Together, these findings indicate differing patterns of response across levels of analysis, with broad reductions in self-reported anxiety and arousal across both auditory conditions and greater condition sensitivity in the primary cortisol and midline-theta analyses. Because the cortisol and theta interactions were not retained in models including all physiologically valid observations, these condition-dependent findings should be interpreted cautiously.
