items.title: Noncausal joint-action scenes facilitate Mandarin-speaking preschoolers' interpretation of intransitive verbs with conjoined subjects.
items.abstract: Children learn novel verb meanings by integrating sentence-level cues with information from the surrounding event. Although sentence frames provide information about verb transitivity, success with intransitive frames varies across languages and tasks. In Mandarin, preschoolers have been reported to struggle with conjoined-subject intransitive sentences, raising the question of whether this difficulty reflects a limitation in syntactic bootstrapping or partly stems from how children construe the comparison scenes. In a forced-choice pointing task, Mandarin-speaking 3-, 4-, and 5-year-olds heard transitive or conjoined-subject intransitive sentences containing novel verbs and chose between a causal scene and a noncausal scene. Critically, the noncausal scene was either a parallel-action scene or a joint-action scene. In the joint-action scene, the two participants acted together in physical contact but without a causal asymmetry. Children at all ages reliably matched transitive sentences to causal scenes. For intransitives, 3-year-olds performed at chance in both scene conditions, 4-year-olds succeeded only with joint-action scenes, and 5-year-olds succeeded in both. Thus, performance with intransitives improved with age and was facilitated when the noncausal alternative was easier to construe as a single noncausal event. These findings suggest that previously reported failures with Mandarin conjoined-subject intransitives cannot be attributed solely to insensitivity to argument structure, but also depend on how candidate events are visually and conceptually represented. More broadly, the results are consistent with a multiple-factor view of verb learning, in which syntactic cues interact with semantic, and event-based information.

items.title: Environmental Exposures, Chronic Sinusitis, and Olfaction in People With Cystic Fibrosis.
items.abstract: Environmental air pollutants may contribute to chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS), but their relationship with upper airway disease in people with cystic fibrosis (CF) remains poorly understood. This study evaluated associations between long-term ambient air pollutant exposure and CRS severity and olfactory dysfunction in adults with CF and CRS. 80 adults with CF and comorbid CRS were prospectively enrolled from 2019 to 2023 at multiple U.S. academic rhinology centers. Long-term exposure to PM2.5, PM10, CO, SO2, NO2, and ozone was estimated using the nearest U.S. Environmental Protection Agency monitor linked to each participant's residential ZIP code, with 3-year mean exposure calculated before enrollment. CRS severity and olfaction were assessed using Lund-Kennedy endoscopy scores, Lund-Mackay CT scores, SNOT-22, Questionnaire of Olfactory Disorders-Negative Statements, and 40-item Smell Identification Test. Analyses used Spearman correlations and nonparametric group comparisons. Higher ozone exposure was associated with worse total SNOT-22 scores (Rs = 0.34 p = 0.002), including ear/facial, psychological, and sleep dysfunction domains, as well as worse olfactory-specific outcomes, including higher QOD-NS scores (Rs = 0.30, p = 0.007) and lower Smell Identification Test scores (Rs = -0.30, p = 0.018). Other pollutants did not show significant associations with CRS or olfactory outcomes. In adults with CF and CRS, higher long-term ambient ozone exposure was associated with greater sinonasal symptom burden and worse olfactory function. These findings suggest that ozone may be an environmental contributor to upper airway disease severity in this population and support further study in larger, adjusted analyses. Increased ozone pollution correlates with more severe CRS in people with CF. Among people with CF and CRS, higher ozone exposure is associated with worse olfactory function.

items.title: Evaluation of Agricultural Heat-Related Illness Prevention Training in Colorado.
items.abstract: Agricultural workers have high rates of heat-related illnesses (HRI). State-level regulations regarding HRI prevention in agriculture have been evolving and include requirements for heat-related prevention training of workers. There has been limited evaluation of the effectiveness of HRI prevention training. This study aimed to evaluate a train-the-trainer HRI prevention program. In 2024 and 2025, there were 13 train-the-trainer HRI prevention sessions held in English and Spanish in Colorado. The trainers then trained agricultural workers in their workplaces. Using the Kirkpatrick evaluation framework and a series of surveys and focus groups, changes in participant reaction levels, learning, behavior, and workplace outcomes were assessed. Descriptive statistics and paired t-test were used to analyze survey responses. Thematic analysis was used to analyze focus group data. Across 13 sessions, 143 trainers completed the train-the-trainer program, who then trained 1,270 agricultural workers. The trainers expressed high levels of satisfaction with the training and had significant improvement in their knowledge of HRI symptoms and prevention strategies. Training led to increased confidence among trainers in their ability to train workers. Trainers and agricultural workers reported adopting practices to prevent HRI. This study provides evidence that a bilingual, regulatory-aligned train-the-trainer program can be an effective approach to build HRI prevention capacity among agricultural employers. The Colorado-based train-the-trainer HRI prevention program increased trainer knowledge and confidence and in turn improved agricultural worker workplace heat-related prevention practices. These changes may protect worker health while also improving their well-being and productivity in the long term.

items.title: Written exposure therapy augmented with transcranial direct current stimulation for posttraumatic stress disorder: A pilot randomized clinical trial.
items.abstract: Written exposure therapy (WET) is an evidence-based, trauma-focused psychotherapy for posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) that has been tested with several trauma-exposed samples. Although many individuals who receive WET and other trauma-focused psychotherapies experience a significant reduction in PTSD symptoms, there remains room for improvement given that a meaningful proportion of individuals continue to meet the diagnostic criteria following treatment. Adjunctive interventions that can be easily combined with trauma-focused psychotherapies for PTSD may improve treatment outcomes. Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) is a noninvasive neurostimulation intervention that has demonstrated preliminary evidence of reducing PTSD symptoms. In this study, we combined WET with tDCS to treat PTSD in a pilot randomized clinical trial. Participants (N = 25) received five WET sessions and were randomized to active or sham tDCS targeting the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. Results showed no statistically significant group differences in PTSD symptom reductions at 1-month follow-up, as assessed using the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5 or PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5), ps = .573-.619, and both treatment groups demonstrated significant PTSD improvements, ps < .001, at the final assessment point. However, there was a significant two-way interaction for the PCL-5, p = .010. Deconstruction of this interaction showed that WET with tDCS had an accelerated effect, with larger PTSD symptom reductions occurring earlier in treatment relative to WET with sham tDCS. The findings highlight the potential of tDCS to accelerate PTSD outcomes when combined with WET and support conducting larger randomized clinical trials.

items.title: Classroom-based observation and intervention of executive function for special education teachers working with preschoolers with Autism.
items.abstract: Executive function (EF) related behavioral challenges are frequently observed in preschool children with autism spectrum disorder. However, structured, classroom-based observation of these behaviors by teachers remains difficult, resulting in limited practical assessment and recommendations for classroom-based support. This study aimed to examine the feasibility of teacher-administered EF assessment in special education centers and to formulate preliminary, expert-informed recommendations for autistic children with varying communication abilities. A mixed-methods sequential design was used. A total of 793 children with autism aged 3-6 years were assessed by trained teachers. Multidisciplinary expert consultation was conducted to formulate preliminary recommendations for classroom activities based on age and communication profiles. Teachers achieved at least 85% accuracy in score conversion and interpretation, supporting the feasibility of its use in a special education classroom. Patterns of EF-related behavioral challenges observed in 793 children aged 3-6 years were integrated with existing evidence and multidisciplinary expert consensus to inform preliminary recommendations for classroom activities. Working memory, inhibitory control, and cognitive flexibility were most evident, especially in children with limited verbal communication and those requiring intensive classroom support. Expert-informed classroom activities, including structured play, rule-changing games, memory-based exercises, emotional reflection tasks, and narrative planning, were subsequently suggested with increasing complexity across age groups and levels of communication ability. The findings provide preliminary support for the teacher-administered MU.EF-102 of the classroom use and informed age- and communication-responsive, expert-informed classroom activity recommendations. The effectiveness of these recommendations requires evaluation in future intervention studies.

items.title: Hemocyte, Biochemical, and Histopathological Responses of Biomphalaria alexandrina, the Egyptian Intermediate Host of Schistosoma mansoni, to Sublethal Deltamethrin Exposure.
items.abstract: Deltamethrin is among the pyrethroids most frequently detected in Egyptian irrigation canals and drains, the same water bodies that support Biomphalaria alexandrina, the snail that transmits Schistosoma mansoni in Egypt. The objective of this study was to characterize the response of adult B. alexandrina to sublethal concentrations of a commercial deltamethrin formulation, using hemocyte, biochemical, and histopathological biomarkers. The hypothesis tested was that sublethal deltamethrin reduces the number of circulating hemocytes, alters the balance between hemocyte classes and damages hemocyte structure, at concentrations comparable with those measured in Egyptian watercourses. Adult snails were exposed to a commercial deltamethrin emulsifiable concentrate, the form applied in the field. The 24-h median lethal concentration (LC50) was 0.41 mg/L as nominal active ingredient. Snails were then held for 48 h or 10 d at nominal LCo (0.04 mg/L), LC5 (0.25 mg/L), and LC10 (0.28 mg/L), the lowest of these being 1.2-fold the highest deltamethrin concentration so far reported from Giza-area watercourses. Circulating hemocytes fell by 35% after 48 h and by 45% after 10 d at LC10 (p < 0.001). The differential profile shifted toward granulocytes, from 66% in the 10-d control to 84% at LC10 (p < 0.001), at the expense of hyalinocytes and blast-like cells. Exposed cells showed retracted pseudopodia, incomplete mitotic figures, cytoplasmic vacuolization, and membrane rupture. Binucleate hemocytes rose from 12.50% to 35.87% and micronucleated cells from 2.63% to 6.43% (p < 0.001). Aspartate aminotransferase (AST), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), and glucose rose while total protein and albumin fell; reduced glutathione (GSH) rose alongside malondialdehyde (MDA) and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2); and the digestive gland and the ovotestis degenerated with concentration. The hypothesis was accepted. The hemocyte compartment is a sensitive target of sublethal pyrethroid exposure in a snail of direct public health importance.

items.title: Information quality, understandability, actionability and readability of large language models for HIV health education: A cross-platform evaluation.
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate health education materials, but their suitability for patient-facing human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) education remains insufficiently evaluated. We assessed the information quality, understandability, actionability, readability, text structure and source transparency of HIV patient education materials generated by six LLMs or artificial intelligence platforms. In this cross-sectional study, 100 common HIV patient education questions across 10 domains were submitted once in English to ChatGPT 5.4-Thinking, DeepSeek-V3.2, Doubao, ERNIE Bot 5.0 Preview, Ant Afu and Gemini 3.1 Pro, yielding 600 responses. Responses were evaluated using Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Printable Materials (PEMAT-P), EQ IP-36, DISCERN, Global Quality Score (GQS), artificial intelligence response quality metric (AIRM), Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) benchmarks and seven readability indices. Platform comparisons used paired Friedman tests with Wilcoxon-Holm post hoc analyses; topic analyses used question-level aggregation followed by Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn-Holm comparisons. Significant family-adjusted differences were observed across platforms for all prespecified text-structure, quality/understandability/actionability and readability outcomes. At the topic level, five of six text-structure outcomes, PEMAT-P Understandability, PEMAT-P Actionability, the exploratory PEMAT-P composite score and all seven readability indices differed significantly after family adjustment, whereas EQ IP-36, DISCERN, GQS, AIRM and JAMA did not. Overall actionability was limited and readability demands were high. LLM-generated HIV patient education materials showed substantial cross-platform and topic-level heterogeneity. These findings support the use of LLMs as expert-reviewed drafting tools rather than independent patient education sources. Direct factual accuracy, guideline concordance, hallucination and clinical safety were not assessed.

items.title: Management Strategies and Clinical Outcomes of Methicillin Resistant Staphylococcus Aureus Native Vertebral Osteomyelitis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is a major cause of native vertebral osteomyelitis (NVO) and is associated with persistent infection, complications, prolonged hospitalization, and increased mortality. We conducted this systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the antimicrobial and surgical approaches used for MRSA NVO and their associated clinical outcomes. Systematic review and meta-analysis. A systematic literature search of MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted on November 27, 2025. Studies were eligible if they included adults with MRSA NVO, evaluated medical or surgical treatment strategies, reported clinical outcomes, and included at least five patients. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and the Murad et al. tool. Random-effects models were used to pool proportions of treatment success, reinfection, and mortality. Thirty studies including 677 patients were included. Treatment strategies were heterogeneous and included prolonged anti-MRSA antimicrobial therapy and surgical approaches ranging from debridement and drainage to decompression and spinal stabilization or fusion. Vancomycin-based regimens were the most frequently reported antimicrobial strategy. Among studies reporting treatment duration, intravenous therapy commonly ranged from 4 to 8 weeks, with some patients receiving oral step-down or suppressive therapy. The pooled treatment success rate was 84.9% (95% CI, 76.7%-90.7%), pooled reinfection rate was 15.3% (95% CI, 9.5%-23.6%), and pooled mortality rate was 3.1% (95% CI, 0.8%-10.8%). Subgroup analyses were not feasible because treatment-specific data were limited and inconsistently reported. Management of MRSA NVO varied substantially across studies, with vancomycin-based antimicrobial therapy and diverse surgical strategies commonly reported. Pooled outcomes showed high treatment success with lower rates of reinfection and mortality. The substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity of the available evidence highlights the need for prospective studies with standardized treatment and outcome reporting.

items.title: Dose Optimization of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: A Policy opportunity to reduce costs and improve access to immunotherapy in the United States.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized cancer treatment, but are associated with high costs and limited accessibility. Optimizing dosing strategy to achieve a Pharmacokinetics/Pharmacodynamics (PK/PD) supported alternative lower dose (PPALD) that maintains clinical benefit and offers a cost-minimization strategy with substantial health system savings. We conducted a literature review of Phase 1/2 trials describing the PPALD dose of three commonly used ICIs: Pembrolizumab, Nivolumab and Atezolizumab. Alternate dosing strategies based on data for pembrolizumab (2mg/kg), nivolumab (2mg/kg) and atezolizumab (10mg/kg) were proposed. Public CMS Medicare Part B data on expenditure for these therapies was used to obtain average cost/dose, mg/dose, and number of Medicare beneficiaries between 2018-2021. Costs were calculated based on current FDA approved dosing and alternate dosing strategies. PPALD resulted in substantially lower drug costs per patient for an 80kg individual compared with fixed dosing: pembrolizumab ($7,393.60 vs $9,242.00), nivolumab ($4,153.60 vs $12,460.80), and atezolizumab ($5,744.00 vs $8,616.00). Estimated 2018-2021 Medicare savings based on beneficiaries were $382.2 million for pembrolizumab, $943.1 million for nivolumab, and $114.4 million for atezolizumab, totaling nearly $1.44 billion. Alternate immunotherapy dosing represents a high-value cost saving strategy to reduce health care costs and improve global access. Implementation requires regulatory adaptation, smaller vials, or vial-sharing to minimize waste. This policy analysis demonstrates that evidence-based alternate dosing of commonly used checkpoint inhibitors (Pembrolizumab, Nivolumab and Atezolizumab) could substantially reduce drug expenses while maintaining efficacy. Using Medicare Part B utilization data, we estimated that implementation of these alternative dosing strategies can help save over $1.44 billion between 2018-2021. These findings have important implications for health policy by improving patient access to immunotherapy and curtailing financial toxicity. This can be further facilitated by the support of policymakers, regulatory agencies supporting prospective validation studies and development of reimbursement models that encourage dose optimization.

items.title: A randomized controlled trial of a novel AI-based prognostic decision support tool integrated into the electronic health record for ischemic heart disease: Rationale and design of the PM Heart trial.
items.abstract: Ischemic heart disease (IHD) is the leading global cause of years of life lost. Although the clinical presentation and progression of IHD differ widely, clinical management is relatively uniform. To improve risk stratification and clinical management, we developed a decision support tool - the PMHeartIHD Algorithm (also named PMHNet) - based on extensive clinical, registry and biochemical data. This algorithm automatically calculates one-year survival following an IHD event. We hypothesize that presenting the prognoses calculated by the PMHeartIHD Algorithm to the treating physicians will improve both the clinical management and outcome of the individual patient. The objectives of the PM Heart trial include clinical and technical aspects. First, the primary aim is to investigate if the clinical use of the prognosis calculated by the algorithm improves patient prognosis and minimizes the risk of re-hospitalization, compared to standard of care. A secondary objective is to generate knowledge on how decision support tools in cardiology may be implemented, received, and used directly in clinical practice. The PMHeartIHD Aalgorithm has been integrated into the electronic health record (EHR) system (Sundhedsplatformen (SP), EPIC) for clinical use. The PM Heart trial is designed as a multicenter, prospective, randomized, open-label, clinical trial, automatically enrolling and randomizing hospitalized patients with coronary artery disease at the cardiology departments in The Capital Region and Region Zealand in Denmark. Patients are randomized (1:1 ratio) immediately after coronary angiography, to either show or hide the calculated PMHeartIHD-prognosis or not in the electronic health record. The primary outcome is a composite outcome consisting of re-admissions within 30 days and one-year survival rates after randomization. Inclusion began September 2023, and follow-up is expected to finish in 2026. We present the design of and rationale for the PM Heart trial. Our aim is to assess the clinical value of implementing an artificial intelligence-based decision support tool in clinical practice.

items.title: Educational attainment and systemic inflammation: Evidence of a stable gradient from two measurements in the Tromsø study (2007-2016).
items.abstract: Disadvantaged socioeconomic position (SEP) is associated with increased systemic inflammation. However, the mechanisms and potential persistence of these molecular differences remain poorly understood. We investigated the association between educational attainment, an indicator of SEP, and the levels of 52 plasma inflammatory proteins measured in the same individuals seven to eight years apart. We analyzed data from 909 participants of the sixth (2007-2008) and seventh (2015-2016) waves of the Tromsø Study, a longitudinal population-based study in Tromsø, Norway. Inflammatory protein levels were measured using the Olink Target 96 Inflammation panel and educational attainment was retrieved from questionnaires. Cross-sectional and longitudinal associations between educational attainment and inflammatory protein levels were assessed using multivariable linear models and linear mixed models, respectively. We identified a consistent association between higher educational attainment and lower levels of CCL20, CDCP1, and HGF, and higher levels of CST5 at both waves (FDR < 0.1). In addition, we observed that higher educational attainment was associated with lower levels of CCL19, IL-6, and OSM, and higher levels of FGF19 at the second wave only. Nonetheless, all associations were attenuated after adjustment for lifestyle factors, body-mass index, health conditions, and medication. Longitudinal analyses indicated a stable educational gradient across the two waves, with no significant changes in the association between educational attainment and inflammatory protein levels. Our findings indicate a stable educational gradient in the levels of several plasma proteins involved in cell migration, growth, and tissue remodeling in adults, across the seven-to-eight-year period, with modifiable lifestyle factors and body-mass index substantially attenuating the education-protein associations.

items.title: Adaptive local region super-resolution for high-field MRI: A diffusion-based approach with structural and frequency-domain constraints.
items.abstract: High-field MRI offers superior SNR but is constrained by the trade-off between spatial resolution and acquisition time. Existing global deep learning super-resolution (SR) methods often incur computational overhead by ignoring regional image content. This motivates an adaptive local SR strategy to optimize efficiency and detail preservation. To address this, we developed a local SR method that adaptively allocates computational resources to information-rich regions. The proposed framework regularized an entropy-based local region processing strategy with a diffusion model fortified by frequency-domain and structural constraints. We retrospectively evaluated our method on two diverse datasets: a proprietary 7.0 T dental MRI dataset (25 T2-weighted DESS sequences from 10 beagle dogs) and a public 5.0 T brain MRI dataset (Diff5T, 50 diffusion-weighted sequences). Image quality was quantified using PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and FID. On the 7.0 T dental test dataset (2 subjects), our method achieved a PSNR of 27.31 [26.83, 27.79] dB and the lowest LPIPS of 0.19 [0.18, 0.20]. On the 5.0 T brain test dataset (10 subjects), the method achieved a PSNR of 27.15 ± 0.10 dB, an LPIPS of 0.14 ± 0.00 and an FID of 54.01, with lower perceptual metrics than the evaluated baselines. Ablation studies indicated that the proposed frequency-domain and structural constraints reduced LPIPS and FID, with trade-offs in PSNR and SSIM. In conclusion, the evaluated framework showed improvements in perceptual metrics by integrating targeted local processing with frequency-domain and structural regularization, accompanied by a trade-off in pixel-wise fidelity metrics, supporting the technical feasibility of addressing the resolution-time trade-off in high-field MRI. Future work will focus on expanding the dataset and evaluating the framework in human dental cohorts to address anatomical differences between the current canine model and human dental anatomy.

items.title: Carbonization and nitrogen plasma doping of zeolitic imidazolate framework‑8/bacterial cellulose aerogel membrane anodes for improved bioelectrocatalysis.
items.abstract: To address the performance bottlenecks in microbial fuel cells (MFCs), we fabricate a novel N-doped zeolitic imidazolate framework-8/bacterial cellulose aerogel membrane (N/ZIF-8/BAM), integrating two-level porous with plasma-assisted high-level nitrogen doping. Carbonized bacterial cellulose provides a three-dimensional interconnected macroporous network that facilitates Bacillus subtilis colonization and transport, while ZIF-8 derived carbon introduces nanopores to expand the electrochemical active surface area. After N2 plasma doping, N/ZIF‑8/BAM contains substantial pyrrolic N, pyridinic N, and graphitic N species. Zeta potential measurements reveal that N/ZIF‑8/BAM exhibits an overall negative surface potential (-34.6 mV), yet local positively charged N-doping sites improve bacterial adhesion at the anode interface, consistent with bacterial colonization observations. Optimized N configurations lower charge transfer resistance and promoting bio-electrocatalysis. The hierarchical porous structure enhances extracellular electron transfer between bacteria and the anode, thereby yielding a peak power density of 0.56 mW cm-2. This work offers a feasible strategy to design high-performance anodes for MFCs.

items.title: Comparative evaluation of time-to-event analysis methods for mobility limitation in older adults: A multi-cohort benchmarking study.
items.abstract: Time-to-event models are central to aging research, quantifying both whether and when an event occurs. However, guidance on selecting among traditional statistical and machine learning (ML) methods for prediction modeling remains limited, particularly for epidemiologic aging cohorts with wide assessment intervals. Mobility limitation, as a clinically important aging outcome with such complexities, provides a relevant test case for methodological benchmarking. We conducted a systematic benchmark comparison of 14 statistical and ML time-to-event methods using harmonized data from four longitudinal U.S. aging cohorts (N = 14,821). The outcome was time to incident mobility limitation, defined by self-reported walking difficulty or gait speed < 0.8 m/s. Models were evaluated using 4-fold cross-validation repeated 100 times within cohorts. Performance metrics captured complementary dimensions of predictive quality: discrimination (C-index), accuracy and calibration (Brier score, integrated log loss, calibration index), and computational efficiency (model training time). Prespecified decision rules synthesize results across metrics to identify preferable methods. Across pooled analyses, multiple methods demonstrated comparable discrimination, including penalized Cox models, tree-based ensembles, and boosting approaches. Oblique random survival forest achieved the most favorable overall trade-off, combining high discrimination (C-index 0.673), good calibration (Brier score 0.147), and moderate training time (9.2 min). When computational efficiency was prioritized, penalized regression methods may be preferable, with good discrimination and Brier score. These findings support random forest and penalized regression as strong defaults for time-to-event prediction modeling in gerontologic research and highlight the importance of joint evaluation of discrimination, calibration, and feasibility.

items.title: Menstrual Health in Children, Adolescents, and Young Adults with Cardiac Disease: An Underrecognized Component of Heart Failure, Mechanical Circulatory Support, and Transplant Care.
items.abstract: Menstrual abnormalities, including heavy menstrual bleeding, amenorrhea, and dysmenorrhea, are frequently encountered among children, adolescents, and young adults with congenital and acquired heart disease, yet remain underrecognized in routine cardiovascular care. Anticoagulation, thrombosis risk, heart failure physiology, and limited high-quality evidence complicate management and contribute to substantial variation in practice. The Advanced Cardiac Therapies Improving Outcomes Network convened a multidisciplinary working group of cardiologists, hematologists, gynecologists, adolescent medicine specialists, and allied health providers. Following a literature search, the group met monthly via virtual meetings to synthesize current evidence and clinical experience and develop consensus guidance. The consensus emphasizes routine, developmentally appropriate menstrual screening and recognition that traditional definitions of heavy menstrual bleeding may underestimate its clinical impact in patients with heart disease. Management requires individualized assessment of bleeding risk, thrombotic risk, cardiac physiology, and patient preferences. Menstrual abnormalities may warrant broader evaluation for changes in overall health, cardiac status, or energy availability. Menstrual health is integral to comprehensive cardiovascular care. Integrating screening and individualized management into cardiology practice may reduce morbidity, improve quality of life, and support equitable, sex-informed care. Further research and culturally responsive, multidisciplinary implementation are needed to strengthen the evidence base and improve care consistency.

items.title: Integrated transcriptomics and histological analysis reveal gill adaptation mechanisms to hypoxic stress in largemouth bass (Micropterus salmoides).
items.abstract: Largemouth bass (Micropterus salmoides) is a globally significant freshwater aquaculture species known for its rapid growth, high-quality flesh and excellent nutritional value. Given the increasing incidence of hypoxia in its aquaculture setting, understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying gill adaptation to hypoxic stress is critical for improving resilience in this species. To achieve this, we employed full-length transcript sequencing using PacBio Iso-Seq and high-throughput Illumina RNA-Seq to construct a comprehensive transcriptome profile. Histological analyses revealed apparent structural alterations in gill tissues under hypoxic stress (dissolved oxygen: 2.0 ± 0.5 mg/L, duration: 96 h), including curved and swollen gill filaments, apoptosis and epithelial cell vacuolation. Comparative transcriptomic analysis revealed pronounced shifts in the expression of genes involved in energy metabolism, angiogenesis, immune responses, cell proliferation and apoptosis. Notably, the down-regulation of genes associated with cell cycle and proliferation suggests that M. salmoides may conserve energy by suppressing cell division under hypoxic conditions. In contrast, the increased expression of apoptosis-related genes, including casp7, indicates that apoptosis may play a protective role in maintain tissue homeostasis under hypoxia. Furthermore, the suppression of chemokine-mediated immune pathways implies that hypoxia redirects energy toward essential metabolic processes at the cost of local immune responses. GO and KEGG enrichment analyses identified TNF-α and chemokine-mediated signalling pathways as key pathways involved in tissue homeostasis and adaptive responses to hypoxic stress. These findings enhance our understanding of the mechanisms underlying hypoxia adaptation and provide valuable genetic resources for breeding strategies aimed at enhancing hypoxia tolerance in M. salmoides.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in multidisciplinary and cross-sector public health practice: A scoping review.
items.abstract: This scoping review examined how artificial intelligence is applied in multidisciplinary and cross-sector public health practice, focusing on public health roles, collaborative implementation, and cross-sector governance and equity risks. Scoping review. Following Arksey and O'Malley's framework and PRISMA-ScR reporting guidance, six databases were searched. Sources were included if they examined artificial intelligence or artificial intelligence-enabled decision support in public, population, or community health contexts and provided information on public health functions, collaboration, implementation, equity, or governance. Data were charted and synthesised narratively by study characteristics, artificial intelligence roles, collaborators, implementation conditions, and governance risks. 27 sources published between 2021 and 2026 were included. Most were reviews, evidence syntheses, policy or guidance documents, or conceptual papers, with relatively few empirical or practitioner-oriented studies. Artificial intelligence was mainly used for surveillance and early warning, population risk modelling, health communication, misinformation detection, policy intelligence, participatory co-creation, and routine public health operations. Implementation depended on collaboration among public health practitioners, epidemiologists, data scientists, policymakers, legal and ethics experts, communication specialists, community organisations, and affected populations. Cross-sector governance and equity risks included poor data quality, limited interoperability, workforce gaps, weak real-world evaluation, privacy risks, and unclear accountability. Artificial intelligence applications in public health are expanding, but the evidence base remains heterogeneous and empirically limited. Routine operational support and AI readiness, together with surveillance and early warning, were among the more frequently represented roles, while empirical evidence on real-world implementation, community engagement and governance evaluation remained limited. Future research should move beyond model performance to examine workflow fit, equity impact, public trust, accountability and population-level outcomes.

items.title: AI without reach: The last mile problem in preventive public health.
items.abstract: Examine the "last mile problem" in artificial intelligence (AI) applications for preventive public health. Conceptual short communication introducing a five-stage pathway to examine where AI-enabled prevention breaks down. This draws on emerging literature in AI, health services research, and implementation science to distinguish between predictive capacity and real-world impact. A five-stage pathway model of prediction, translation, delivery, uptake, and sustainment is introduced to characterize where breakdowns occur between identifying risk and changing outcomes. Current AI applications in public health are heavily concentrated in prediction, with limited attention to delivery, engagement, and sustained behavior change. These gaps are particularly consequential in prevention, where action must occur before consequences are visible, and in contexts such as family caregiving, where individuals operate as de facto delivery systems without adequate support. Traditional measures of healthcare access further obscure the problem by suggesting that services are available when real-world barriers prevent their use. The last mile problem is not evenly distributed; it disproportionately affects populations facing structural disadvantage, meaning that AI systems that fail to account for delivery and context risk widening existing inequities. Addressing the last mile requires reorienting AI from a primarily predictive tool to one embedded in systems of care and daily life. This includes integrating real-time data, designing for context, and evaluating AI on whether it enables timely, sustained action, not on predictive accuracy alone. Until AI reaches the last mile, its contribution to prevention will remain incomplete, accurate in prediction but limited in impact.

items.title: AEX-1: A Vero cell variant with enhanced permissiveness for influenza virus replication.
items.abstract: Continuous cell substrates with improved permissiveness for influenza virus replication are of considerable interest for vaccine development and manufacturing. Vero cells have an excellent regulatory track record; however, their relatively low influenza virus productivity limits their broader application. We developed the AEX-1 cell line by co-cultivating Vero cells with chicken embryo amniotic membrane fragments. Cellular morphology, intracellular acidification, influenza virus replication, transcriptomic profile, genetic stability, and tumorigenicity were evaluated. AEX-1 cells displayed distinct morphology and enhanced endosomal/lysosomal acidification compared with parental Vero cells. At 72 h post-infection, a commonly used harvest time for influenza vaccine virus production, AEX-1 cells produced higher infectious titres of WHO-recommended egg-derived A/Sydney/5/2021 (H1N1)pdm09-like and B/Austria/1359417/2021 vaccine viruses, with titres approaching those obtained in embryonated chicken eggs and exceeding Vero cell yields by 0.9-1.7 log10 EID50/ml. No replication advantage was observed for the egg-derived A/Croatia/10136RV/2023 (H3N2) vaccine virus, carrying the egg-adaptive HA G53D substitution, or for the egg-derived A/duck/Vietnam/NCVD-1584/2012 (H5N1) vaccine strain. However, the A/Darwin/9/2021-like Vero-derived primary isolate A/Austria/1516645/2022 (H3N2), lacking G53D, reached infectious titres up to 3.0 log10 TCID50/ml higher than in Vero and 2.3 log10 TCID50/ml higher than in MDCK cells. H1N1 UniFluVec-based influenza virus vectors also replicated efficiently in AEX-1 cells. Transcriptomic analysis revealed changes in genes involved in proton transport, vesicular acidification, and intracellular pH regulation. AEX-1 remained genetically stable after prolonged passaging and showed no evidence of increased tumorigenicity in vitro or in vivo. Enhanced intracellular acidification may contribute to improved influenza virus replication in AEX-1 cells, suggesting that modulation of endosomal acidification may provide a rational strategy for developing improved cell substrates for influenza vaccine production.

items.title: Physical activity and sleep patterns in women 1 year after gestational diabetes: Results from the Face-it study.
items.abstract: Moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) and adequate, high-quality sleep are important for cardiometabolic health in women with recent gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) but are likely reduced during early motherhood. These behaviours may be associated; however, device-measured sleep data and studies of these associations remain scarce in this population. This cross sectional study characterised MVPA and sleep patterns and examined their associations in women with recent GDM. In the Face-it trial, 185 women provided device-measured MVPA and sleep data 1 year after delivery. Sleep variables included duration and efficiency, reflecting sleep quantity and quality. Duration was categorised as 8 h/night. Associations with MVPA were analysed using linear mixed-effects models with site as a random intercept, adjusted for potential confounders. Two-thirds (61.6%) met WHO recommendations for moderate-intensity physical activity (PA), whereas few (3.2%) met recommendations for vigorous-intensity PA. Most met recommendations for sleep duration (87.6%) and sleep efficiency (83.8%). Compared to 6-8 h/night, there was no difference in MVPA among those sleeping 8 h/night were associated with less MVPA (β = -13.5, 95% CI = -23.0, -4.0, p = 0.006). Sleep efficiency was positively associated with MVPA (β = 0.6, 95% CI = 0.1, 1.1, p = 0.018). The association between high-quality sleep and greater MVPA suggests that PA and sleep may not only independently be relevant to cardiometabolic health but may also be associated in women with recent GDM.

items.title: Sacrificial-Template Fabrication of Orientation-Controlled Porous Titanium Lattices With Bioactive Surfaces.
items.abstract: Porous titanium scaffolds for bone repair require coordinated control of pore architecture, mechanical behavior, and surface bioactivity. Here, we report a sacrificial-template route based on polymer 3D printing that produces orientation-controlled porous titanium scaffolds with hierarchical macro- and microporosity without direct metal additive manufacturing. Polylactic acid lattices printed by fused deposition modeling are infiltrated with a titanium powder slurry and then subjected to template removal and sintering. The process yields ortho-grid, tri-lattice, and quad-lattice structures with approximately 26% isotropic linear shrinkage, 65%-67% porosity, preserved geometric fidelity, and a relative density of approximately 95% in the sintered strut walls. Uniaxial compression tests reveal architecture-dependent behavior along the tested loading direction, whereas finite element simulations predict lower directional sensitivity under off-axis loading as strut-orientation diversity increases. Micro-arc oxidation forms a Ca-P-containing microporous oxide layer and improves cell spreading, proliferation, and alkaline phosphatase activity relative to untreated titanium scaffolds in vitro. In a rat calvarial defect model, uncoated titanium scaffolds achieve bone regeneration comparable to commercial porous tantalum, while micro-arc oxidation further enhances bone formation. Fabrication of cone augments and other non-prismatic geometries further demonstrates the adaptability of the approach to complex implant-relevant structures.

items.title: Economic evaluation of the Akwenda Intervention Program for children and young people with cerebral palsy in rural Uganda: A trial-based analysis of costs and outcomes.
items.abstract: To relate the trial-based costs of the Akwenda Intervention Program, a multi-component, community-based intervention for children and young people with cerebral palsy (CP) in rural Uganda, to multiple prespecified child and caregiver outcomes. An economic evaluation was conducted within a cluster-randomized, assessor-blinded trial of 94 participants with CP (aged 2-23 years; 42 females) and their caregivers, allocated to intervention or usual care. Programme delivery costs were assessed from a restricted health care or provider perspective; selected out-of-pocket costs incurred by participating families were reported separately over 12 months. Outcome-specific incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) were estimated for child outcomes (66-item Gross Motor Function Measure, Pediatric Evaluation of Disability Inventory [Ugandan version], and Picture My Participation) and caregiver outcomes (Zimbabwe Caregiver Challenges Scale and Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory Family Impact Module). Uncertainty was assessed using bootstrapping, cost-effectiveness planes, and exploratory acceptability curves. Costs were also determined per minimal clinically important difference (MCID) gained. The mean incremental cost per child was US$1069 to US$1075. Outcome-specific ICERs ranged from US$26 to US$352 per unit of improvement for 10 of 11 outcomes; the Pediatric Evaluation of Disability Inventory (Ugandan version) mobility had a higher and highly uncertain ICER. Costs per MCID gained ranged from US$230 to US$600. Acceptability analyses were presented as exploratory uncertainty analyses because no established Uganda-specific willingness-to-pay thresholds exist for these outcome measures. The Akwenda Intervention Program improved child functioning, participation, and caregiver well-being at additional but predictable costs. This trial-based economic evaluation quantifies the costs associated with improvement across multiple prespecified outcomes and provides economic information relevant to the implementation of community-based rehabilitation in low-resource settings.

items.title: Hammersmith Infant Neurological Examination: Prediction of neurodevelopmental delay in children born between 29 and 36 weeks of gestation.
items.abstract: To evaluate the ability of the Hammersmith Infant Neurological Examination (HINE) at 3 months 2 weeks corrected age to identify developmental difficulties at 2 years corrected age in infants born preterm between 29 and 36 weeks of gestation. In this prospective cohort study, the HINE was administered at 3 months 2 weeks corrected age. Development was assessed at 2 years corrected age using the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition (Bayley-4) and MacArthur-Bates Communicative Development Inventories. Developmental delay was defined using Bayley-4 scores less than 1 SD below the mean; expressive language delay was defined as a score less than the 10th centile for the number of spoken words expected for age. The cohort was largely free of brain lesions typically associated with cerebral palsy (5% intraventricular hemorrhage, with no other major brain lesions reported). Associations were examined using linear regression, screening performance using receiver operating characteristic curves, and incremental predictive value by comparing adjusted R2 across models, including perinatal and socioenvironmental factors with and without the HINE. A total of 174 infants were included in the analyses. The HINE total score was not associated with motor, cognitive, or language outcomes. Discriminative performance was poor (area under the curve = 0.48-0.57); adding the HINE total score to models including perinatal and socioenvironmental factors did not improve predictive performance. A single HINE at 3 months 2 weeks corrected age has limited utility for identifying mild-to-moderate developmental difficulties in this population and should not be used alone to determine developmental surveillance needs. Longitudinal surveillance incorporating complementary sources of developmental, clinical, and socioenvironmental information may be more effective.

items.title: Longitudinal associations between dietary intake and common mental disorders among adolescents in Australia.
items.abstract: There is a need for more longitudinal research exploring temporal associations between diet quality and common mental disorders (CMDs) during adolescence. This study examined prospective associations between indicators of adolescents' diet quality (fruit, vegetable, sugar-sweetened beverage [SSB] intakes) and risk of depression and anxiety onset over 3 years. We hypothesised that higher fruit and vegetable intake, and lower SSB intake, would be associated with lower risk of CMDs. 6537 Australian adolescents (mean age 12.65 years at baseline) completed surveys at baseline, 1-, 2- and 3-year follow-ups. We fitted Generalised Estimating Equations Poisson regression models to assess longitudinal associations between daily servings of fruit, vegetables and SSBs, and risk of depression and anxiety onset (binary cut-points on validated scales) over 3 years. Models were re-run for males and females. Analyses excluded participants who met thresholds for depression or anxiety at baseline to increase confidence that diet predicted CMD onset. Higher fruit intake was associated with lower risk of depression (adjusted RR: 0.87, 95% CI: 0.82-0.93) and anxiety (adjusted RR: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.87-0.99) over 3 years, with limited evidence of sex differences. Higher SSB intake (log-transformed) was associated with higher CMD risk for both sexes, but more strongly for males (depression: adjusted RR: 3.25, 95% CI: 2.02-5.23; anxiety: adjusted RR: 5.50, 95% CI: 3.39-8.90) than females (depression: adjusted RR: 3.10, 95% CI: 2.06-4.68; anxiety: adjusted RR: 2.04, 95% CI: 1.23-3.37). Results inform the Global burden of disease Lifestyle And mental Disorders project (DERR2-https://doi.org/10.2196/65576). Longitudinal research exposing temporal associations between diet and CMDs may inform prevention/intervention efforts targeting modifiable risk factors for CMDs.

items.title: Prevalence and Determinants of Maternal Malnutrition Among Pregnant and Lactating Women in Gaza: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: ObjectivesTo assess the prevalence of mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC)-defined malnutrition and identify associated sociodemographic factors among pregnant and lactating women in Gaza.MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted from September 1, 2025, to February 28, 2026, between 09:00 and 13:00 daily, among 3000 participants aged 15-49 years recruited from selected health facilities and community-based maternal and child health service points across four geographic areas of the Gaza Strip. The questionnaire was developed and administered in Arabic. Malnutrition was assessed using MUAC, with MUAC <23 cm defining malnutrition. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS version 26, with significance set at p-value < 0.05.ResultsOverall, 44.9% of the included participants were malnourished, with a higher prevalence among lactating women (49.3%) than pregnant women (42%). Younger age was associated with higher odds of malnutrition: women aged 18-24 years had increased odds (AOR = 1.30; 95% CI: 1.02-1.66; p = 0.034), whereas those aged 25-45 years had lower odds (AOR = 0.73; 95% CI: 0.54-0.97; p = 0.033). Compared with Gaza City, residents of the Middle Area (AOR = 0.66; 95% CI: 0.54-0.81; p = 0.001) and North Gaza (AOR = 0.47; 95% CI: 0.38-0.58; p = 0.001) had lower odds of malnutrition, while internally displaced women had higher odds (AOR = 1.33; 95% CI: 1.07-1.67; p = 0.012).ConclusionMUAC-defined malnutrition was highly prevalent among the women, with younger age, geographic area, and displacement associated with higher odds of malnutrition. The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, and MUAC alone does not capture all dimensions of maternal nutritional status. The facility- and community-based sampling and equal geographic allocation, the prevalence estimate should not be interpreted as a population-weighted estimate for all pregnant and lactating women in Gaza.

items.title: Readability, reliability, and quality of AI-Generated responses on pelvic congestion syndrome: A comparative analysis of ChatGPT, gemini, and perplexity.
items.abstract: ObjectivePelvic congestion syndrome (PCS) is a vascular cause of chronic pelvic pain arising from ovarian and pelvic venous insufficiency, typically presenting as dull, aching pelvic pain that worsens with prolonged standing, physical activity, and the premenstrual period, and is particularly common among multiparous women of reproductive age. Online health information on this condition is frequently accessed by both patients and healthcare professionals. This study aimed to evaluate the readability, quality, and reliability of responses generated by three popular artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots-ChatGPT-4o, Gemini, and Perplexity-regarding the most commonly asked questions on PCS.MethodsFrom 25 PCS-related keywords identified through Google Trends, duplicates and irrelevant terms were excluded, yielding a final set of 18 keywords. These were separately submitted to the three AI chatbots. Readability was assessed using the Gunning Fog Index (GFOG), Simple Measure of Gobbledygook (SMOG), and Flesch Reading Ease Score (FRES), among other indices, calculated via two independent readability tools. Quality was measured using the Global Quality Score (GQS) and the Ensuring Quality Information for Patients (EQIP) tool, while reliability was assessed with the Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) benchmark criteria and the modified DISCERN instrument.ResultsReadability analyses revealed that all chatbot responses significantly exceeded the sixth-grade level recommended by the AMA and NIH (p < .001). ChatGPT-4o achieved the highest readability on the CLI and ARI, whereas Gemini performed better on the remaining indices, and Perplexity consistently produced the most complex responses. Among the three evaluated freely accessible platforms, Perplexity achieved the highest scores on several quality and reliability measures (JAMA, DISCERN, and GQS), while Gemini outperformed the others on EQIP scoring.ConclusionAlthough AI chatbots hold promise for providing accessible information on PCS, their readability levels remain above recommended standards, and overall quality scores are suboptimal. Producing clearer, more balanced, and more reliable content could enhance the contribution of these technologies to public health.

items.title: Aptamer-Based Targeted Protein Degradation: Mechanistic Principles, Delivery Strategies, and Translational Opportunities.
items.abstract: Targeted elimination of pathogenic proteins remains a fundamental challenge in therapeutic intervention, particularly for proteins considered "undruggable" by conventional inhibition-based approaches. Aptamer-based targeted protein degradation (TPD) has emerged as a versatile strategy that leverages the high specificity, structural programmability, and chemical tunability of nucleic acid aptamers to redirect disease-relevant proteins toward endogenous degradation pathways. Intracellular platforms, exemplified by aptamer-conjugated proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs), induce ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of cytosolic and nuclear targets. In parallel, extracellular and membrane-targeting modalities, including aptamer-conjugated lysosome-targeting chimeras (LYTACs) and related lysosomal degradation systems, enable clearance of secreted and membrane-bound proteins that are inaccessible to proteasome-based strategies. Collectively, these approaches broaden the potentially degradable proteome and offer opportunities to improve target selectivity and therapeutic safety. However, most aptamer-based TPD systems remain at the proof-of-concept or early preclinical stage, with limited standardization of degradation potency, kinetics, selectivity, and in vivo efficacy. Additional challenges include the discovery of functionally active aptamers, preservation of affinity and activity after chemical modification or conjugation, efficient delivery, chemical stability, controlled biodistribution, and mitigation of innate immune activation. This review provides a mechanistic and comparative framework for intracellular and extracellular aptamer-based TPD strategies, with emphasis on quantitative performance, delivery considerations, technical bottlenecks, and their translational potential for precision protein-targeted therapeutics.

items.title: Minimal Clinically Important Difference of the Modified Barium Swallow Impairment Profile (MBSImP) Pharyngeal Total Score in Post-Stroke Dysphagia.
items.abstract: The Modified Barium Swallow Impairment Profile (MBSImP) is widely used to quantify swallowing physiology during videofluoroscopic swallowing assessment, but the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) for its pharyngeal total score in post-stroke dysphagia remains unclear. This study estimated the MCID for improvement in the MBSImP pharyngeal total score during inpatient rehabilitation. This prospective multicenter observational study included stroke survivors with dysphagia admitted for inpatient rehabilitation 2 weeks to 3 months after stroke onset. Baseline and 10-day follow-up assessments included the MBSImP pharyngeal total score, Functional Oral Intake Scale (FOIS), Penetration-Aspiration Scale (PAS), and Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC). The FOIS was used as the primary anchor, while the PAS and PGIC were secondary anchors. Anchor-based estimates were calculated using average change, change difference, linear regression, and receiver operating characteristic analyses. Distribution-based estimates and minimal detectable change were used as complementary context for interpreting the anchor-based estimates. Sensitivity analyses were performed using stricter or collapsed anchor definitions, including collapsed FOIS categories, ≥ 2-level FOIS improvement, collapsed PAS categories, and a stricter PGIC threshold. An exploratory interaction analysis additionally examined whether the MBSImP change associated with exactly 1-level versus exactly 2-level FOIS improvement varied according to baseline FOIS level. A total of 161 participants were included. The MBSImP pharyngeal total score decreased from a median of [9.00 (7.00, 11.00)] to [4.00 (2.00, 6.00)]. The mean improvement, used for anchor-based MCID estimation, was 4.27 points. Changes in the MBSImP pharyngeal total score were significantly correlated with the FOIS, PAS, and PGIC (r > 0.3). The pooled average-change and change-difference estimates under the prespecified anchor definitions were 2.977 and 2.004 points, respectively. Under stricter or category-based anchor definitions, average-change estimates increased to 4.633-5.141 points, whereas change-difference estimates remained comparatively stable at 1.731-2.554 points. ROC-derived cutoffs were 2-3 points under the prespecified definitions and 5 points under the stricter definitions. In the exploratory FOIS analysis, there was no evidence that the contrast between exactly 1-level and exactly 2-level improvement varied by baseline FOIS level (P for interaction = 0.776); findings were similar when restricted to baseline FOIS levels 2-5 (P = 0.503). Clinically important change in the MBSImP pharyngeal total score depended on the anchor definition and intended interpretation. Under the prespecified anchor definitions, average-change estimates were approximately 3 points, whereas stricter functional or swallowing-safety improvement definitions showed estimates close to 5 points. In contrast, change-difference estimates were comparatively stable at approximately 2 points across anchor definitions.

items.title: Astrocyte-Associated ABCA1/APOE Responses Accompany Hippocampal Lipid Remodeling and Ectopic Neuronal Accumulation During Epileptogenesis.
items.abstract: Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is characterized by progressive hippocampal remodeling, including reactive astrogliosis and aberrant neuronal positioning. Although lipid disturbances are implicated in epileptogenesis, how astrocyte-associated lipid responses relate to hippocampal remodeling remains poorly understood. Here, human TLE and kainic acid (KA)-treated mouse transcriptomic datasets identified ATP-binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1)/Abca1 as a nominal astrocyte-associated candidate, while KA- and pilocarpine-induced status epilepticus (SE) elicited astrocyte-associated ABCA1/apolipoprotein E (APOE) responses. Ectopic granule cells and immature neurons accumulated in the hilus and were spatially associated with ABCA1-positive cells, including astrocytic profiles; perilipin 2 (PLIN2)-positive puncta were nearby. Pretreatment with the retinoid X receptor (RXR) agonist bexarotene increased hippocampal ABCA1 expression, delayed severe KA-induced behavioral seizure onset, and was associated with fewer chronic spontaneous seizures and reduced ectopic neuronal accumulation. Post-SE bexarotene administration was associated with lower seizure frequency, ectopic neuronal accumulation, and astrocytic marker-positive cell densities. Multi-omic profiling identified bexarotene-associated metabolic and lipidomic changes; transmission electron microscopy (TEM) showed a smaller mean hilar neuronal lipid-droplet area per image, and protein analyses identified early changes in p38 and extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2 (Erk1/2) phosphorylation. Together, these findings warrant further investigation of astrocyte-associated lipid pathways as potential therapeutic targets in epilepsy-associated hippocampal remodeling.

items.title: COVID-19 communication campaigns in Southeast Asia countries with multilingual communities: A scoping review.
items.abstract: BackgroundThe complexities of multilingualism in COVID-19 communication campaigns across Southeast Asia's multicultural countries remain unexplored.ObjectiveThis paper aims to map and summarize the development, implementation, and evaluation of COVID-19 preventive behavior and vaccination campaigns in the region.MethodsUtilizing the PRISMA-ScR framework, major databases were searched for relevant articles published between January 2020 and March 2025, focusing on the content and delivery of COVID-19 communication campaigns within multilingual Southeast Asian countries.ResultsTwenty articles were retrieved, most of which originated from Indonesia (n = 11), followed by Vietnam (n = 3), Malaysia, the Philippines, and Singapore (n = 2 each). Studies on prevention (n = 13) outnumbered those on vaccination campaigns (n = 5). Of the 86 described campaign materials, posters (n = 63) were the most prevalent media type, primarily developed by the government (n = 60). Most materials used the country's official language for the campaigns, with 49 for prevention and 27 for vaccination. Channels varied; government social media dominated in Malaysia, while physical public spaces were most common elsewhere. The strategic implementation of multilingual and culturally specific communication emerged as a key opportunity, in contrast to the major challenge of the widespread anti-vaccine misinformation on social media.ConclusionsThe reported communication materials were largely characterized by an urgent, mass-reach approach using a country's official language, which endangered linguistic minorities. Crucially, this review highlights a systemic mishap in campaign assessment, marked by a near-total absence of evidence-based impact data, hindering the evaluation of effective strategies for public health outcomes.

items.title: Mapping care interventions for people living with motor neurone disease: a living evidence and gap map.
items.abstract: Motor neurone disease (MND) is a debilitating, life-limiting neurodegenerative disease that has no cure. Caring for a person living with MND requires a multidisciplinary team delivering interventions to address symptoms. We aimed to map evidence supporting care of those living with MND. Evidence and gap maps (EGMs) were developed according to Campbell and JBI guidance for scoping reviews. Databases searched included CENTRAL, MEDLINE, EMBASE, and PsycINFO with no date restriction. Articles describing care interventions for people living with MND, carers, asymptomatic genetic carriers, family, friends, and healthcare professionals were included. 2390 reports were drawn from 1594 articles that were included across five EGMs, supportive and symptom management (n = 673 articles), pharmacological (n = 592), models of care (n = 196), medical and clinical interventions (n = 185), and technology and equipment (n = 91). Interventions primarily addressed people who are living with MND (n = 1732). No articles were identified specifically concerning First Nations Peoples, Culturally and Linguistically Diverse Peoples, or those living in remote, rural or regional areas. MND care interventions are diverse. Further research is needed to understand options for Culturally and Linguistically Diverse Peoples, First Nations Peoples, and those living in rural, regional, and remote communities.

items.title: Exploring a culturally tailored psychoeducational intervention for Vietnamese Australians affected by alcohol, other drugs and gambling in South Western Sydney: A pre-post qualitative study.
items.abstract: Vietnamese communities in South Western Sydney experience migration-related stressors, stigma, and barriers to accessing alcohol and other drug (AOD) and gambling services. Culturally tailored psychoeducational interventions may improve recovery-oriented outcomes; however, qualitative evidence in this population is limited. This study explores how Vietnamese participants with lived or indirect experience of AOD and/or gambling frame their experiences and examines the perceived impact of a culturally tailored psychoeducational program on recovery and quality of life. An exploratory pre-post qualitative study was conducted within a public drug and alcohol service in South Western Sydney, Australia. Seventeen Vietnamese-background adults enrolled in a five-session psychoeducational program covering AOD literacy, family communication, legal awareness, stress management, and self-care. Eleven participants completed all program sessions and both pre- and post-intervention interviews and were included in the final analysis. Semi-structured interviews were conducted primarily in Vietnamese before and after the intervention and were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Four interrelated themes were identified:(1) migration stress, stigma, and family-centred framing of addiction; (2) limited pre-intervention service and legal literacy; (3) psychoeducation as a pathway to empowerment and emotional regulation; and (4) recovery reframed as quality of life and relational repair. Participants reported improved self-efficacy, emotional regulation, communication skills, and knowledge of treatment and legal systems. Recovery was conceptualized beyond abstinence, encompassing strengthened recovery capital, reduced stigma, and improved family functioning. Culturally tailored psychoeducation was acceptable and beneficial for Vietnamese participants affected by AOD and gambling harms. It enhanced recovery capital, reduced stigma, and supported culturally meaningful recovery pathways. Such interventions may serve as valuable adjuncts to mainstream AOD services for culturally and linguistically diverse populations.

items.title: Necropolitics of ıntimacy: family violence and trans lives in Türkiye.
items.abstract: This article examines the violence experienced by trans individuals in Türkiye within family and intimate relationships, treating it as a structured, enduring regime rather than a series of isolated acts. Drawing on semi-structured interviews with 17 trans individuals, the study uses reflexive thematic analysis to trace how violence originates within the family and extends into intimate relationships, public spaces, and institutional encounters. The analysis brings together Agamben's state of exception and bare life with Mbembe's necropolitics and politics of enmity to show how trans individuals are excluded from legal and moral protection and governed through abandonment, exposure, and slow death. Relocating Agamben's concepts from the concentration camp, his paradigmatic site of exception, to the family, the article distinguishes domination within family membership from the revocation of membership itself and treats bare life as a negotiated asymptote rather than an inhabited condition. The findings show that violence is normalised through discourses of love, protection and morality, while state institutions often withdraw from their protective role or become sites of secondary harm. Preventing violence against trans individuals requires political interventions that simultaneously address familial relations, intimate life, and institutional responsibility.

items.title: Patterns of cardiovascular disease subtypes and associated factors among young adults in Peshawar, Pakistan: a multicenter hospital-based cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are a major cause of morbidity and mortality. Evidence on CVD subtypes in young Pakistani adults is limited. This study characterized CVD subtypes and associated factors among young adults in Peshawar Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. A multicentre, cross-sectional study was conducted at four hospitals among patients aged 18-45 years. Data were extracted from three-year hospital records. Associations were assessed using chi-square/Fisher's exact tests and logistic regression. 8,650 CVD cases, 2,090 (24.2%) were young adults, predominantly male (64.6%), with a median age of 40 years (IQR: 36-44). ACS was the most common subtype (61.0%), followed by cardiomyopathy (39.0%). Overweight/obesity (77.0%), hypertension (56.5%), smoking (39.7%), dyslipidaemia (21.8%), and diabetes (14.4%) were the most prevalent factors. Compared with ACS, cardiomyopathy was independently associated with high heart rate, hypertension, dyslipidaemia, diabetes, and family history. Smoking was associated with lower odds of cardiomyopathy than ACS (aOR: 0.50, 95% CI: 0.41-0.61, p < 0.001). Young adults accounted for 24.2% of CVD cases, with ACS and cardiomyopathy the most common subtypes, highlighting the need for targeted strategies. The cross-sectional design, findings indicate subtype differences rather than causal effects, while supporting smoking cessation and early hypertension detection in young adults.

items.title: Exposure to childhood adversity and adult alcohol, nicotine, and illicit drug use in Germany: a cross-sectional analysis of the German National Cohort (NAKO)
items.abstract: Rationale: Exposure to adversity in childhood and adolescence (i.e., "early-life stress"; ELS) is a well-established risk factor for substance use. Objectives: The aim of this study was to investigate associations between ELS exposure and substance use across subtypes of ELS, different substance classes, and behavioral profiles of substance use. Methods: In this cross-sectional study, we examined associations between ELS exposure and substance use in a population-based sample of 172,173 adults aged 19-74 years from the German National Cohort (NAKO). ELS exposure was assessed using the Childhood Trauma Screener. Substance use included nicotine, alcohol, and illicit drug use. Associations were examined using regression models evaluating overall ELS exposure, cumulative trauma load, and ELS subtypes. Latent class analysis (LCA) was conducted to identify substance use profiles. Results: ELS exposure was associated with higher odds of smoking, greater smoking severity, heavier alcohol consumption among drinkers, and higher odds of lifetime illicit drug use. Overall, the strongest associations were observed for opioid and stimulant use. Dose-response analyses revealed higher risk with increasing numbers of ELS subtypes. Abuse-related subtypes, particularly exposure to physical and sexual abuse, consistently showed strongest independent associations across substances, whereas neglect exhibited weaker, more variable associations. LCA identified four substance use profiles, with ELS exposure predicting membership in more severe polysubstance classes. Conclusions: ELS emerged as a robust risk factor for adult substance use, underscoring the need for trauma-informed approaches in clinical practice, public health, and policy to mitigate the long-term consequences of early adversity.

items.title: Community-based primary care and inpatient costs and length of stay in Henan, China: retrospective cohort study of 5.9 million older adults
items.abstract: Abstract Background Community-based primary care is a cornerstone for managing chronic disease in ageing populations, but whether prior enrolment is associated with resource use during subsequent admissions is not well established. We examined whether enrolment in China’s National Essential Public Health Services (NEPHS) elderly health management programme before admission was associated with inpatient costs and length of stay among older adults. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study (2019–2024) linking public hospital discharge records, the NEPHS elderly health management registry, and patient identifier files from Henan Province, China. Adults aged 65 years or older with at least one inpatient admission were eligible. The exposure was NEPHS enrolment recorded before the index admission, with management duration categorised as 3 years or less, 4 to 9 years, or 10 years or more. Outcomes were total inpatient costs (log scale) and length of stay, estimated by multivariable linear regression and compared with inverse probability of treatment weighting, overlap weighting, propensity score matching, and within-person fixed effects contrasts. The Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) was examined as a candidate clinical pathway. Results Of 19,425,809 admissions among 5,938,289 patients, 10,377,454 occurred after NEPHS enrolment (mean [SD] age, 73.15 [6.13] years) and 9,048,355 among patients not enrolled (74.89 [7.30] years). In the primary adjusted model, enrolment was associated with 9.9% lower total inpatient costs (95% CI -10.1% to -9.8%) and a 0.68 day shorter length of stay (95% CI -0.70 to -0.66). Weighted and matched estimates were consistent in direction; within-person estimates were smaller (2.6% lower cost). Concurrent CCI accounted for 32.7% of the cost association and 26.9% of the length-of-stay association. Associations were larger with longer management duration and among patients aged 85 years or older, those with a CCI of 3 or greater, and admissions covered by the New Rural Cooperative Medical Scheme. Conclusions Prior NEPHS enrolment was associated with lower per-admission inpatient costs and shorter length of stay, with larger differences among patients with greater comorbidity burden. These are observational associations; prospective or quasi-experimental studies are needed before causal or resource allocation

items.title: Early and accurate prediction of COVID-19 hospitalization risk - methodological framework for pandemic preparedness
items.abstract: Abstract As demonstrated by the public health crisis caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, pandemic preparedness requires rapid identification of early biomarkers predicting need of hospitalization. Furthermore, COVID-19 treatment eligibility is currently determined by patient demographics and pre-existing clinical conditions, but these factors do not provide accurate severity predictions. However, previous research on COVID-19 severity biomarkers has focused on already hospitalized patients. Here, we investigated point-of-care biomarkers capable of accurately predicting COVID-19-related hospitalization risk and disease progression shortly after a positive diagnosis. Previously uninfected non-vaccinated individuals (N=201) were recruited at, or shortly after, SARS-CoV-2 diagnosis, and biochemistry and serum cytokine levels were longitudinally measured. Biomarker combinations were tested by multi-dimensional clustering followed by dimension reduction. The combination of high levels of LDH or serum IL-6 showed the most accurate prediction (sensitivity=100%, specificity=94.5%) for hospitalization risk. The combination of four cytokines (IFN-a, IFN-g, IL-6, IL-8) was the most accurate predictor for moderate versus mild disease. Age and BMI showed significantly lower predictive values for hospitalization risk and were not predictive of mild versus moderate symptoms. Thus, early accurate prediction of COVID-19 hospitalization and severity is possible using biomarkers feasibly measurable at point-of-care, thus allowing optimizing personalized treatment and public health management. The methodology used here sets out a paradigm for severity prediction in the framework of pandemic preparedness.

items.title: From STEM to STEM+S: Integrating Sustainability, Systems Thinking, and Engineering Design in Science Education
items.abstract: As global environmental crises intensify, the limitations of compartmentalized academic disciplines become increasingly apparent in science education. While conventional STEM education excels at fostering technical problem-solving and modeling skills, it frequently marginalizes the ethical, ecological, and systemic dimensions of technological advancement. In response to this critique, this review explores the STEM+S (STEM + Sustainability) framework as a necessary pedagogical evolution aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). By evaluating the theoretical integration of sustainability into STEM curricula, this paper highlights the efficacy of approaches such as design thinking, project-based learning, and socio-scientific issues. Ultimately, we unpack current barriers to teacher preparedness and propose actionable pathways for both future research and classroom implementation.

items.title: Drivers of forest loss and habitat degradation in Zambia’s Greater Kafue Ecosystem
items.abstract: Habitat conversion threatens the Greater Kafue Ecosystem (GKE), Zambia, one of southern Africa’s most important protected-area landscapes, yet its spatial predictors remain poorly quantified. We used a Random Forest classifier to map susceptibility to natural-habitat conversion across Kafue National Park (KNP) and its surrounding Game Management Areas (GMAs). The binary response was derived from Landsat classifications for 1984 and 2024, treating natural-to-anthropogenic cover transitions as conversion and fourteen socio-economic, climatic, topographic, proximity, and conservation predictors were evaluated. Because most predictors are contemporary, the model characterises spatial correlates of cumulative conversion rather than temporal drivers. On an independent, spatially blocked test set ( n = 1,751), it achieved an accuracy of 0.77, AUC-ROC of 0.83, F1-score of 0.81, and Cohen’s Kappa of 0.53, remaining stable under ten-fold spatial cross-validation (accuracy = 0.84 ± 0.07). A higher false-positive rate (0.34) than false-negative rate (0.14) indicated a precautionary bias suited to screening. Percentage cultivated land was the strongest predictor (mean decrease in impurity = 33.6%; univariate AUC = 0.91). Model-derived cut-points near 10% cultivated cover, 0.036 persons ha⁻¹, 4 km from settlements, and 898 mm rainfall discriminated higher- from lower-susceptibility conditions, though these are screening values, not validated ecological thresholds. Susceptibility mapping identified Bilili, Namwala, and Mumbwa as the principal high-susceptibility GMAs, whereas KNP remained predominantly low. The results support targeted monitoring and conservation prioritisation across the GKE and comparable Miombo landscapes.
