items.title: Adverse Childhood Experiences, Emotional-Cognitive Profiles, and Response to Cognitive Remediation and Emotion Skills Training in Anorexia Nervosa.
items.abstract: Anorexia nervosa (AN) involves restrictive eating and marked difficulties in emotion regulation and cognitive flexibility. Cognitive Remediation and Emotion Skills Training (CREST) targets these domains, but outcomes may vary by psychological profile and adverse childhood experiences (ACEs). This study examined the associations of emotional-cognitive profiles and ACEs with treatment response following CREST in inpatients with AN. We studied 198 female inpatients with AN who completed baseline and post-treatment assessments after an 8-week group CREST programme. Cluster analysis of the Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale (DERS), Toronto Alexithymia Scale-20 (TAS-20), Detail and Flexibility Questionnaire (DFLEX), and Obsessive-Compulsive Inventory-Revised (OCI-R) identified subgroups. Outcomes (ΔEDE-Q, ΔDFLEX, ΔTAS, ΔBMI) were compared across clusters. Childhood Trauma Questionnaire (CTQ) subscales were tested in multinomial regression and moderation models. Three clusters emerged: Cluster 1 (low impairment), Cluster 0 (moderate impairment), and Cluster 2 (globally impaired). Groups differed in age, illness duration, BMI, and adversities exposure (all p < 0.05). Psychological outcomes differed: ΔDFLEX (H = 63.7, p < 0.001) and ΔTAS (p < 0.001), with Cluster 2 showing the greatest gains. Emotional abuse was positively associated with both the moderate and globally impaired profiles, whereas physical abuse specifically predicted the globally impaired profile. Sexual abuse was inversely associated with both impaired profiles. Moderation analyses indicated that associations between ACE severity and psychological change varied across emotional-cognitive profiles, with direction and magnitude differing by outcome and ACE subtype. Greater short-term psychological changes were observed in the globally impaired profile, although baseline severity warrants cautious interpretation. Adverse childhood experiences were associated with profile membership and heterogeneous patterns of psychological change across profiles.

items.title: Protocol for integrated phosphoproteomic and proteomic analysis of the mouse ventral tegmental area with functional and kinase motif enrichment.
items.abstract: We present a protocol for label-free proteomic and phosphoproteomic analysis of the mouse ventral tegmental area (VTA). We describe steps for combining region-specific biopsy-punch collection, parallel proteomic and phosphoproteomic processing, liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), and downstream enrichment analysis. We detail procedures for SynGO-based synaptic localization, g:Profiler/DAVID pathway enrichment, and iceLogo/pLogo motif analysis. This protocol enables quantitative assessment of protein abundance, phosphorylation dynamics, and functional interpretation from limited brain region samples. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Diezel et al.1.

items.title: Network-guided Thalamic Neuromodulation for Epilepsy.
items.abstract: This review takes a network-based perspective on thalamic neuromodulation for epilepsy, examining how each target (e.g., anterior (ANT), centromedian (CM), and pulvinar (PUL) thalamic nuclei) engage distinct seizure networks, what evidence supports each, and how stimulation/electrophysiologic mapping can guide individualized targeting rather than a fixed, syndrome-based approach. Randomized and prospective trials have expanded the evidence for ANT and CM stimulation, while emerging data support the pulvinar as a target for posterior quadrant and temporal lobe epilepsies. Syndrome-specific sweet-spot analyses reveal distinct optimal sites within the CM for LGS and IGE. Thalamic sEEG with single-pulse stimulation and trials of DBS-style stimulation now enables characterization of seizure network engagement and identification of acute biomarkers that may inform target and parameter selection. Multi-target strategies combining thalamic nuclei, or thalamic and cortical leads, show preliminary promise for broadly distributed seizure networks. No single thalamic target is uniformly effective across epilepsy types; optimal targeting requires individualized, network-informed characterization. This supports a shift toward connectomic and individualized approaches, with future work needed to refine target selection, stimulation paradigms, and individualized optimization using clinical outcomes and electrophysiological biomarkers.

items.title: Adolescent-onset regular cannabis use is associated with altered neural and behavioural responses during anticipation and feedback of monetary reward and loss.
items.abstract: Regular cannabis use has been associated with alterations in reward-related neural processes, yet findings remain inconsistent and the relationship between neural activity and behavioural performance is not fully understood. The present study aimed to characterise neural and behavioural correlates of reward processing in regular cannabis users (CU) compared with matched non-users (NU) using the Monetary Incentive Delay Task (MIDT). Twenty adolescent-onset regular cannabis users (CU; ≥4 days/week for 2 years, with regular use initiated before age 18) and twenty age- and sex-matched non-users (NU) completed the Monetary Incentive Delay Task during functional MRI. Firstly, we assessed behavioural performance through reaction times, accuracy and monetary earnings to determine whether potential neural alterations were reflected in task performance. Secondly, focusing on reward-related brain regions, we examined group differences in BOLD functional MRI activity during anticipation and outcome phases separately for monetary win and loss conditions. Finally, we explored the association between behavioural performance and neural activation. Our findings provide preliminary evidence that adolescent-onset regular cannabis use is associated with altered engagement of key nodes within the mesocorticolimbic circuit accompanied by impaired behavioural performance. Particularly, compared with NU, CU showed (I) lower striatal activity during anticipation of monetary win and higher ventral striatum and frontal pole activity during anticipation of monetary loss; (II) different VTA BOLD contrast estimates during outcome of successful monetary win and loss avoidance, and lower frontal pole activity during outcome of unsuccessful loss avoidance; (III) lower monetary rewards and a trend towards slower reaction times and reduced accuracy; (IV) disrupted brain-behaviour coupling. Results from this study may help inform future research on the neurobiological mechanisms underlying changes in reward function and the resultant behavioural consequences of adolescent-onset cannabis use.

items.title: Improving the fairness and robustness of deep learning classification models through bias mitigation and post hoc calibration.
items.abstract: The goal of this study was to enhance the fairness and clinical applicability of deep learning models for classifying Alzheimer's disease from structural MRI scans. To achieve this, we addressed two key challenges: age-related bias and unreliable probability estimates. Specifically, we investigated in-processing debiasing strategies to achieve age-invariant predictions while preserving diagnostic accuracy. We also systematically evaluated post hoc calibration methods to improve the reliability, interpretability, and clinical usefulness of predicted probabilities across diverse patient populations. Structural MRI data from three independent cohorts (ADNI, AIBL, and DELCODE) were preprocessed using a standardized pipeline. Age-related bias was addressed using two in-processing strategies, adversarial training (CF-Net) and GLM-based feature residualization (PMDN), implemented in a shared 3D convolutional neural network (CNN) framework. Additionally, post hoc calibration was performed using four regression methods: logistic, probit, isotonic, and Bayesian binning. We evaluated model performance, fairness, and calibration using classification as well as calibration-specific metrics. PMDN achieved the best overall performance, with higher balanced accuracy (0.71) and improved calibration (Brier ≈ 0.22), showing substantially reduced variability compared to baseline and CF-Net. PMDN effectively removed age-related bias, achieving near-zero age prediction correlation; CF-Net, however, showed only partial and unstable debiasing. Post hoc calibration further improved probability reliability, with nonparametric methods (isotonic regression and Bayesian binning) yielding the lowest calibration errors (MCE ≈ 0.21-0.24). This study shows that, although deep learning models achieve similar classification performance, they differ significantly in terms of calibration, stability, and fairness. PMDN provides more consistent and effective age bias mitigation than the CF-Net approach, particularly in clinically relevant subgroups. Post hoc calibration improves probability reliability further, with nonparametric methods achieving the best calibration.

items.title: Imaging findings of sacroiliac joint degeneration are prevalent in asymptomatic adults: a systemic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: The purpose of this study is to determine the prevalence of imaging findings of sacroiliac joint (SIJ) degeneration in asymptomatic adults. All studies reporting the prevalence of cross-sectional imaging findings of SIJ degeneration in asymptomatic adults through May 2026 were included. Pooled prevalence and 95% confidence intervals were calculated using a random-effects model. Heterogeneity was assessed with I2 and Cochran's Q. Age and sex subgroup analyses were performed. Seventeen studies (3873 patients) were included. Any feature of degeneration was observed in 71.1% of patients (95% CI [25.8, 94.6]) with significant heterogeneity among studies (I2 = 96%, p < .01). Osteophyte formation was most prevalent (68.4%; 95% CI [37.5, 88.7], I2 = 92%), followed by joint space narrowing (45.2%; 95% CI [9.8, 86.3], I2 = 99%), subchondral sclerosis (39.1%; 95% CI [11.7, 75.7], I2 = 96%), vacuum phenomenon (14.3%; 95% CI [6.4, 28.7], I2 = 94%), subchondral cyst formation (5.5%; 95% CI [3.0, 9.9], I2 = 59%), erosions (5.0%; 95% CI [2.1, 11.2], I2 = 86%), and joint ankylosis (2.8%; 95% CI [1.2, 6.5], I2 = 66%). There was a correlation between age and osteophytosis, subchondral sclerosis, and vacuum phenomenon. Our study reveals a high prevalence of imaging findings related to SIJ degeneration in asymptomatic adults, which may have a connection with age in several findings. These findings emphasize the importance of correlating imaging with clinical symptoms and physical examination findings in the evaluation of low back pain. Findings should be interpreted with caution because confidence intervals were wide and between-study heterogeneity was high, reflecting differences in imaging modality, lesion definitions, and patient categorization.

items.title: Slow-wave sleep selectively amplifies network signatures of the presumed epileptogenic zone in focal epilepsy.
items.abstract: Slow-wave sleep increases interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) and seizures in focal epilepsy, but how sleep stages reshape epileptogenic tissue remains unclear. We assessed whether sleep stages selectively modulate network properties of the presumed epileptogenic zone (pEZ) relative to irritative (IZ) and non-involved (NIZ) zones. We studied 22 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy undergoing pre-surgical intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG). IED-free resting-state epochs spanned four vigilance stages: wakefulness, non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep stages 2 and 3, and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. Spectral power, functional connectivity, graph-theoretic indices, and the 1/f exponent were quantified across seven frequency bands. Sleep stage and zone interactions were tested using permutation testing. pEZ electrodes were classified using elastic net logistic regression with leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. NREM3 selectively amplified within-pEZ gamma-band synchrony beyond surrounding zones (pEZ-NIZ: d=1.204, P=0.027). pEZ local efficiency and betweenness centrality rose in beta1 and gamma bands versus wakefulness. The aperiodic exponent steepened within the IZ versus NIZ during NREM3 and NREM2 (d =1.452 and 0.87, P < 0.001 and P=0.015). A three-feature classifier (NREM3 aperiodic exponent, beta2 connectivity, gamma local efficiency) localised the pEZ without ictal recordings (median AUC 0.859 pEZ vs. non-pEZ). Slow-wave sleep selectively unmasks pEZ network properties via amplified power, synchrony and hub topology. NREM3-derived multimodal features may complement conventional pre-surgical biomarkers. Prospective validation in larger cohorts is needed to determine whether these markers improve surgical planning and outcome prediction.

items.title: From spatial bias to temporal integration: Anorthoscopy neutralizes pseudoneglect.
items.abstract: The present study investigated interaction between spatio-temporal integration under conditions of sensory impoverishment, "anorthoscopic viewing", and the lateralized spatial biases, such as pseudoneglect, aiming to clarify whether such asymmetries originate from early perceptual mechanisms or from intrinsic properties of high-level neural representations. A 64-object array, organized in 2 × 6, was presented in two experiments: (1) anorthoscopic viewing (stimuli were presented sliding behind a static aperture) and (2) the whole condition. Participants were asked to recall as many items as possible for each trial in both experiments. Results demonstrate a robust pseudoneglect effect in Experiment 2, characterized by significantly higher recall for items on the left side of the arrays compared to the right. Pseudoneglect was absent in the anorthoscopic condition. Notably, while the recall of left-sided items decreased during the anorthoscopic session, performance for right-sided objects remained statistically stable across both experiments. These findings indicate that anorthoscopic procedure doesn't impair performance through generic degradation or excessive cognitive load. Because attentional and mnemonic factors interact, these results should be interpreted as reflecting an interplay between the two mechanisms. Accordingly, we suggest that pseudoneglect is not an intrinsic property of static internal mental representations, but a dynamic consequence of active visual scanning.

items.title: Neurofilaments in cerebrospinal fluid and/or serum as a possible biomarker of pediatric spinal muscular atrophy.
items.abstract: BackgroundSpinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a severe, genetically determined neuromuscular disorder characterised by progressive muscle weakness resulting from motor neuron degeneration. Although therapies such as nusinersen have altered disease trajectories, objective biomarkers for treatment monitoring remain lacking. Neurofilament proteins, particularly phosphorylated neurofilament heavy chain (pNFH), are promising candidates for this role.ObjectivesTo evaluate pNFH levels in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and serum as potential biomarkers for monitoring treatment response to nusinersen in paediatric patients with SMA.MethodsThis two-center observational study involved 56 SMA patients (types I-III) treated with nusinersen and 30 age-matched controls. pNFH concentrations in CSF and serum were measured at predefined intervals using ELISA kits. Motor function was assessed with CHOP INTEND, HFMSE, or MFM scales at baseline and after 3, 6, and 12 months. Mixed linear regression modeling evaluated changes in neurofilament levels and motor function.ResultsBaseline pNFH levels in both CSF and serum were significantly higher in SMA patients compared to controls. Following nusinersen therapy, pNFH levels decreased significantly in both compartments, especially in the first 6 months. Younger patients had higher initial serum pNFH levels. A significant correlation was found between CSF and serum pNFH concentration. An association between pNFH levels and motor scores was observed.ConclusionspNFH levels in CSF and serum show potential as objective biomarkers for monitoring the initial treatment response in paediatric SMA. Longitudinal changes are more informative than single measurements. Further validation in larger cohorts and using more sensitive methods is warranted.

items.title: Lymphocytosis as a biomarker for natalizumab treatment response in multiple sclerosis: The link with anti-drug antibodies.
items.abstract: Natalizumab is a high-efficacy therapy drug for multiple sclerosis that inhibits lymphocyte migration into the central nervous system, increasing lymphocyte counts in the peripheral blood. Anti-drug antibody responses may limit drug efficacy, but current guidance recommends anti-drug antibody testing only after evidence of 'reduced efficacy'. To assess the lack of relative lymphocytosis as a biomarker of anti-drug antibody responses. Lymphocyte counts and immunogenicity data from the pivotal AFFIRM clinical trial (n = 627 natalizumab vs n = 315 placebo) and real-world data from the Cardiff MS register (n = 185) were analysed to assess the relationship between lymphocyte counts, anti-drug antibody responses, drug levels and disease activity. Natalizumab treatment induced an absolute change in lymphocyte counts by week 12 (1.40 ± 0.92 vs -0.05 ± 0.62 × 109 cells/L in natalizumab vs placebo; p < 0.0001) that was absent in the persistent anti-drug antibody group (-0.12 ± 0.60 × 109 cells/L). Increases in lymphocyte counts by ⩾ 0.8 × 109 cells/L from the baseline discriminated individuals without anti-drug antibody responses with high sensitivity (≥ 84%) and specificity (≥ 91%). The absence of relative lymphocytosis is associated with anti-drug antibody responses and may provide a simple biomarker to prompt anti-drug antibody testing before disease breakthrough occurs.

items.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted categorization of interictal abnormalities in adult long-term electroencephalographic monitoring: Comparable diagnostic accuracy with marked efficiency gain.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) classifies routine electroencephalograms (EEGs) with expert-level accuracy, but interpretation of long-term EEG monitoring (LTM) remains reliant on time-intensive visual review. We evaluated whether autoSCORE, a clinically approved implementation of SCORE-AI integrated into an EEG reader, achieves expert-level diagnostic accuracy for LTM interpretation and whether expert-supervised use reduces review time versus conventional analysis. A fixed-and-frozen AI model was tested on an independent single-center dataset of 78 adult patient LTM recordings (52 normal, 26 abnormal), with epilepsy monitoring unit discharge diagnosis as the external reference standard. The AI model was benchmarked against two expert panels (three readers each); Panel 1 reviewed autoSCORE EEG detections (hybrid approach), and Panel 2 interpreted full recordings (conventional approach). Diagnostic accuracy and time to diagnostic decision were assessed for fully automated, hybrid, and conventional approaches. Interrater reliability (Gwet's AC1) was evaluated for hybrid and conventional interpretation. Interrater reliability was significantly higher for hybrid than conventional approach (AC1 = .81, 95% confidence interval [CI] = .73-.89 vs. AC1 = .43, 95% CI = .32-.53; p .99). Hybrid approach diagnostic accuracy was significantly greater than fully automated analysis (.75, 95% CI = .66-.83 vs. .55, 95% CI = .44-.65; adjusted p < .001). Expert oversight of AI-assisted categorization of interictal epileptiform and nonepileptiform EEG abnormalities improves interrater reliability and efficiency, increases diagnostic sensitivity versus conventional interpretation, and increases diagnostic accuracy versus fully automated analysis in adult LTM.

items.title: Multimodal modeling of the ictal onset zone in refractory insular epilepsy and seizure outcome of magnetic resonance-guided laser interstitial therapy: A pediatric single-center retrospective study.
items.abstract: This study was undertaken to evaluate seizure outcomes after magnetic resonance-guided laser interstitial thermal therapy (MRgLITT) in children with insular epilepsy and to assess how the extent of ablation overlaps with multimodal definitions of the ictal onset zone (IOZ). We conducted a retrospective, single-center study including consecutive pediatric patients treated with MRgLITT for insular epilepsy. All patients underwent presurgical evaluation including electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI); fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) and stereo-EEG (SEEG) were performed in negative-MRI cases. Epileptic zone was identified by visual analysis of SEEG recording. Postablation contrast-enhancing volumes were manually segmented and coregistered with IOZ estimates derived from Multi-centre Epilepsy Lesion Detection (MELD) MRI analysis, FDG-PET voxel-based analysis, and the Epileptogenicity Index, when available. Spatial concordance between modalities was assessed using Dice similarity coefficients, and the proportion of each IOZ modality encompassed within the ablation volume was correlated with postoperative seizure outcomes (International League Against Epilepsy classification). Eight children (median age = 10.4 years, range = 2.3-17) were included, with a median postoperative follow-up of 38 months. Two patients had insular tumors, and both achieved seizure freedom after complete ablation. Among the six MRI-negative patients, FDG-PET revealed insular hypometabolism in four, MELD detected a median of one insular cluster (range 1-3), and SEEG identified focal insular ictal activity in three cases. Overall, four negative-MRI patients achieved seizure freedom: three after MRgLITT alone and one after MRgLITT combined with frontal opercular resection. One transient postoperative aphasia was observed. Intermodality spatial concordance was low across all comparisons. A greater proportion of FDG-PET hypometabolism included in the ablation volume was associated with better seizure outcomes (p = .012). MRgLITT is an effective and safe treatment option for focal insular epilepsy in children, either as standalone therapy or in a combined approach. Optimal outcome depends on accurate preoperative delineation of the IOZ and its complete ablation.

items.title: Local-Global Spherical Sliced Wasserstein Graph Kernel for Schizophrenia Identification.
items.abstract: Accurate identification of schizophrenia (SZ) using functional connectivity (FC) is fundamentally challenged by the non-Euclidean geometry of neuroimaging data and information loss from arbitrary graph thresholding. To overcome these bottlenecks, this study proposes the local-global spherical sliced Wasserstein graph (LG-SSWG) kernel. By embedding FC profiles onto a hyperspherical manifold, the proposed framework utilizes geodesic optimal transport to construct a mathematically rigorous, positive-definite graph kernel. This threshold-free approach synergistically integrates macroscopic whole-brain topology and region-specific functional architectures. Evaluated on the public COBRE dataset, LG-SSWG achieves a superior 84% accuracy, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art baselines. Beyond predictive accuracy, the method exhibits strong clinical interpretability by identifying critical neuroanatomical biomarkers, particularly the left thalamus and right precuneus. Network analysis reveals pervasive functional hyperconnectivity within subcortical relays and cognitive networks in SZ patients. Notably, this hyperconnectivity correlates positively with PANSS positive symptom scores. Consequently, these altered thalamocortical and precuneus-anchored circuits indicate that SZ clinical symptoms may be closely associated with disrupted sensory gating and functional segregation. Ultimately, the LG-SSWG kernel provides a principled geometric learning tool that advances both the objective diagnosis and mechanistic understanding of schizophrenia.

items.title: A self-organizing developmental framework for the head direction ring attractor.
items.abstract: The head direction (HD) system provides a continuous representation of the animal's facing direction and is a core component of the spatial navigation network. Although mature HD circuits have been studied extensively, their developmental origin remains unclear, particularly because young animals already show attractor-like internal coherence before stable visual anchoring is established. Here we propose a developmental computational framework of the lateral mammillary nucleus and dorsal tegmental nucleus (LMN-DTN) circuit, in which a functional HD ring attractor emerges through staged self-organization without preconfigured topology or early external supervision. In the model, a randomly connected LMN network first generates stable travelling waves through relative refractoriness. These waves provide a temporal scaffold for subsequent learning. Local STDP-like and structural plasticity then consolidate wave-based statistics into locally enhanced recurrent connectivity, followed by direction-selective shift-feedback learning in the DTN→LMN pathway. At a later stage, recruited long-range inhibition transforms the travelling-wave manifold into a stable single activity profile (bump) attractor. Visual input acts mainly as a late calibration signal for global integration gain: it improves short-timescale path integration, but does not remove long-term drift. The framework provides a testable account of the developmental dissociation between early internal organization and later sensory anchoring. More broadly, it suggests that key components of classical ring attractor models, including local recurrent structure, direction-selective shift feedback, and late stabilizing mechanisms, can arise through a staged developmental process rather than relying on a preconfigured network architecture.

items.title: Leveraging Preclinical Models to Understand Human Neurobiology and Behavior.
items.abstract: Rodent models have become indispensable tools for investigating the neurobiological mechanisms underlying human behavior and disease. Despite the substantial phenotypic differences between rodents and humans, shared evolutionary history, conserved genomic architecture, and analogous neural circuitry allow preclinical findings to meaningfully inform our understanding of human conditions. This chapter reviews the behavioral paradigms most commonly used to evaluate five core domains in rodent models: motor function, stress and anxiety-like behavior, repetitive and restrictive behaviors, social behavior, and learning and memory. For each domain, we describe established assays, discuss the underlying innate behaviors they leverage, and highlight examples in which preclinical data have advanced mechanistic understanding or therapeutic development for human neuropsychiatric and neurodevelopmental disorders. We emphasize that behavioral findings must be interpreted with careful precision, as rodent behaviors are not direct equivalents of humans' intentional, complex behaviors or human emotional states but rather analogous outputs of neural circuits that can be operationally quantified. Throughout this chapter, we highlight critical considerations for rigor and reproducibility, an ongoing issue in the preclinical rodent behavioral space, such as the influence of environment; the appropriate selection of control groups; the importance of litter effects and background strain; and sex as a biological variable. Taken together, this chapter provides both a practical guide to preclinical behavioral neuroscience and a framework for maximizing the translational value of animal model research.

items.title: The Importance of Translational Research for Neurodevelopmental Disorders and Autism Spectrum Disorders.
items.abstract: Translational research is the process of transforming fundamental biological discoveries into safe and efficacious interventions for patients. This specialized field is of particular importance for neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), a broad class of behaviorally defined conditions including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDDs), and related disorders. NDDs present unique translational challenges including (i) a lack of biological diagnostic markers; (ii) the fact that they are diagnosed exclusively by behavioral criteria; (iii) their involvement of dysfunction in complex brain circuitry; and (iv) that there is no single unifying biological mechanism. This chapter reviews the current landscape of translational neuroscience for NDDs, examining the strengths and limitations of preclinical model systems, including rodent models humanized mice, human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) 3D spheroids and brain organoids. This work emphasizes that research emanating from the varying preclinical experimental systems above should be leveraged and their complementary strengths integrated, coordinated, and considered collaboratively, to strengthen current knowledge, identify the remaining research gaps, and prioritize future research. We also emphasize the importance of rigorous, reproducible methodology and conservative interpretation of behavioral and functional outcomes. Discussion is presented on key translational bridges or connections that are urgently required to advance the field: bridging non-human model systems to humanized models, identifying and validating translational biomarkers, bridging in vitro and in vivo findings, and developing corroborative alternatives to animal models. It is our stance that integrating multiple complementary model systems, limiting erroneous behavioral inferences, relying on evolutionarily conserved circuits, and prioritizing robust and reproducible outcome measures will reduce failures in the translational pipeline and accelerate the development of meaningful therapies for individuals with NDDs.

items.title: Allocentric navigation is computationally universal.
items.abstract: I present three proofs that idealized neurocomputational architectures capable of navigation guided by allocentric maps with landmark structure can be computationally universal. Navigation may occur online, in the environment, or offline, in the animal's head. The first proof encodes the counters of a two-counter machine as positions of movable markers on orthogonal axes. The second directly simulates a one-tape Turing machine using a writable tape-path embedded in the map. The third realizes the tape-path's predecessor/successor relation through local cues at a two-row landmark track rather than through a globally indexed path primitive. I establish universality in two senses: each class of navigation models is Turing-complete, and each contains a single machine that simulates every machine in its class. These constructions are mathematically close to classical graph-based models, including Kolmogorov-Uspensky machines, storage-modification machines, and graph Turing machines, so the bare computability results are unsurprising. My contribution is to reconstruct them explicitly within an allocentric cognitive-map architecture whose representational and computational primitives are drawn from empirical and theoretical work on spatial navigation and cognitive control. This shows that an allocentric navigation-based architecture can be computationally universal and opens the possibility of reconstructing aspects of biological cognition, including symbolic processing, in navigation-based terms.

items.title: The dual role of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR axis in glial cell survival and neuroinflammation.
items.abstract: Multiple sclerosis is characterized by a triad of inflammation, demyelination, and neurodegeneration, yet current disease-modifying therapies are limited in their ability to halt progressive neurodegeneration or promote remyelination. The PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway is a master regulator of these divergent cellular processes and therefore represents a biological paradox in multiple sclerosis. In the pathogenic facet of the disease, activation of this axis supports the differentiation and effector functions of pro-inflammatory T- and B-cells and contributes to inflammatory programs in microglia and macrophages. In the regenerative facet, physiological PI3K/AKT/mTOR activity is required for oligodendrocyte precursor-cell survival, differentiation, myelin synthesis, and maintenance of myelin integrity. Astrocytic signaling adds another layer of context-dependence, with pathway activity influencing reactive gliosis and the inflammatory or reparative properties of the lesion environment. Consequently, systemic inhibition of the pathway may suppress neuroinflammation while simultaneously interfering with endogenous repair. This review therefore considers PI3K/AKT/mTOR axis according to these opposing pathogenic and protective functions, highlighting the importance of cell type, disease stage, and treatment timing. Precision strategies capable of selectively suppressing inflammatory signaling while preserving or restoring pro-regenerative activity, potentially through cell-specific molecular targets, may provide a more rational therapeutic approach than generalized pathway inhibition.

items.title: Reinforcement learning deficits in at-risk mental state for psychosis: the role of primary negative symptoms.
items.abstract: Negative symptoms such as amotivation begin to emerge in the at-risk mental state for psychosis (ARMS), and in some cases, these symptoms are idiopathic (i.e., primary negative symptoms, PNS). While deficits in reinforcement learning (RL) are evident in patients with first-episode and chronic schizophrenia and are associated with the severity of negative symptoms, whether these deficits are present during ARMS warrants further investigation. Additionally, it is unclear whether these deficits, especially those driven by rewards, are particularly characteristic of ARMS individuals with PNS. This study compared 97 ARMS individuals and 37 healthy controls (HC) on probabilistic RL. We then compared ARMS individuals with PNS (n = 15), those without PNS (n = 82), and HC on probabilistic RL. Reward- and punishment-driven RL (both trial-by-trial and procedural) and value-guided choice were assessed using two probabilistic RL tasks: Go/NoGo (GNG) and Gain vs. Loss-Avoidance (GLA) tasks. Compared with HC, ARMS individuals showed impairments in overall procedural RL on both RL tasks, as well as subtle, task-specific alterations in value-guided choice. Furthermore, ARMS-PNS individuals, relative to HC, showed particular deficits in reward-driven RL (trial-to-trial RL on GLA task and procedural RL on both tasks), as well as impaired positive expected value representations to guide decision-making on GLA task. Extending the results in patients with established psychosis, our findings indicate that deficits in RL exist before the onset of a psychotic disorder. With a modest sample of ARMS-PNS individuals, preliminary evidence suggests that deficits in reward-driven RL may be more specific to PNS.

items.title: Spontaneous spiking in photoreceptors of Periplaneta americana.
items.abstract: Insect photoreceptors are non-spiking neurons that encode visual information with graded voltage responses produced by stochastic activation of the phototransduction cascade in the microvilli. However, light-evoked, voltage-gated sodium channel (Na V ) dependent axonal spikes have been reported in several species, where they are thought to support downstream signal transmission. Here we report a new mode of electrical activity in rhabdomeric photoreceptors: spontaneous trains of small, fast spikes appearing in darkness immediately after piercing the membrane. These spike trains differed from both quantum bumps and conventional axonal spikes. They occurred without light stimulation, persisted for tens of seconds to minutes, exhibited several millivolt amplitudes, and had kinetics and waveforms resembling Na V -dependent regenerative action potentials. Several lines of evidence indicated that spikes are generated in distal parts of the axon. First, spiking was suppressed by off-axis illumination that produced minimal somatic hyperpolarization, consistent with the effects of lateral interactions on axon terminals in the neuropil. Second, observation of spike superposition indicated that they can arise from multiple electrotonically separated loci and summate at the soma, suggesting distal, spatially separated spike-generating sites. Third, while spiking was sensitive to experimentally imposed changes in somatic membrane potential, spike frequency and duration often changed spontaneously and independently of it. Spiking spontaneously and irreversibly terminated through a gradual decline in spike frequency and often amplitude, consistent with a progressive reduction in Na V channel availability. Our results suggest that spontaneous spike trains reflect a transient shift in axonal excitability, possibly triggered by electrical perturbations associated with membrane penetration.

items.title: Drought-induced plant dominance shift amplifies functional niche differentiation in steppe communities.
items.abstract: Trait-based studies on community assembly under environmental change often overlook intraspecific trait variation (ITV), despite its considerable role in modulating community dynamics, which may largely mislead the inference of community assembly. Under simulated extreme droughts in a temperate steppe, we integrated ITV and interspecific trait variation for four key traits, plant height (Height), specific leaf area (SLA), leaf dry matter content (LDMC), and leaf thickness (LT), to examine how drought alters functional niche structure and underlying processes. Drought shifted communities toward conservative resource-use strategies, reduced community variation in LT, and interspecific trait overlap in terms of SLA, LDMC, LT, and the multivariate trait space, whereas community-level ITV remained stable across all traits. These changes were driven primarily by diversity loss and increases in the dominance of fewer species, with negligible effects of intraspecific trait plasticity or species turnover. Communities with fewer but more dominant species exhibited smaller trait overlap. Our findings advance our understanding of the paradigm of trait convergence under environmental filtering. Drought-induced diversity loss amplifies functional niche differentiation, underscoring the critical role of species reorganization through dominance shifts, with little evidence for intraspecific trait plasticity in mediating community assembly under climate extremes.

items.title: Targeted pathway mining reveals novel modified hexapeptides from the demiguisin family.
items.abstract: Following the discovery of the piperazic acid (Piz)-containing hexapeptide demiguisin A from a toxic bird-associated Amycolatopsis strain, we aimed to investigate the structural diversity and bioactive potential of this natural product family. Here, we used the dmg biosynthetic gene cluster from Amycolatopsis sp. PS_44_ISF1 as a pathway mining probe to search for alternative demiguisin A producers. A global search identified only one other soil-derived Amycolatopsis sp. NBC_01488, encoding a highly syntenic pathway. Under feather-mimicking conditions, PS_44_ISF1 demonstrated enhanced growth and metabolite production relative to NBC_01488. Despite phylogenomic distance, both strains produced shared metabolites, while NBC_01488 yielded more abundant demiguisins, enabling the isolation of five novel derivatives characterized by two Piz-moieties with different hydroxylation patterns and glycine truncation. Two congeners displayed potent activity against the avian pathogen Mycobacterium intracellulare and moderate activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis. These findings show that targeted pathway mining guided the expansion of the chemical diversity of Piz-modifications and demiguisin congeners with promising anti-Mycobacterium activity.

items.title: Collinear genes and karyotype evolution resolve the phylogenetic uncertainty of biebersteiniaceae within sapindales.
items.abstract: The phylogenetic placement of the herbaceous family Biebersteiniaceae, a monotypic lineage with an exceptionally low chromosome number (2n = 10), has remained contentious within the order Sapindales, particularly regarding the relationships among Biebersteiniaceae, Sapindaceae, and Nitrariaceae. To address this, we generated a chromosome-level genome assembly for Biebersteinia heterostemon. Phylogenetic analyses based on single-copy nuclear genes and plastome sequences yielded strongly conflicting topologies. In contrast, a species tree reconstructed from collinear genes supported a third, well-defined topology: Biebersteiniaceae is sister to a subclade comprising Anacardiaceae, Meliaceae, and Rutaceae that further is sister to the subclade comprising only Sapindaceae. We further reconstructed the ancestral karyotype of Sapindales and traced karyotype evolution across the order. Reconstruction of ancestral karyotypes revealed that Anacardiaceae, Meliaceae, and Rutaceae share a chromosomal fusion supporting their monophyly. Biebersteiniaceae shares an additional fusion with this subclade, supporting its sister relationship. Furthermore, Biebersteiniaceae, Anacardiaceae, Meliaceae, Rutaceae, and Sapindaceae share another fusion that is absent from Nitrariaceae, suggesting that Nitrariaceae represents the earliest-diverging lineage among these families. Our study demonstrates that integrated phylogenomics based on collinear genes and karyotype evolution can resolve long-standing deep phylogenetic conflicts where traditional analyses fail, providing a robust framework for understanding trait evolution.

items.title: Impacts of plastic type and surface properties on periphyton biovolume and composition under contrasting nutrient and temperature scenarios in shallow lake mesocosms.
items.abstract: Plastics have become pervasive pollutants in aquatic ecosystems, acting not only as contaminants but also as novel substrates for organism colonization. Periphyton communities are highly sensitive to environmental disturbance such as eutrophication and climate warming, which may interact with plastic surfaces to alter ecosystem structure and function. In this study, we examined the combined effects of temperature (ambient, +3 °C, +4.5 °C), nutrient levels (low, high), polymer type, and surface roughness on periphyton development using outdoor mesocosms, running since 2003. Warming and nutrient enrichment exerted strong and interactive effects on periphyton biovolume and community composition. Biovolume increased under both stressors, plateauing at the higher temperature level. Substrate roughness promoted biovolume accrual, particularly on highly roughened surfaces (R2), whereas polymer type had no significant effect. Community composition was primarily driven by temperature and nutrient levels, with Oedogonium, Closterium, and Fragilaria accounting for up to 70% of the compositional dissimilarity between treatments. Warming favored thermotolerant taxa such as Achnanthidium, Fragilaria, and Gongrosira, whereas Closterium and Gomphonema dominated under ambient temperature conditions. Under high nutrient conditions, generalist taxa such as Gongrosira and Cocconeis were predominant. Overall, our results demonstrate that warming and eutrophication jointly enhance periphyton biovolume on plastics, suggesting that the persistence of plastics in natural waters may reinforce periphyton colonization and alter aquatic ecosystem dynamics under global change.

items.title: Lignosulfonate-derived sulfur functionalization of bimetallic Ni/Co-MOF for effective removal of Hg(II) from wastewater.
items.abstract: The high toxicity and persistence of mercury (Hg(II)) severely threaten the safety of aquatic environments. In this study, a strategy based on sodium lignosulfonate (Na-LS) functionalized Ni/Co-MOF was proposed, successfully constructing a series of sulfur-doped lignin-MOF composite adsorbents (LS-Ni/Co-MOF). The introduction of Na-LS enabled efficient sulfur doping, which significantly enhanced the Hg(II) adsorption performance of the resulting composites. Batch adsorption experiments at 298 K showed that the Langmuir model calculated the maximum Hg(II) adsorption capacity of 0.5-LS-Ni/Co-MOF, 0.75-LS-Ni/Co-MOF, and 1-LS-Ni/Co-MOF to be 781.7, 799.7, and 802.1 mg g-1, respectively, with equilibrium attained within 60 min at an initial concentration of 100 mg L-1. Furthermore, LS-Ni/Co-MOF exhibited highly selective adsorption toward Hg(II) over various competing ions, including Ca(II), Al(III), Pb(II), Cd(II), Mg(II), Co(II), Ni(II), Zn(II), and Mn(II). The Kd values for Hg(II) reached 349237.3, 450760.9 and 471704.5 L g-1 for 0.5-LS-Ni/Co-MOF, 0.75-LS-Ni/Co-MOF, and 1-LS-Ni/Co-MOF, respectively. After five consecutive adsorption-desorption cycles, the Hg(II) removal efficiency remained above 70%. Dynamic column tests showed a 50% breakthrough time of 3120 min, demonstrating great potential for practical application. In real wastewater, the materials achieved a removal efficiency of 90% for Hg(II). Finally, Spectroscopic analysis and DFT calculations revealed that the adsorption mechanism involves a coordination interaction between the surface hydroxyl and sulfonate groups and Hg(II). This work provides a promising materials design pathway for the functional utilization of lignin and the purification of heavy metal-contaminated wastewater.

items.title: Privileged in-situ deposited MnO x mediates efficient inorganic nitrogen removal during the treatment of actual mine-tailing wastewater in single-chamber microbial electrolysis cells.
items.abstract: Sustainable, cost-effective and stable single-chamber microbial electrolysis cells (MECs) for the treatment of typical actual mine-tailing wastewater (MTW) containing ternary components of dissolved manganese, inorganic nitrogen (NH4+-N and NO3--N) meeting the China national discharge standards of pollutants from the rare earths industry are demonstrated over 100 days fed-batch operation. The MECs inoculated with anammox granular sludge initially induced Mn removal and privileged the in-situ deposition of oxygen vacancies (Ov) rich nanoscale manganese oxides (MnOx) over the graphite felt electrodes. The deposited MnOx mediated, more preferentially, the biotic (rather than the electrochemical) conversion of inorganic nitrogen (NH4+-N: 91.3%; NO3--N: 92.3%; total N: 93.6%) with a 100% selectivity to N2, achieving appreciable increments (NH4+-N: 54.5-fold and 1.3-time; NO3--N: 3.4-time and 5.1-fold; total N: 8.7-fold and 1.9-time) over the abiotic controls and the open circuital conditions, respectively. The nitrogen removal processes were driven more influentially by bioanodic oxidation due to the greater variety of nanoscale MnOx deposited over the bioanodes presenting greater Ov. Moreover, the harboring of higher cytochrome b and riboflavin within the bioanodic extracellular polymeric substances with more exoproteins contributed to these processes, besides the properties of specific bioanodic and biocathodic microbial communities. The calcination of the MnOx deposited bioelectrodes and their reuse, confirmed a solid framework for further system development. Overall, this study explores new cost-effective and stable processes for treating actual MTW (containing dissolved manganese, NH4+-N and NO3--N) with simultaneous recovery/reuse of manganese, contributing to the sustainability of mineral mining and processing industries.

items.title: Genome-centric metagenomic analysis revealed the microbial superiority of the developed anaerobic digestion startup strategy based on combination of raw and concentrated digestate.
items.abstract: Concentrating the digestate as inoculum to initiate new anaerobic digestion (AD) reactors has been proven to be feasible. However, functional microorganisms after centrifugal concentration have poor activity in the initial stage, resulting in a long startup period. In this study, AD was initiated through addition of centrifugal concentrated digestate combined with different proportions of raw digestate (0%, 9%, 18%, and 27%, in terms of total working volume), aiming to restore the metabolic activity rapidly with a minimum amount of raw digestate to reduce the startup cost. The result showed that Cen-18% (bioaugmentation of 18% raw digestate on the top of concentrated digestate) was the most suitable startup strategy in terms of methane production rate and methane yield. Metagenomic absolute quantitative analysis revealed that methane metabolism (ko00680) was enhanced in Cen-18% (2.9 × 1010 copies/g V.S. (1.5-1.8) × 1010 copies/g in other groups) along with the AD progress by upregulating the abundance of key functional genes in carbohydrate metabolism (gapA, fbaA and eno) and amino acid metabolism (carB, argG and argH). Moreover, genome-centric metagenomic analysis implied that the Cen-18% accelerated carbon conversion by enriching higher abundance of the identified key carbohydrate and protein degraders (i.e., Bacteroidales_MAG2 and Bacteroidales_MAG8) in Cen-18% than other experimental groups. Hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis performed by Methanomicrobiales_MAG1 and Methanomicrobiales_MAG2 was the dominant methanogenic pathway in Cen-18%, which was highly symbiotic with the acetate oxidation bacteria DUMP01_MAG3, DUMP01_MAG1, and Thermosediminibacterales_MAG2. This study provides practical support for the startup of newly built biogas digesters.

items.title: Embryonic exposure to polystyrene nanoplastics alters developmental, antioxidant and metabolic responses without detectable short-term behavioral impairment in Plestiodon chinensis.
items.abstract: Terrestrial soils are major sinks for nanoplastics, threatening soil-dwelling oviparous reptiles that lay permeable eggs. The present study investigated the effects of embryonic exposure to an environmentally relevant dose of polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs; 1 mg/L) during incubation in the Chinese skink (Plestiodon chinensis). PS-NPs penetrated eggshells and accumulated in embryos, slowing egg growth, prolonging incubation, triggering oxidative stress, and altering immune-related responses. Crucially, the oxidative stress response was associated with different developmental stages, reflecting the lower functional capacity of early-stage antioxidant systems that rely heavily on non-enzymatic defenses. In contrast, no significant differences were detected in hatchling locomotor performance, boldness, or activity under the behavioral conditions tested. Untargeted metabolomic profiling further identified differences in several important metabolites in hatchlings exposed to PS-NPs. Collectively, these findings indicate that embryonic exposure to PS-NPs is associated with measurable changes to developmental, antioxidant and metabolic responses, while not producing detectable short-term behavioral impairment under the conditions tested in this study. Notably, this study provides the first evidence that antioxidant responses to nanoplastic exposure differ between developmental stages in reptiles. This offers novel insights into the physiological vulnerabilities of oviparous wildlife to soil pollution, and highlights the need to incorporate multiple developmental stages when conducting risk assessments for environmental contamination.

items.title: Perceived social support and mental health among shidu parents: The moderating role of stigma following the loss of an only child.
items.abstract: Perceived social support is a psychosocial resource that protects the mental health of parents who have lost an only child (shidu parents), but its benefits likely vary depending on stigma-a challenge that these parents face in social contexts. We used data from 482 shidu parents (Mage = 66.63, SDage = 6.88) who reported perceived support (overall and by specific source, family, peer, and others), depressive symptoms, perceived stigma, and demographic characteristics. Linear regressions showed that family support and others support were negatively associated with depressive symptoms, consistent with the finding for overall perceived support, whereas peer support was not in the main-effect analysis. Perceived stigma consistently moderated associations with depressive symptoms across overall and source-specific support: social support was negatively associated with depressive symptoms when stigma was low, but not when stigma was high. These findings refine our understanding of social support and inform stigma-reduction to maximize its psychological benefits for shidu parents.

items.title: Transport of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in DOM-influenced complex groundwater systems: Insights into aromatic ring number and π-electron characteristics.
items.abstract: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH) contamination in groundwater is a global environmental and public health concern, strongly influenced by dissolved organic matter (DOM) and geochemical conditions. In DOM-rich and redox-active groundwater systems, coupled physicochemical and microbial processes regulate PAHs transport, yet the relationships between molecular characteristics and transport behavior under such geochemical conditions remain poorly understood. Herein, we investigated the coupled processes of sorption, transport, and biodegradation of naphthalene (NAP, 2-ring) and phenanthrene (PHE, 3-ring) across molecular to pore scales, from the perspectives of aromatic ring number and π-electron characteristics. Specifically, PHE exhibited slower transport than NAP, with higher retardation factors (R = 4.38 vs. 2.94), consistent with its stronger sorption affinity (KF = 2.96 vs. 0.23 at 318 K). Molecular simulations suggested that enhanced π-electron delocalization of PHE increased electrostatic polarization and interactions with hydrated metal species ([Fe(H2O)6]3+ and [Mn(H2O)6]2+), resulting in stronger adsorption energies (-65.56 to -60.13 vs. -57.13 to -56.92 kJ mol-1), shorter interaction distances (2.08 Å vs. 2.22 Å), and lower diffusion coefficients (0.031 vs. 0.077 Å2 ps-1) compared to NAP. Under DOM-influenced conditions, PAHs transport exhibited scale-dependent behavior: π-mediated interactions with DOM and hydrated metal species were associated with reduced molecular mobility at the molecular-scale, whereas DOM-associated processes may facilitate PAHs co-transport at the pore-scale. Anaerobic enrichment of Desulfosporosinus and Trichoderma was associated with enhanced microbial biodegradation of PAHs. Overall, this study provides new insights into contaminant transport behavior, contributing to improved prediction, risk assessment, and groundwater management in complex groundwater systems.

items.title: Thermal stress induces dual damages to physiology and reproductive capacity of Galaxea fascicularis during its reproductive stage.
items.abstract: Driven by ocean warming and intensifying marine heatwaves, increasingly frequent and severe coral bleaching events are causing declines in coral populations worldwide. Post-disturbance coral population recovery relies heavily on sexual reproduction, yet this reproductive process often sustains long-term detrimental impacts under thermal stress. Here, we investigated the effects of varying degrees of thermal stress on physiological function and reproductive capacity, as well as the underlying molecular responses in the heat-resistant coral Galaxea fascicularis. Our results showed that even 7 days at 29 °C induced mild coral bleaching accompanied by significant declines in physiological performance and sexual reproductive capacity, highlighting the vulnerability of corals during their reproductive period. KEGG enrichment analysis of the coral host transcriptome indicated that glutathione metabolism, peroxisome, and the TCA cycle were significantly enriched for upregulated genes. Meanwhile, the Symbiodiniaceae community shifted from clade C17 to C1, with a high abundance of thermotolerant microbes of the family Rhodothermaceae. Together, these changes might indicate the recovery potential of mildly bleached corals. However, when thermal stress intensified to 32 °C, there was a massive loss of symbiotic Symbiodiniaceae, severe depletion of energy reserves, and significant reductions in oocyte size and abundance. Downregulated genes were significantly enriched in the base excision repair and mRNA surveillance pathways, which may predict the emergence of irreversible cellular damage. Findings of this study advance our understanding of how broadcast-spawning G. fascicularis responds to varying degrees of thermal stress, and highlight the necessity of assessing environmental tolerance in corals during the reproductive period.

items.title: Smart Piezoelectric Hybrid Ceramic Membrane With the Capacity of Pulsed Responsive Self-Cleaning and Anti-Fouling Functions.
items.abstract: Organic fouling remains a major challenge for ceramic membrane filtration because of the strong adsorption of organic foulants on membrane surfaces. Herein, a novel design strategy is proposed for smart piezoelectric hybrid ceramic membranes featuring self-powered nano-brushes. Specifically, a self-powered nano-brush smart piezoelectric hybrid ceramic membrane (ATPAA--PBM) with the pulsed pressure responsiveness and self-cleaning capability was prepared by grafting negatively charged sodium PAA polymer chain (PAA-) on the surface of BaTiO3 (BTO) piezoelectric ceramic membrane. Under the pulsed pressure, alternating piezoelectric charges induced reversible conformational oscillations of the self-powered nano-brushes, promoting the detachment of the foulant layer by the flowing water and thereby enabling in situ self-cleaning. Meanwhile, the grafted PAA- nano-brushes strongly associated with water molecules to establish a 462 nm-thick hydration layer, while generating electrostatic repulsion toward humic acid (HA), jointly preventing foulant adhesion and enabling nearly complete rejection. The membrane exhibited outstanding retention, anti-fouling ability, and remarkable flux retention ratio (FRR = 92.3%, 10 d) during a long-term filtration process. Consequently, a novel excellent rejection and anti-fouling mechanism of "self-powered nano-brush dynamic oscillation self-cleaning & hydration barrier" was proposed. This study provides a new perspective for the fabrication of self-cleaning smart piezoelectric hybrid ceramic membranes.

items.title: Molecular evidence of Bartonella spp. in wild felids from Brazil.
items.abstract: Among Felidae, domestic cats play a role as reservoirs for Bartonella henselae, Bartonella clarridgeiae, and Bartonella koehlerae. Despite the well-known relationship between Bartonella spp. and domestic cats, to date, there is still a paucity of reports on Bartonella spp. in wild felids. The aim of this study was to molecularly detect and characterize Bartonella spp. in blood and tissue samples from wild felids sampled in Brazil. Among 291 DNA samples (211 blood, 77 spleens and three livers), 3.09% (9/291) were positive in the Quantitative Real-Time PCR (qPCR) assay for Bartonella spp. based on the nuoG gene: 1/44 Leopardus pardalis, 3/61 Leopardus geoffroyi, 1/66 Panthera onca, 1/3 Herpailurus yagouaroundi, and 3/32 Leopardus wiedii. In the phylogenetic analyses, while the gltA sequence detected in L. wiedii grouped with Bartonella henselae, the gltA and ftsZ sequences detected in L. geoffroyi clustered within the same subclade as Bartonella sp. sequences previously identified in wild rodents and associated fleas. These findings reinforce that besides harboring Bartonella species associated with cats, wild felids also may act as accidental hosts for Bartonella species associated with wild small mammals, possibly as a consequence of predation.

items.title: Analysis of Lassa Fever Incidence in Nigeria Demonstrates a Clear Climate-Disease Interaction.
items.abstract: Lassa fever remains a major public health concern in Nigeria, where climatic variability, ecological dynamics, and socio-behavioral factors combine to influence transmission patterns. This review synthesizes current evidence on how atmospheric conditions shape Lassa fever incidence through their effects on ecosystems, rodent reservoirs, and human exposure pathways. Drawing on studies in epidemiology, disease ecology, climate science and remote sensing, the review highlights that temperature, rainfall, humidity, vegetation change and large-scale climatic oscillations all contribute to fluctuations in Mastomys natalensis populations which serve as the primary reservoir of Lassa virus. These climatic drivers modify food availability, breeding cycles and habitat suitability for rodents which in turn affect the probability of viral spillover. Modeling approaches including statistical regression, time series analysis, ecological niche modeling and spatiotemporal remote sensing demonstrate that environmental variables significantly improve predictions of disease risk. However, important gaps remain including limited long-term ecological data, underreporting in surveillance systems, insufficient integration of rodent ecology with climate data and a need for more comprehensive socio-behavioral studies. The review recommends future directions such as sustained monitoring of Mastomys populations, high-resolution climate-sensitive modeling, genomic analysis of Lassa virus across climatic gradients and multidisciplinary approaches that combine environmental science with public health research. Improving climate-informed surveillance and early warning systems is essential for strengthening preparedness and reducing the burden of Lassa fever in Nigeria.

items.title: Compatibility among Bacillus strains is linked to synthetic communities function, rhizosphere microbiome assembly and plant performance.
items.abstract: Microbial compatibility is an important consideration for synthetic communities (SynCom) function, but its ecological and physiological consequences for plant-microbe interactions remain insufficiently understood. We investigated compatible and incompatible Bacillus-based SynComs and their effects on tomato growth, rhizosphere microbiome assembly, and microbial network organization. Compatible co-cultures exhibited enhanced co-culture phenotypes, including merged colony morphology, enhanced biofilm formation, and altered growth dynamics, whereas incompatible combinations formed demarcation zones, indicative of antagonism. The compatible pair NMCN6+LNXM12 showed higher attached biomass and relative indole-3-acetic acid production compared with most incompatible or single-strain inoculations. Greenhouse experiments revealed that compatible SynComs significantly promoted tomato growth, increased plant height, root length, photosynthesis, and stomatal conductance, while incompatible combinations showed distinct soluble sugar responses rather than consistent evidence of plant stress. Amplicon sequencing revealed treatment-associated variation in rhizosphere bacterial community composition. Compatible SynComs were associated with enrichment of specific bacterial taxa and produced more interconnected and stable co-occurrence networks, whereas incompatible combinations showed distinct taxonomic profiles and comparatively fragmented microbial associations. Community composition differed significantly among individual treatments but not among broader compatibility categories with unequal within-group dispersion. Collectively, the observed co-culture, plant, and microbiome responses highlight differences among the selected Bacillus combinations that cannot be attributed to compatibility alone. These findings may provide the selection of Bacillus strain combinations for further evaluation as plant inoculants.

items.title: Implementation of a universal psychosocial screening program across the pediatric cancer treatment trajectory: a standard of care.
items.abstract: Guided by Rapid Evaluation and Assessment Methods (REAM) and using rigorous quality improvement processes, we describe implementation of an evidence-based psychosocial screening program at key transitions in childhood cancer treatment to guide care matched to need. Pediatric cancer patients (≥ 11 years) and caregivers (patients 0-17 years) were offered screening questionnaires electronically at 4-6 months, 18-24 months, and 4-6 years post-diagnosis through a phased implementation across three cancer center sites and in their preferred language (English, Spanish, Arabic). Screening questionnaires assessed cancer-related symptoms, health-related quality of life, cognitive function and school needs, caregiver adjustment and family risk, and resource needs. To assess adoption, feasibility, penetration, and sustainability, data related to screening processes, documentation completion rates, and adaptations were tracked and summarized. Qualitative interviews with patients, caregivers, and clinicians, based on the Consolidated Framework for Intervention Research (CFIR), were coded for acceptability and screening program optimization. Across sites and timepoints, from June 2023 through November 2025, there was a 56% screening completion rate (470/846). Patient physical functioning, emotional functioning, and neurocognitive functioning, caregiver adjustment, and resource needs were consistently flagged for follow-up. Documentation of follow-up varied with rates of 74% for social workers and 34% for medical clinicians. Patients, caregivers, and clinicians endorsed moderate acceptability. Barriers to electronic health record integration complicated clinician workflows. From initiation, over 2 years, 55 adaptations were made to improve workflow, implementation strategies, screening processes, and measures. We achieved development, implementation, and optimization of a psychosocial screening program across our cancer center.

items.title: Cell wall polymer interactions, rather than polysaccharide fine structure, underlie recalcitrance in energy cane varieties.
items.abstract: Second-generation bioethanol production from lignocellulosic biomass has driven the development of high-fiber sugarcane varieties known as energy canes, which combine high tillering, high biomass accumulation, lower sucrose, and improved agronomic performance. However, energy canes have been reported to be more recalcitrant to enzymatic saccharification. We compared biomass and cell wall composition, non-cellulosic polysaccharide extractability, and saccharification efficiency in two energy cane varieties, Vertix V2 and Vertix V3, and sugarcane. Sugarcane contained three times as much sucrose and less fiber than energy canes. After removing soluble sugars from the biomass, reduced digestibility became evident in the two energy cane varieties, particularly in V2. Saccharification increased with alkali and doubled after acidic sodium chlorite treatments. Although the main polysaccharides and linkage structures were broadly conserved across genotypes, minor changes were observed in their relative abundance and extractability. Glucuronoarabinoxylans (GAX) were the predominant wall polysaccharides (72%), while pectins [homogalacturonan (HG) and rhamnogalacturonan I (RG-I), each 1%], arabinan side-groups (4-6%), glucomannans (1%), and xyloglucan (2-4%) occurred in smaller proportions. Sugarcane contained higher abundances of xyloglucan, β-glucan, glucomannan, and arabinan, whereas energy canes had higher HG and RG-I. Chlorite oxidation solubilized GAX and RG-I, indicating that polymers are associated with phenylpropanoids and contribute to wall recalcitrance. The contrasting saccharification behavior of the sugarcane and energy cane varieties examined here appears to arise not from major changes in polysaccharide fine structure, but from differences in biomass allocation, phenylpropanoid abundance, extractability, and molecular interactions among cellulose, matrix polysaccharides, and phenylpropanoids within the cell wall. Understanding these properties in relation to enzyme-mediated disassembly is fundamental to accessing grass walls and improving biomass saccharification.

items.title: Assessing divergent ecological responses to forest and grassland dynamics using RSEI and interpretable machine learning in Northern Hebei, China.
items.abstract: Vegetation gains and losses may exhibit unequal or counterintuitive ecological responses because of differences in their initial conditions and land use transition pathways. In this study, we quantified changes in the remote sensing ecological index (RSEI) associated with forest and grassland dynamics in northern Hebei, China during from 2000 to 2022. We assessed asymmetry in the RSEI responses associated with forest and grassland gain and loss and used eXtreme Gradient Boosting with Shapley Additive Explanations (XGBoost-SHAP) model to identify the principal environmental driving factors. The results indicated that mean RSEI increased by 29.79%, and 52.38% of the study area showed a substantial increase (0.005 a -1 , P mirror = - 0.049), when the negative response associated with forest loss exceeded the positive response associated with forest gain. Grassland gain was associated with lower RSEI and grassland loss with higher RSEI, whereas their aggregate asymmetry was not statistically supported. The reversed grassland responses were closely related to their transition pathways because grassland gain originated mainly from cropland and was associated with lower RSEI, whereas grassland loss areas transitioned mainly to forest or cropland and were associated with higher RSEI. Across from 2000 to 2022, DEM (28.04%) and evapotranspiration (ET, 20.59%) were the leading predictors of forest gain, whereas nighttime light (NTL, 22.66%) and precipitation (20.20%) ranked highest for forest loss. Grassland gain was primarily associated with ET (34.50%) and precipitation (15.88%), while ET (20.65%) and DEM (20.48%) ranked highest for grassland loss. SHAP dependence relationships were non-linear and varied among vegetation types, change directions and study periods. These findings show that vegetation area change alone cannot adequately indicate ecological improvement and that gain and loss should be interpreted relative to stable conditions and specific land use pathways.

items.title: Shotgun metagenomic and untargeted metabolomic analysis of gut microbiome associated with peripheral artery disease
items.abstract: Background: While the human gut microbiome is a potentially important and modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular diseases, the links between the gut microbiome and peripheral artery disease (PAD) and its clinical subgroups (claudication and chronic limb-threatening ischemia; CLTI) are not well understood. Methods: We used shotgun metagenomics and untargeted metabolomics to analyze the fecal samples of people with PAD and age- and sex-matched non-PAD controls collected in a cross-sectional manner. We used functional prediction pathways, a network analysis, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis of metagenomic, metabolomics, and clinical data to better understand PAD-associated dysbiosis. Results: Alpha and beta diversity were similar between the PAD (n=78) and non-PAD (n=20) groups. Differentially abundant species were dominated by those belonging to the Lachnospiraceae, Ruminococcaceae and Enterobacteriaceae families. Fecal butyrate levels were reduced between the non-PAD and PAD groups, but differences were not statistically significant. There was significantly reduced alpha diversity in the samples of the CLTI compared to claudication subgroup. Abundance of multiple butyrate producers were greater in the claudication group compared to CLTI. Network analysis revealed 5 meta-modules, each with specific associations to PAD presentation and metabolomic profiles, and species that are both top module hubs and differentially abundant between groups. Community interconnectedness appears to increase in claudication, followed by community disintegration in CLTI. Conclusions: This metagenomic-metabolomic analysis of the gut microbiome of individuals with PAD, highlights the importance of studying functional capacity, diversity, and connectivity between species. Microbial modules may allow an integrative view of the microbial ecology relevant to presence and progression of PAD.

items.title: Decentring artistic practice beyond national narratives. An analysis of the European pavilion as a post-national model
items.abstract: Background: The national pavilion model, epitomised by the Venice Biennale, functions as an internal cultural border that aligns artistic production with state sovereignty and Eurocentric universality. This representational framework fails to accommodate contemporary, mobile, and post-national artistic practices. To explore an alternative paradigm, this article evaluates Liquid Becomings, a 2024 waterborne project commissioned by the European Cultural Foundation. Navigating four major European rivers—the Danube, Rhine, Vistula, and Tagus—this itinerant civic laboratory sought to test how a post-national community might be lived through fluid, non-extractive practices. Methods This study employs a qualitative, interdisciplinary methodology bridging contemporary curatorial critique with decolonial theory and political geography. Utilizing the framework of the institutional archive versus the embodied repertoire, the empirical analysis juxtaposes official curatorial materials, manifestoes, and video documentation from the four river routes against ex-post reflective accounts of the project’s final transition to a land-bound festival in Lisbon. Results The river residencies successfully disrupted state-centric visual regimes by shifting the locus of enunciation onto mobile platforms. The routes reconceptualized European borders through decolonial delinking, relational opacity, hydrofeminist ecology, and human-powered navigation. However, translating these slow, somatic, and non-representational practices into an urban festival in Lisbon generated significant structural friction, revealing a fundamental disconnect between the transient embodied repertoire of the river journeys and the spectacle-driven expectations of land-based cultural institutions. Conclusions The study concludes that the material absence, insularity, and spatial diffusion observed at the Lisbon festival do not represent operational failures. Synthesising participatory aesthetics, the distribution of the sensible, and agonistic pluralism, the article demonstrates that these frictions constitute a radical aesthetic of withdrawal that evades institutional capture and resists state-sanctioned narratives of European identity.

items.title: Contextual Stress Exposure and Longitudinal Change in Mental Health and Sleep Among US Latino/a Adolescents.
items.abstract: This research examines how contextual stress exposure within the immigration environment predicts sleep problems and internalizing symptoms for Latino/a adolescents. Participants included N = 547 adolescents listed as "Hispanic" on 2017-18 middle school enrollment lists in a suburban Atlanta, GA, school district. Using three time (T) points of survey data (2021-23), structural equation models tested paths from immigration-related stressors to changes in sleep problems and internalizing symptoms. Missing data were addressed using multiply imputed datasets and full information maximum likelihood. At T1, the 244 (44.6%) male and 303 (55.4%) female participants had a mean (SD) age of 16.2 (.91) years. Across time, 28.8%-40.3% of youth reported <7 hours of sleep on average. The prevalence of clinical internalizing symptoms ranged from 31.1% to 35.9% for female participants and from 29.9% to 44.3% for male participants. T1 immigration-related stressors predicted T1 to T2 increases in sleep problems (ß = .12 [95% CI = .03-.20]) and internalizing symptoms (ß = .09 [95% CI = .01-.17]). T2 sleep problems mediated associations between T1 immigration-related stressors and T2 to T3 increases in internalizing symptoms (indirect effect: ß = .01 [95% CI = .00-.03]) and sleep problems (indirect effect: ß = .07 [95% CI = .02-.12]). Sleep problems and internalizing symptoms were reciprocally associated from T1 to T2 (sleep to internalizing: ß = .11 [95% CI = .02-.20]; internalizing to sleep: ß = .14 [95% CI = .04-.25]) and from T2 to T3 (sleep to internalizing: ß = .11 [95% CI = .03-.20]; internalizing to sleep: ß = .10 [95% CI = .00-.20]). For Latino/a adolescents, immigration-related stressors may harm mental health through increased sleep problems.
